# @nextlyhq/plugin-accounts

## 0.0.2-alpha.76

### Patch Changes

- [#4053](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4053) [`d283cb3`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/d283cb3af16224bb85379e4b6885719d3ad55684) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A blog scaffolded with the code-first approach now gets its first migration written from its own config. Once the dependencies are installed, the CLI runs `nextly migrate:create initial` for the database you chose, so the build's `nextly migrate` creates every table the blog reads, the form-builder plugin's included. Before, the scaffold copied the visual blog's hand-written SQL to a folder the code-first config never read, so the build migrated nothing. With `--skip-install`, the next steps name the command to run after installing. A visual blog still gets the template's migration.

- [#4193](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4193) [`aba11f0`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/aba11f05ea62c79a2fe570b503dccd5fe48988b9) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - On MySQL, `db:sync` and the dev reload keep a code-first field group's text column at the width they narrow it to. A text field that states no width is `varchar(255)` in a field group defined in code, as the sync plans it, but the table handed to the push described it as TEXT, so every sync narrowed the column and the push widened it straight back.

- [#4045](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4045) [`4a60f0c`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/4a60f0c2561041f89d45732e4c9167b248eb4c8e) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A `nextly migrate` run in development mode, which is how it runs when `NODE_ENV` is not set, now writes the registry rows its migrations record. On a fresh database it adds every collection, Single and field group row the newest applied snapshot records, and it brings the row of each entity an applied migration changed to that migration's record, on a later run too when the run that applied it could not write the row. Before, it added only the rows an older template-shaped snapshot listed, so a site migrated with `migrate:create` files had no registry rows until a development start synced them. Rows a live sync edited with no migration for the edit are still left as they are.

  A run in any mode also adds the rows a template's older-format snapshot lists (the blog template's hand-written migration), where the registry lacks them. Outside development such a snapshot was read as unreadable, so a site built from it got none of those rows from `nextly migrate`. A snapshot that cannot be read for another reason is still refused.

- [#3895](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3895) [`6f12301`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/6f123018e58ab0fed2147a9c5c2375dc6f4f3230) Thanks [@aqib-rx](https://github.com/aqib-rx)! - A development start ensures each permission once, and skips the entities that have not changed since the last one. A start used to ensure every collection's and Single's permissions twice, one statement at a time, and read every content table's shape on each restart; an unchanged start with 50 collections sent 2,836 statements. Now the permissions are ensured once, against one read of the table, and a development start reads the tables of only the collections, Singles and field groups whose declaration changed since the last development start, as recorded in `nextly_meta`; a restart with nothing changed writes no permissions, roles, registry rows or user field definitions, and sends the same number of statements whatever the number of entities. An upgrade of Nextly, a change of database, or a change to `localization` or `experimental.perLanguageStorage` makes the next start check everything again.

  Code-defined user fields are written only where they differ from what is stored: a configuration declaring none no longer deletes on every start and `db:sync`.

- [#3913](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3913) [`4bfd670`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/4bfd67031a7d09dfee48e230019fc09f59cf295d) Thanks [@zeshan-rx](https://github.com/zeshan-rx)! - A field changing between translated and shared now keeps what every reader sees, and says so first.
  - **The shared value is the one readers saw.** When a field stops being translated, an entry's shared value comes from the default language where it's live; otherwise from the first live language in the site's language order; otherwise from the default language's draft; otherwise from the site's order. Previously an entry with no default-language value took the first language by code, which could be a draft no reader saw. Every other language's value is archived, and `nextly i18n:restore` brings it back.
  - **The summary names whose page changes.** The Schema Builder's preview counts what goes to the archive with the same rule, and lists the languages entries take their shared value from. A field becoming translated now has a summary too: how many values become the default language's.
  - **Password and virtual fields can't be marked translatable.** A configuration that sets `localized: true` on one is refused, naming the field; it was quietly stored as shared. The Schema Builder no longer offers the switch on a password field.

- [#4115](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4115) [`bb77364`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/bb77364170619f9fcbf5ad697be240668dd6dd15) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The form builder's start reads less. It no longer reads every form to warn about a bot check missing its keys: the site default's missing keys are still said at start, from the plugin's options alone, and a check a form names itself is said when that form is saved and when the first submission is accepted unchecked. A redirect target's `localized` setting is taken from the collection's declaration in the configuration instead of its registry row; only a collection made in the Schema Builder is still asked of the registry. An unchanged start sends one statement where it sent six.

- [#4022](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4022) [`3e08502`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/3e08502ccc7bc20afb8a96dcbd5a87c6efd51da8) Thanks [@zeshan-rx](https://github.com/zeshan-rx)! - A held save under per-language storage hands its part drafts a language its types guarantee, never the shared slot. Behaviour is unchanged: the same value reaches the store, and `check-types` accepts it.

- [#4231](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4231) [`def1cad`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/def1cad9cb15d8d839c68ed798a17ec0568e8378) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - A plugin's own item at the icon rail's foot no longer moves the rail as the admin finishes loading. The rail's foot is held to the bottom of the window, and the item was drawn inside the box that holds the Inbox and the account menu, so when the admin's answers arrived that box grew upwards by one item's height. The Inbox and the avatar stayed where their loading shapes stood, but the browser recorded the rail's foot as moving. The item now has a box of its own above the Inbox, which appears whole once the answers are in, so nothing already drawn on the rail moves. It looks the same as before: the item sits above the Inbox, in the same order and at the same spacing, and in the top bar (where a surface takes the rail away) nothing changes.

- [#4006](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4006) [`081277c`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/081277c241aaf2968ca852bcc8b1e9ab47b6194f) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A plugin may no longer be named `app`. The site's own permissions are stored under the owner `app`, and a plugin's under its name, so a plugin with that name could not be told apart from the site: uninstalling it, `nextly migrate` or a `migrate:down` could take one's permissions for the other's. Startup and every CLI command now refuse a plugin named `app`, in any letter case, with `PLUGIN_RESOLUTION_ERROR` (`logContext.reason` `plugin-name-reserved`). Compatibility: a plugin named `app` stops the app from starting until it is renamed; `apps`, `my-app` and other names are unaffected.

- [#4046](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4046) [`3b3817b`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/3b3817b78b1510cf19435c69e056d2371f3cb2e8) Thanks [@zeshan-rx](https://github.com/zeshan-rx)! - The SEO and Page Builder plugins' published types now carry the admin place they type. The Page Builder's Settings place (`nextlyhq-plugin-page-builder.settings`) was declared in `AdminPlaces` by a module augmentation that the build left out of every published declaration file. A project type-checking the installed plugins was then refused the place's name in the SEO plugin's Page Builder tab. Both plugins' declarations now include the augmentation, and nothing else changes.

- [#4050](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4050) [`9a4f3fe`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/9a4f3fe8404150533d1916b09d4d6fc303370052) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A number in a plugin's panel now counts drafts too. A count declared as `{ collection, where }` counts every entry the reader may open, drafts included, as the collection's own list shows them, where it counted published entries only. A `where` still narrows it, to drafts for one.

- [#4069](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4069) [`ea4dc01`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/ea4dc016da5f2e2e3610d747b53e01efa81ff924) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A production start no longer creates or changes a table. Every start used to create the tables its configuration declared and the database lacked (a collection's, a Single's, a field group's, a translated entity's translation table, the user fields' columns), rename a table whose `dbName` changed, add a plugin's field to a Schema Builder entity, create a missing PostgreSQL schema, and set up every table of an empty database, in production too and with no lock between cold starts. A production start now serves the structure `nextly migrate` made: a missing translation table answers that its translations are not ready, and a field the database lacks answers `ENTITY_NOT_MIGRATED`. A development start (`next dev`) is unchanged.

  A production start against a database with no Nextly tables, or without its configured PostgreSQL schema, creates nothing and refuses to start with `NEXTLY_DATABASE_NOT_SET_UP`, telling you to run `nextly migrate`. With `db.runMigrationsOnBoot`, the start runs that step first, which sets the database up as the command does.

  A changed `dbName` now needs a migration. `nextly migrate:create` writes it as a dropped table and a new one, so until it writes a table rename, replace those statements with a rename by hand, as the production migrations guide shows. A site whose production tables were made by its starts, with no migration for them, takes a baseline (`nextly migrate:baseline`) before upgrading.

- [#4095](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4095) [`8625cf2`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/8625cf29d01a143fbb003fc042e7720cc469f95f) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A production start waits on the database far fewer times. It read the Schema Builder's registries four or five times each, and asked the database's catalog the same questions from several steps, one after another (on SQLite once per field group), so a start against a database 100 ms away spent about 4.5 seconds waiting before Nextly served. It now reads the catalog and each registry once, sends the reads that need nothing else together, and runs the independent steps after them together: about 12 waits on PostgreSQL and MySQL and 18 statements on SQLite, the same for 5 entities and for 50, outside the migrations at start and the plugins' own start-up code.

  A production start no longer writes to `nextly_meta` to discard a setup token when none is stored, and the email templates' reconciliation no longer runs an update when no row needs it, so a start of a set-up site writes nothing of its own.

  Each plugin's own start-up time (its `init` and `onReady`) is logged at debug level after the plugins start, and a warning names every plugin whose start-up took longer than 500 ms, with its time: every cold start waits for it before Nextly serves.

  On SQLite, the catalog is read through SQLite's table-valued PRAGMA functions, a few statements whatever the number of tables, wherever Nextly reads it (migrations and `nextly migrate:create` included).

- [#4031](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4031) [`14fe629`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/14fe629941b26136c71b5c323970beefe6ca8dae) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A production start no longer writes the registry, the permissions, the roles or their grants, or the user field definitions, and no longer marks an entity migrated. Every start used to write the registry rows of your collections, Singles and field groups from the configuration of the build that was starting, seed the permissions and preset grants before `getNextly()` resolved, and mark a plugin collection's table `applied` though it lacked the plugin's new column. So whichever build started last decided what the database said, an older one included, and a start ran a few statements for every collection, Single and permission. A production start now serves what `nextly migrate` (and a plugin's install and uninstall) wrote, and runs the same number of statements however many entities the site has. A development start (`next dev`) keeps its live sync, unchanged.

  `nextly migrate` now also makes the built-in Public role and grants it what visitors read: `read-media`, the read of each collection and Single whose read rule answers a visitor `true`, and what your plugins declare for it, each once. A plugin's install grants what that plugin declares. Before, only a start did this.

  Run `nextly migrate` before serving. The scaffolded build script already runs `nextly migrate && next build`; a deployment that relied on its start to bring a new field, collection or permission into the database must now run `nextly migrate` first. Until it does, a read or write that reaches a declared field the database has not been migrated for answers `ENTITY_NOT_MIGRATED`, naming the field to trusted server code. With `db.runMigrationsOnBoot`, the start runs `nextly migrate` first and gets the same.

  Moving production back to a Nextly release from before this one is outside this guarantee: such a release seeds the permissions and preset grants at every production start, from its own configuration and presets, and has no setting that turns that off.

- [#4113](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4113) [`be9d517`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/be9d517ac830fcf7c0a54846d1f0b2770848b9a0) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The admin no longer sends a refused read a second time. A read the server answers with a 4xx status, such as 401 while signed out, 403, 404 or 422, is shown at once; a timeout (408), a rate limit (429), a server error (5xx) or a lost response is still sent once more. The signed-out sign-in screen asks for the general settings once rather than twice.

- [#4192](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4192) [`1700426`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/170042620907e4d30587ca6423f35eb399d4f3f8) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - A Builder save on MySQL that makes a field required while rows hold no value in it is again refused with its reason alone: nothing of it ran. MySQL writes that change as a statement built from the live column, which the save could not read a table from, so it reported the refusal as a migration that failed part-way, told you to settle it with `nextly migrate:resolve`, and kept the save's files. It now reads that statement as the column change it makes.

- [#4191](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4191) [`446e80b`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/446e80b2ff138b0b2ead18631feaa37861b98366) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - Collections, Singles and field groups registered in the same second now list in one order on MySQL. MySQL keeps their creation time to the second, so entities a start registers together came back in whichever order the server sorted them that time: the setup card could list the Singles differently from one load to the next. Among entries created together, the registry now lists by slug.

- [#4148](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4148) [`c078251`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/c078251b10821023d0d34eaa32f228192d8df2f1) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - A field group renamed while another field takes its old name now keeps its stored values. When a site renames its own `seo` field group to `legacySeo` and adds the SEO plugin, whose `seo` group lands on the same types, in one change, `nextly migrate:create` now offers the rename (and `--accept-renames` accepts it), so the migration moves the group's rows to `legacySeo` and moves them back in its down step. Before, the old name still being in use hid the rename: the rows stayed under `seo`, where nothing reads them, and `legacySeo` read empty. A field group that changes which groups it holds, or whether it repeats, under the same name now counts as removed and added in the same way, in the Schema Builder too, so another field group renamed in the same save can take its rows.

- [#4021](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4021) [`3cd690b`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/3cd690be527558ed85cdfcb0128166f0213e4f2d) Thanks [@zeshan-rx](https://github.com/zeshan-rx)! - **Breaking:** a restore through the APIs writes the working draft and never publishes. Restoring
  a version through REST (`POST …/versions/{n}/restore`) no longer writes the live document or its
  status: the chosen fields (all of them by default, or the ones `fields` names) go into the drafts
  of the parts the version holds, and what readers see stays as it is until the draft is
  published. A collection or Single kept without drafts (`versions: { drafts: false }`, or no
  `status`) has no draft to write, so its restore is now refused with `422 BUSINESS_RULE_VIOLATION`
  before anything changes. To put a version back live there, edit the values back, or turn drafts
  on and publish the restored draft.

  The Direct API gains `nextly.versions` (`list`, `get`, `compare`, `name`, `restore`,
  `markSeen`), and plugins gain `ctx.services.versions.restore`; both are experimental. Each
  restored value records the version it came from: a restore records its own, and a save names
  its restored fields in `_restoredFrom`. Retention keeps every version a recorded source names.

  **Storage:** the versions table gains a nullable `field_sources` column. `nextly migrate` and
  start-up add it to an existing database, with no migration file and no change to existing rows.

- [#4000](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4000) [`1399960`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/13999606adbbe6cf0ed4025f64f3dedefbca497c) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - `nextly migrate:down` now keeps the registry in step with the database once the database has its registry record. A rollback that brings the database back to the point that record was taken at undoes the rolled-back migrations' own changes to the bookkeeping, in the same transaction as the last migration it rolls back: each collection, Single and field group row goes back to how it stood when the record was written, the row of an entity those migrations added is removed and its permissions marked as no longer declared, a permission they added is marked the same way with its grants kept, and a permission they marked is declared again where that point declares it: the app's own, an entity's or Nextly's where the baseline holds it, and a plugin's where the plugin is installed and its current release declares it. What plugin installs and uninstalls wrote in the meantime, and Nextly's own permissions, stay as they are. A rollback that would leave the database at any other point where nothing records the registry (an earlier migration without the registry metadata, or the point before any app migration when the record is not there) is now refused before it changes anything, naming that point; write a new migration to undo the change instead. On MySQL, where schema statements commit as they run, a rollback whose bookkeeping cannot be written is left recorded as a failed rollback rather than as rolled back.

- [#3931](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3931) [`c3f076d`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/c3f076ddf359abcf271f416f691069b9e6f3fba5) Thanks [@aqib-rx](https://github.com/aqib-rx)! - A run that can no longer show it holds the schema lock now stops. That covers `nextly migrate`, `migrate:down`, the boot migrate step, `db:sync`, the development push and the Schema Builder's saves. A run loses the lock when another run took it, or when the run stalled past its lease without confirming it. It then starts no further statement, writes nothing further to the migration ledger, and says it lost the lock, naming the last migration it applied.

  A run that takes over a lock whose holder stalled or was killed now first asks the database to stop each statement that holder sent which is still running (PostgreSQL and MySQL), and waits for them to end before it changes anything. If one is still running when the wait is over, the run gives the lock back and stops, naming the statement and its database session. A holder killed while a statement runs leaves a lock that lapses within one lease once no statement of it is running, so the next run proceeds without anyone unlocking it by hand.

- [#4128](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4128) [`b7ca686`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/b7ca68688f73048b1b381842a5f0a25a522b92d9) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - A save to a working draft that already exists keeps every translated value it sends. On a translated content type keeping drafts, the second and later saves of a draft dropped the translated fields they changed, a translated named group included, in every language, while the save reported success; the first save of the draft and field groups were not affected.

- [#4100](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4100) [`23d7e70`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/23d7e70395860c149f87f9d926be2ae20ad9b42d) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The SEO plugin no longer rewrites its bookkeeping at every start. The start-up catch-up of the address record is skipped whenever the address templates, the site's content types and the pending moves are unchanged since its last run, including on a site where no page holds an address yet, and a run that finds a stored note already current leaves it as it is. The note that the site's Proxy runs is written only when the stored one is an hour old or more, so a server's first request after a start writes nothing within that hour.

- [#4072](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4072) [`df8eb70`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/df8eb70b321adc7507101ac0cf344777a5cbe05d) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - A Single read or saved for the first time by two requests at once no longer fails one of them. On a fresh site, the first page views reading a Single that has no document yet (such as a plugin's settings) could each try to create it, and on PostgreSQL and MySQL one failed with a duplicate key error. Exactly one document is now created, with its defaults, first version and "created" history event written once, and every request gets it.

- [#4032](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4032) [`42c694b`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/42c694bde85bc4919693a52c32fc48eb5d804942) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - Sites that render their own pages now get the SEO plugin's head and structured data without workarounds.
  - `singlePageMetadata` and `singlePageStructuredData` (from `nextly/runtime`) answer a Single a site reads itself, as `contentPageMetadata` and `contentPageStructuredData` answer an entry. Both take the address the page was served at, so a later page of a Single's list (`/blog/page/2`) gets its own canonical; Single routes take the same address as a new `path` option.
  - `seoStructuredData(path, options)` (from `@nextlyhq/plugin-seo`) gives a page built in code its structured data from the same answer as `seoMetadata`.
  - `jsonLdScriptProps(data)` (from `nextly/runtime`) places structured data in a page, `<script {...jsonLdScriptProps(data)} />`, escaped so no value can end the element.
  - The plugin's title is served as `title: { absolute }`, so a root layout's `title.template` no longer adds the site name a second time. A route's own title keeps the form the route gave it.
  - A route's `noindex` (and `nofollow`) is kept: the route can hide a page, never list one the plugin hides, and a page built in code its route hides leaves the plugin's sitemap. Google's `max-image-preview`, `max-snippet` and `max-video-preview` limits and the route's other robots directives are kept.
  - A page the plugin gives no canonical, such as one whose type declares no public address, keeps the canonical and `og:url` its route set.
  - A page served before anything in its worker started Nextly (every read a cache hit, or prerendered by `next build`) now starts it and is served the plugin's answer, rather than silently its route's own head.

- [#4030](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4030) [`c7a8a45`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/c7a8a45f5443c8ca55890f0d720593d7c207a6ca) Thanks [@aqib-rx](https://github.com/aqib-rx)! - A run refused because an earlier holder's statement would not stop now names that statement's migration file and its database session, never the statement's text. The text could hold a literal value, such as a key, which no longer reaches the message or the logs.

- [#4056](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4056) [`1adc552`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/1adc552a027dc67cde6309d5b9631a8d5e0e6f94) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A form submission's page keeps unsaved work safe. Answers or a note typed and
  not yet saved now hold the page, so moving to another submission or away asks
  first; answers typed while a save is on its way stay in the editor; a note
  draft is never saved over someone else's newer note; a failed refresh keeps
  the page and its drafts instead of replacing them with an error; and after a
  submission is deleted the page moves on without asking about it. Fields a
  site adds to submissions with `formSubmissionOverrides.fields` show, read-only,
  in the page's Details.

- [#4086](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4086) [`504266d`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/504266d1e47ca16768db13cc651db047aafbd7a0) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A write no longer reads the same registry rows again and again inside its transaction. Each collection's registry row is read from the database once per transaction and then answered from that transaction's own memo, which a registry or schema write in the same transaction, or a rollback to a savepoint, makes it read again; no other transaction ever sees it. An entry update that read `dynamic_collections` ten times now reads each collection once.

  Two start-up costs go too. A retention pass offered while its marker is current is now refused by one read, where it deleted nothing and then sent an insert the primary key refused, a failed statement in the database log for every pass each process offered. And a boot settles every email template's engine from one read of the engine marks, where each template read the meta table twice.

  `DrizzleAdapter` gains an experimental `transactionInFlow()`, which names the open transaction the calling flow runs in and says whether its part has rolled back to a savepoint.

- [#4078](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4078) [`d0c7b28`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/d0c7b2869a475d409518e19312e2678241cc85c3) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Closing a release's Add documents dialog gives focus back to the Add documents button again. Since the dialog's code began loading on first open, the dialog shown while it loaded held focus, and closing left it at the top of the page.

- [#4071](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4071) [`30cab7e`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/30cab7effc283db2677c1978b29fdde34d7db63a) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Lists, the rich-text editor and the account menu read correctly to screen readers and keyboards. A list's sortable column headers keep their sort state, rows and row cards are no longer controls wrapped around other controls (each row is reached through its title), the title link is a larger target, and the rows-per-page selector is named. The rich-text toolbar's icon buttons and a code field's editor are named, and the account menu no longer hides the page behind it from assistive technology while it is open.

- [#4116](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4116) [`9f26449`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/9f26449b29fad7aff59873d49af9828ebb20eba1) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - The SEO import now covers every version of a page a value applies to, in one run. A translated content type or Single is imported into each of the site's languages, from each language's own values, and a type that keeps working drafts is imported into what is published and into the draft waiting beside it, each on its own: a value an editor typed in the draft is kept, the draft stays a draft, and a page with no draft gets none. Pages never published are imported into too. The import's last step shows one row per version, such as English · published, English · draft and Deutsch · published, each value with its own result, and the downloaded report has a Version column. It is still all or nothing: whatever is written outside the one step (a Single, another language, a draft of a type that isn't translated) is put back as it was when anything after it fails. A page in another language with a draft waiting is left as it is, and said so, until the draft is published or discarded.

  Plugins can list the site's languages as they are now, a list set in Settings included, through `ctx.publicAddresses.languages()`, which the import uses.

- [#4033](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4033) [`694f7ce`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/694f7ce0b0b5191aac6094ee85827030dcbca0f1) Thanks [@zeshan-rx](https://github.com/zeshan-rx)! - A save that changes nothing a language shows no longer withdraws that language's approval on SQLite and MySQL. An approval's record of the content it approved now leaves out every column the framework manages and no client writes, the time the document was first published among them. Those databases read that time back to the second, while the version a publish writes holds it to the millisecond, so a held edit of another language read it as a change.

- [#4088](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4088) [`166c2b8`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/166c2b8c04f7ca8ed28aaad625347aee33d84972) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The admin no longer sends autosave requests for a collection or Single with autosave turned off. The entry and Single editors, and the Page Builder canvas inside them, used to record recovery points there anyway; the server refused each one, so every editing session filled with refused requests. Where autosave is off they now record nothing, look for no recovery point and show no autosave status. Nothing changes where autosave is on.

- [#4138](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4138) [`e61a18f`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/e61a18f3ad6651f7dc545b9e0f3de6dec1a5135e) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - The Builder's form preview fetches its code the first time the preview is turned on, so opening a collection, Single or field group in the Builder no longer downloads the entry form's field editors.

- [#4184](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4184) [`42e2b9c`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/42e2b9cc8304b7b8024da020fc3b9a87107ec04e) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - Code that loads the collection service or the collection dispatcher, such as each request's boot, no longer loads the Builder save writer with it, and with it the migration generator and runner. The writer is now loaded the first time a Builder save, preview or delete through it runs.

- [#3826](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3826) [`e378ae8`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/e378ae8f169f8d462e4f33372df35c100a8ced49) Thanks [@aqib-rx](https://github.com/aqib-rx)! - `nextly migrate:check` no longer reports drift right after `nextly migrate:create` for a Schema Builder collection on MySQL. The check described a Builder collection's table by the code-first column rule, so a text field that states no width was expected as `varchar(255)` while the migration had created it as `TEXT`.

  `nextly migrate:create` now also describes Builder Singles and field groups by the column rule of the Builder that builds them, as `nextly migrate` and the running app already do. On MySQL, an app whose earlier migrations created such a column as `varchar(255)` gets, at its next `nextly migrate:create`, one migration that widens it to `TEXT`; the widening needs no confirmation and keeps every value. A unique text field that states no width stays `varchar(255)` on MySQL for every Builder entity, since MySQL can key only a bounded column; such a field is now accepted there instead of refused. So on MySQL, turning Unique on or off for a text field with no `maxLength` changes its column (`varchar(255)` while unique, `TEXT` otherwise), and the Schema Builder takes it through its schema preview as a change to the table; give the field a `maxLength` to keep its column as it is. A translated field is unique per language and keyed without bounding its column, so a translated unique text field keeps `TEXT`, and turning localization off restores its values into `TEXT` with nothing cut; such a field leaving translation while unique is refused, since its shared column would be bounded. An indexed one is not widened either: where an earlier migration made it `varchar(255)` with an index over the whole column, `nextly migrate:create` refuses with a message naming the column, and asks for a `maxLength` on the field or for its index to be removed. Widening such a column together with its index comes later.

- [#4070](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4070) [`d40d57e`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/d40d57e267135be186aacbdf28d24d09dfa69e0f) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A `contains` filter on a hasMany relationship now works on PostgreSQL. Its ids are stored as a `jsonb` array there, and the case-insensitive match lowered the column, which PostgreSQL refuses for `jsonb` ("function lower(jsonb) does not exist"), so `where: { categories: { contains: id } }` failed while MySQL and SQLite searched the serialized array. The value is now folded as text on PostgreSQL, which also fixes the blog template's category and tag pages there, which listed no posts. A text column matches exactly as before.

- [#4029](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4029) [`a2ed0dc`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/a2ed0dc543e732eaa5ac9a01fbdf14ef13264515) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The admin's Content panel now lists collections and Singles together in one list, each under a heading with its count, instead of switching between them with a segmented control. One search filters both headings, and each heading folds, remembered for you across visits. Collections that set `admin.sidebarGroup` are listed under that group's sub-heading inside Collections. Where no `admin.icon` is set, a collection now shows a list icon and a Single a framed-page icon. A role that can read only one kind sees only that kind's heading, and the panel's title links to the Content overview.

- [#4038](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4038) [`61b76b0`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/61b76b0f057c52cc8d7a4240b17aa1035f411c6f) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The admin has a Content overview at `/admin/content`: a table of the collections you can open, with each one's entries, drafts, last edit and a New action where you may create, and a table of the Singles, with who edited each last, when, and Edit. Collections that set `admin.sidebarGroup` are listed under their group. Clicking Content in the rail opens the overview with the Content panel beside it. `/admin/collections` and `/admin/singles` no longer redirect to the first item: each shows the overview with that one table. A role that can open only Singles is sent from `/admin/collections` to `/admin/singles`, and the other way round for collections only; with neither, each address says there is no content to open, and offers to create a collection to someone who may. A new endpoint, `GET /admin/api/dashboard/content`, answers every row the overview shows in one request.

- [#4108](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4108) [`bbf7151`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/bbf71511a0b175e3501c4446e8f885b1f3115cfa) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Content routes take the site's own `notFound`. `createContentRoute`, `createPublicContentRoute`, `createSingleRoute` and `createPublicSingleRoute` from `nextly/runtime`, and `createContentPage`, `createPublicContentPage`, `createBlocksPage`, `createPublicBlocksPage`, `createSinglePage` and `createPublicSinglePage` from `@nextlyhq/blocks-react/next`, accept a `notFound` function that answers a path the route has nothing for in place of Next.js's `notFound()`, from the page and from `generateMetadata` alike, so a site can do something for each miss, such as logging the address. A handler that returns is followed by `notFound()`, and a route given none answers as before. The page builder's public forms call it only with Cache Components on, since without them a public page's answer is rendered once and kept. The option is experimental.

- [#4235](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4235) [`089dd8f`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/089dd8f9f415b24fa013fc7b9f2cf6c713ef03b3) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - A plugin's block on the dashboard no longer jumps when the cards arrive. A screen's loading outline now holds its place from the first paint, laid out but not drawn until its 0.4 s, so whatever a page draws after a part that is still loading (a plugin's block after the dashboard's cards) is drawn where it will stay, rather than up under the greeting and then pushed off the screen.

- [#4120](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4120) [`2dec523`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/2dec523aaa12fc2fc712e4b3f5a1b1df406c63b2) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - On SQLite, a field group table that a schema push rebuilds keeps its `id` NOT NULL. Before, the
  rebuild wrote `id text PRIMARY KEY` without NOT NULL, so the upgraded table accepted a row with no
  id.

- [#4106](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4106) [`05f6343`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/05f6343bd5e094c11b709924f93175a72b05bfc7) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - The submissions list's chosen status tab is raised with a shadow, as the admin's other segmented controls are, instead of a faint outline that was too light to see in dark mode.

- [#4062](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4062) [`215c66d`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/215c66d44b31ea558a099284e59a35002ecce311) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A form's file field now has an upload route, and a submission's files are deleted with it.

  `POST /admin/api/forms/:slug/upload` (multipart: `field` and `file`) stores a visitor's file for one file field of an open form and answers with its `mediaId`, the value the field's answer names. It refuses a form that is not open, a field that is not a file field, a type or size the field does not take (the field's `accept` and `maxFileSize`, never above the plugin's `uploads.maxFileSize`), and a visitor past five uploads per submission the rate limit allows.

  The plugin records each upload, and a submission written by a request (a visitor, or staff over the API) may only name uploads made for its own form and field that no other submission has claimed; anything else is refused with a validation error on the field. An edit may send back the ids a submission already holds. A write no request produced (the Direct API from server code) is trusted as before, and one naming a file another submission holds is recorded as holding it too, so the file stays while either names it.

  Deleting a submission, one at a time, in bulk, by the nightly retention pass or with its form, now deletes the files it holds once the deletion commits, unless something else on the site uses one. The nightly pass also deletes uploads no submission claimed within a day. Settings › Privacy says so.

  A plugin's `ctx.services.media.delete` now removes the item's stored files durably: they are recorded as left to remove in the delete's own transaction, and the jobs queue retries a removal storage refused until the files are gone, rather than leaving them behind after a storage error.

  Migration: the plugin adds an internal `form-uploads` collection. Existing installations receive it through their own migrations: run `nextly migrate:create` and then `nextly migrate` (or `nextly db:sync` in development). Files named by submissions stored before the upgrade were not recorded, so they are not deleted with them.

  The plugin SDK also re-exports the `date` field factory and the `CollectionConfig` type, as part of its public field-authoring surface, so a plugin can author the collections it contributes without importing from core.

- [#4076](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4076) [`bb940f2`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/bb940f23ca827bf873dc61711206befc02475b6e) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A submission page's links are underlined in a colour that reads in dark mode, and a notification's recipient field fills its row beside Add instead of setting a width of its own.

- [#4082](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4082) [`bc230f5`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/bc230f50b573afae6458cc64b59deb34b2e4babb) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Form notifications are queued in the transaction that saves their submission, so a submission and its notifications are kept together or not at all, and marking a submission as spam cancels and clears its notifications not yet sent in the same transaction. One the provider is sending at that moment finishes: it ends sent if the provider takes it, and cancelled if that attempt fails. A submission flagged as spam still queues nothing, and marking it "Not spam" sends nothing.

  The `form-builder.beforeEmail` hook now runs inside that transaction: a hook that throws refuses the submission, and it may run again if the transaction is retried. No collection or field changes, so there is nothing to migrate.

- [#4092](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4092) [`ecbb6b0`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/ecbb6b0fc1dccbb1f3e20a85aebd8ca3602172ef) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A submission's page shows each notification it sent and, for each recipient, Waiting, Retrying, Sending, Sent, Sent after N retries, Failed or Cancelled (and why), and when; a notification whose recipients differ reads Partly sent. A notification's page lists its recent sends. The Form Builder keeps each send's per-recipient outcome with the submission, by masked hint and keyed digest, updated in the same transaction as each change of the queued email, so it outlives the 90-day delivery log and is deleted with the submission.

  Resend sends a notification again to the recipients who have not received it, plus any the person ticks, and records who asked. It needs both `update-<submissions>` and `manage-email-deliveries`, is refused while a send is in progress, and retires a failed earlier send whose message is still held.

  `@nextlyhq/plugin-sdk` now exports the `json` and `number` field factories, beside `date`, intended to be stable.

  Migration: `form-submission-sends` gains fields (form, notification and its name, state, attempts, retries, when it changed, cancel causes, configured and final recipients, who asked and the resend), and a new internal collection `form-submission-resends` keeps Resend's requests. Run `nextly migrate:create` and `nextly migrate` (or `nextly db:sync` in development). Sends recorded before the upgrade are not listed.

- [#4001](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4001) [`453404a`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/453404adf80784718a926c57752a79bacce8b6aa) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Forms can ask for consent: a Consent field is a required box the visitor ticks to agree to a text, such as a privacy policy. Each submission stores the choice with the text the form showed, so a later change to the text leaves what earlier visitors agreed to as it was, and an edit of a submission can never change or drop its consent. A site that sends the text it showed is held to it: a submission agreeing to a text the form no longer shows is refused.

- [#4008](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4008) [`be32ee2`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/be32ee2f39fc01c914b08f5bc4e1870dd1fb6386) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Deleting a form submission forgets the notifications it sent, in the same transaction: one not yet sent is cancelled and cleared, and the delivery records of one that went out are erased. This holds for one deletion, a bulk deletion, and deleting a form, which now deletes its submissions with it.

  The plugin records what each submission sent in a new internal `form-submission-sends` collection. Existing installations receive it through their own migrations: run `nextly migrate:create` and then `nextly migrate` (or `nextly db:sync` in development). Notifications queued before the upgrade were not recorded, so deleting their submissions does not forget them.

- [#4103](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4103) [`1d9003e`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/1d9003e69b3e4bfb33533edd54801e343f1c001e) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A submission marked Spam no longer offers Resend in its Emails box, which could only be refused; the box says it is marked Spam and to mark it Not spam to send its emails again. The Resend dialog lists who it sends to, rather than showing them as boxes that cannot be unticked, and offers a box only for a recipient who received it, to send it to them again.

- [#4080](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4080) [`2b11e20`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/2b11e20ca57212e0937226a6c6b3be49d8d4139c) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - Forms: a notification whose condition is on a choice field now reads the option by its label ("Only when Joining is In person"), not its stored value ("in_person"), in the notifications list and on the notification page.

- [#4014](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4014) [`aa25ba0`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/aa25ba06b4ff22b278833b6c475e9b277e10f2f3) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Form notifications can send to several team addresses (`recipients`), send only when all or any of several conditions hold (`conditions: { match, list }`), and choose which of the form's file fields they attach (`attachFields`). A notification saved before these reads and sends exactly as it did: its single address and single condition read as lists of one, and it attaches the file fields marked to attach to notification emails. `FormEmailNotification.to` is a list for an email with several recipients and stays a string for one, and each email carries its own `attachments`.

  In the admin, Notifications becomes a list with an Active switch per notification, and each notification opens on its own page (`?notification=<id>` on the form's Notifications page). **Add notification** offers two presets, "Notify your team" and "Confirm to the visitor". The file field's "Attach to notification emails" switch moves to each notification's "Attach files from" choice; a field's stored switch stays what a notification saved before attaches.

- [#4085](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4085) [`f6b9b53`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/f6b9b53d43d5f02304cec4fcc6e6a19d64a5a863) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A required form field left out of a submission is now refused as "<label> is required" (or the field's own error message), not with a raw type error such as "Invalid input: expected string, received undefined". In a form's Settings, "One per network" now says it needs the site to see each visitor's real address through the trusted proxy setting, and that until it can, every response is accepted.

- [#4009](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4009) [`052f95a`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/052f95a8e446c2780480cd4a85ea7c2134da8e84) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Forms can delete old submissions. **Settings › Privacy › Delete submissions after** (Never, 30 days, 90 days or 1 year, stored as `settings.keepDays`) sets how long a form keeps them. A nightly pass the plugin schedules deletes each form's submissions older than that, and spam older than 30 days whatever the setting. Each is deleted the way any deletion is, and a pass that runs out of time continues on the next jobs run.

- [#4026](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4026) [`a9f05ea`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/a9f05ea6511871319d3b502a6113edcfcb4c17e6) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Each form submission has a page of its own, at its own address, in place of the drawer the submissions list opened. It shows:
  - the answers as the visitor was asked them, with option labels, dates in words, links, and files with name, size and download;
  - fields a condition hid, marked as not asked;
  - its activity;
  - a side panel with its status, internal note and details.

  Newer and Older move through the list it was opened from, keeping its filter. Opening a New submission marks it Read for a person who may update submissions. Staff edit answers there, except a consent.

  Each new submission now keeps what it was asked (each field's label, type and option labels, and which fields its conditions hid), so it reads as it was answered after the form changes. It also keeps a title (who sent it, from a name or email answer), which the admin uses in breadcrumbs and lists. A submission stored before this reads with the form as it is now.

  `SubmissionSheet` is no longer exported from `@nextlyhq/plugin-form-builder/admin`; the page replaces it.

  Existing installations receive the new `asked` and `title` columns on the submissions collection through their own migrations: run `nextly migrate:create` and then `nextly migrate` (or `nextly db:sync` in development).

- [#4077](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4077) [`1e194ba`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/1e194ba32ecdbf0f9f502e06aebd0ecc93201795) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The form submissions list shows each form's labels as its columns and a choice
  by its option's label (for example "Backend engineer" rather than
  `backend-engineer`), on a form's Submissions tab and in the list of every
  form, which shows who sent each submission, its form and a summary. The list
  filters by date (today, the last 7 or 30 days, or a range of days) as well as
  by status, with each status tab's count beside it. Ticked rows can be marked
  as read, archived, moved to or out of Spam, exported or deleted, for those
  rows alone, each offered only to a role allowed to do it; Delete asks first.
  Export, with no rows ticked, exports everything the current filter shows, as
  a CSV headed by the form's labels or as JSON. The export route accepts the
  list's date filter (`from`, `to`) and the ticked submissions (`ids`), and its
  CSV reads a choice by its option's label.

- [#4236](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4236) [`296ddd5`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/296ddd55aa1492821d26e9750f1a6c43ff888925) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - Installing a plugin with `nextly plugins install` no longer takes back the access other plugins give site visitors, such as the form builder's public form submissions.

- [#4054](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4054) [`3e9bf1c`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/3e9bf1c5c1881d16fc1e2c47b1668f09dd734d9f) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A JSON value written inside a transaction is now stored as JSON on MySQL. A transaction's `insert` and `insertMany` handed an object or an array to the driver as it was, so MySQL refused the row or stored `[object Object]`, and on PostgreSQL an array was refused as invalid JSON. They now serialize a JSON column's value as the ordinary `insert` does, on every dialect; SQLite, `update` and `upsert` were already correct and are unchanged.

- [#4231](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4231) [`def1cad`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/def1cad9cb15d8d839c68ed798a17ec0568e8378) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - Less of the admin moves as a screen's data arrives. An editor's bar outline now stands at the bar's right end on its own, so the document's trail, which arrives with the document, no longer pushes the bar's controls along, and it draws More and the panel toggle where the bar draws them, with one still bar where the document's own buttons go. A list's outline rows are as tall as its real rows and the pager's frame follows them, so what sits under the table stays put. The dashboard's outline cards are as tall as its cards are first drawn. The Publishing section holds its place while it checks releases, and the bar's controls now reach the bar's right end.

- [#4015](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4015) [`d9b4ba7`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/d9b4ba73dcb55573f67eb77b26a1a5b610943469) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A plugin can ask whether a media item is in use: `ctx.services.media.isInUse(mediaId)` (`@experimental`) answers whether a document's field, an avatar or a logo uses it, the same condition the media library's Unused view applies, and answers in use whenever that cannot be known yet (before the usage table exists, while the usage record is not built, or for an id no item has).

- [#4105](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4105) [`2c8c7f8`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/2c8c7f8dac9e35c86d328b91759f0ab4e8239d84) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - `nextly migrate:create` now asks whether a renamed field group (`fieldGroup({ name })` in your config, including a repeatable one or a list of several groups) is a rename, as it does for a renamed column. Accept it and the migration moves the field's stored values to the new name, with the reverse in its `DOWN`. Before, the migration moved nothing and the renamed field read empty after `nextly migrate`, its values left under the old name. With no terminal, `--accept-renames` accepts it; without that flag it is declined and `migrate:create` warns that the values stay under the old name.

- [#4057](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4057) [`6c835fd`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/6c835fd04253c1b19697e6a871ddd02696dfd3a2) Thanks [@aqib-rx](https://github.com/aqib-rx)! - `nextly migrate:create` now lists every table, column and row a migration would delete before it writes the file, judged the way `nextly migrate` judges it when applying the file. That covers a collection, Single or field group no longer in the config, a removed field, a rename declined into a drop and an add, a type change, and a translation change that moves values before it drops a column or table. Each deletion says why it goes where that is known. Where the database can be read, it adds row counts and each column's count of non-empty values, opened read-only and for at most a few seconds; it needs no database. At a terminal it asks, and a no writes nothing. A run that cannot ask (CI, `--non-interactive`) now writes nothing and exits 1 unless `--accept-data-loss` (or `NEXTLY_ACCEPT_DATA_LOSS`) covers every deletion, where it used to write the file and exit 0; the refusal prints the exact consent to pass. A CI `migrate:create` that turns translation on or off now needs `--accept-data-loss` too, as `nextly migrate` already does to apply it. A file that deletes data carries a `-- Destructive:` line and one `-- Deletes:` line per table and column in its header, Schema Builder files included.

- [#4039](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4039) [`9cf52aa`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/9cf52aaaf60757edbf7e1bfc32305eda051bb46b) Thanks [@aqib-rx](https://github.com/aqib-rx)! - `nextly migrate` now carries every settings change a migration records into the registry rows, and `nextly migrate:down` undoes only what the rolled-back migrations changed there.
  - A field's help text, placeholder, hidden switch and its other admin options change no column, so they never reached a deployed registry row. They are now compared and written, by `nextly migrate` and by the development start alike, which share one comparison.
  - A description or admin block a Schema Builder entity's migration clears is now cleared in the registry. A setting no migration ever recorded for that entity is still left as it is stored.
  - The registry row of a collection, Single or field group that an applied migration drops (its snapshot no longer records an entity the one before it did, and its table is gone) is removed, on the run that applies the drop or on any later run. A row of an entity no snapshot records, or whose table still stands, is left as it is.
  - A migration that changes a field's type now writes that entity's registry row with its file: inside the file's transaction on PostgreSQL and SQLite, so the conversion and the row commit together, and right after the file's last statement and before it is recorded applied on MySQL or in a file marked to run outside a transaction. `nextly migrate`, the boot migrate step and `nextly migrate:down` all do this, so no later file in the run sees the old type.
  - `nextly migrate:down` to a point whose snapshot records the registry brings each row that snapshot records back to it, settings included, so rolling back a settings-only migration undoes it, and removes the row of an entity a rolled-back migration added. Rows nothing in the rolled-back migrations touched are left as they are. A rollback to a point whose snapshot predates recorded settings changes no row.

  ### Compatibility

  Registry writes in production move to `nextly migrate`: deploy a settings change, a dropped entity or a type change by running `nextly migrate`, which now writes what a production start no longer writes. A deployed field whose help text or placeholder differed from the code is rewritten once, at the first development start or `nextly migrate` after upgrading.

- [#4041](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4041) [`d358b0b`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/d358b0b1735cfb2e0438282e07c5c7ea51f634d0) Thanks [@zeshan-rx](https://github.com/zeshan-rx)! - `nextly workflow:move-stranded --dry-run` lists the documents a move would take, with their parts and the stages they leave, and what the move would refuse (an unknown or deactivated person, a stage the workflow lacks or one that allows publishing, no comment), writing nothing. It judges them exactly as the move does.

- [#4051](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4051) [`061dde3`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/061dde3f602907f55a345d0c1e3ad978bfd0f1cf) Thanks [@aqib-rx](https://github.com/aqib-rx)! - `next build` no longer writes to the database. Next.js starts the app while it builds, to prerender pages that read content, and that start used to create missing tables, update the collection registry, run migrations at start when they were turned on, reconcile the email templates, set SQLite's journal mode, and on an empty database create the whole schema. A build may point at a database other deployments share, so Nextly's own start now only reads there. The one write left is sealing a plugin setting that its manifest now marks secret (or that was sealed under a rotated `NEXTLY_SECRET`), which must happen before that plugin starts. A plugin's own `init` and `onReady` code still runs in the build, and what it writes is the plugin's.

  A build against a database with no Nextly tables now stops with `NEXTLY_DATABASE_NOT_MIGRATED`: "The database has no Nextly tables. Run `nextly migrate` before `next build`." On SQLite a database file that does not exist yet is not created, and on PostgreSQL a configured `db.postgres.schema` that does not exist is not created; both refuse with the same advice. Run `nextly migrate` before `next build`, as the scaffolded build script already does. Everything the build skipped happens at the first start after it.

  `@nextlyhq/adapter-drizzle` exports `isNextBuildPhase()` from the new `@nextlyhq/adapter-drizzle/build-phase` subpath, the one check Nextly and the adapters share.

- [#4043](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4043) [`4ad38c3`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/4ad38c3b6ee2dd7b31bcd5ec9447b5db0dcc4ef8) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The Page Builder now has its own item in the admin rail, right after Forms, in place of its heading in the Plugins panel. Its panel lists Patterns, Components, Layouts and Templates with how many of each you can see, then Bindings to fix with a badge while any need fixing. Clicking the item opens the new Page Builder overview: the bindings to fix first, when there are any, then the four libraries with their counts and a New action for those who may create, and the collections and Singles that have a Page Builder field, each opening its list or edit page. The overview is for people who can edit pages; anyone else opening the item lands on the first library they can read. A site preferring the old place can set `placement: "plugins"` for the plugin in `admin.pluginOverrides`.

- [#4107](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4107) [`3aed99d`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/3aed99de0e238eb43054be9629bd9b7b10c432a9) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The page builder no longer reads or writes anything on a write it has no part in. A save to a collection the site's code declares that no template can serve and that holds no blocks field, such as another plugin's private records, no longer reads the templates, writes a lock row to the address store or reads the component registry, so each such save costs several fewer database round trips.

  The composition graph lock's row is now put in place once, by the plugin's migration, on install and on `nextly migrate` for an existing install, instead of at every start. A start on PostgreSQL or MySQL no longer sends an insert that fails on a duplicate key. Run `nextly migrate` after upgrading; until then the first page-builder write that locks the graph inserts the row, as before.

- [#4099](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4099) [`48c8fd2`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/48c8fd2827b343184dca84c112fa6a5ff0d60d18) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A production start no longer makes the page builder's address store write anything, and its background work on served addresses no longer grows with the number of pages. Holding an address's lock reads the lock row for update instead of rewriting it, so a start, and every save that takes a lock, writes no lock row, content event, media usage or cache tag for it. Once the start-up passes have settled every page and entry, the plugin keeps a mark of everything the claims follow from (languages, page path, template addresses, the plugin's version, how many pages and entries there are and when they last changed), and a later start whose mark matches skips the passes after a few reads. When they do run, pages are compared with their claims a batch at a time, and only a page whose claims differ is reconciled.

- [#4111](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4111) [`33ad57f`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/33ad57f9a56795106e5a5ea40b7e6f89f601c9f4) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - A content or Single route in a worker where Nextly cannot be started no longer reads the page's
  content, or works out its own metadata, for a page-metadata provider nobody can ask; it serves the
  route's own head and no structured data, as before, and starts Nextly first where it can.

- [#3991](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3991) [`d8cd783`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/d8cd783388087835ab31209ac8572c434992df36) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A plugin can now choose where its own item goes: the top bar's right end (the default, unchanged for every existing plugin), the rail's foot just above the Inbox, or the person's menu under "Help and community". The bar and the rail's foot take a component that stays mounted on every page and at every width; the menu takes a declared item with a label, an icon, and either a link or an action, never a component. Set it with `contributes.admin.header.place`; the new types are exported from `nextly` and `@nextlyhq/plugin-sdk` as experimental.

- [#4110](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4110) [`8385af5`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/8385af5556b10691786b54f46e9f34c35fadf72b) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - A plugin context no longer fails to start when the media service it is given lacks one of the
  methods a plugin media write runs: only that write fails, when it is called.

- [#4119](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4119) [`3ea4392`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/3ea439223540b561736f852eb67926d8bbedbe25) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A plugin page can now name the data it reads as it opens, with the experimental `startupReads` on a `contributes.admin.pages` entry: reads of the plugin's own routes, each named as the page's `usePluginRoute` names it, at most four. When a tab opens on that page, the admin asks for them inside its startup request, in its first round, and the page's own read takes that answer instead of asking again. Each read keeps its route's own permission check. - [#4018](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4018) [`9b7a456`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/9b7a4560fef8adec3c72a2a34e495cd77e6797ab) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A standalone plugin can now declare its own admin panel: `contributes.admin.panel.groups` draws its menu items under headings, and a menu item takes a quiet `count` or an attention `badge`, counting one of the plugin's own collections for the reader or reading one of its own Needs your attention items. The numbers are read in one request while the panel is open and never hold it up. A menu item linking to one of the plugin's own pages that it does not register is now left out of the admin, and a development start reports it, along with a group, count or badge naming something the plugin does not declare or own. The new types are exported from `nextly` and `@nextlyhq/plugin-sdk` as experimental.

- [#4084](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4084) [`9b16475`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/9b164754a27b1e4f7896fcbd149fec57f11fa0ce) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A plugin is told of each change of its own queued emails inside the transaction that makes it, through `ctx.services.email.onQueuedEmailChange`: an attempt starting, a failure a retry can help, sent, failed, or cancelled with why (a person, the plugin itself, or a request made while an attempt was with the provider). Each change lists every recipient the send went to after `email.beforeSend` filters, with its line, what became of it, a masked hint and the plugin's own rotation-stable digest; no address. `readQueued` reads where the plugin's own queued emails stand, and `recipientDigest` gives the digest for an address.

  Sends and queued sends take `excludeRecipients`, a list of those digests, compared after the filters run: the recipients it names are left out, and when no `to` is left each remaining copy gets a message of its own. People cancel a queued email with `nextly.email.cancelQueued`, which asks the new `manage-email-deliveries` permission of a checked call.

  Migration: `manage-email-deliveries` is seeded on the next start, granted to super-admin only, under the newly reserved system resource `email-deliveries`: an installation with a collection or Single of that slug must rename it. No table or column changes.

- [#4124](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4124) [`e91a85a`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/e91a85a8a1ec664fb83b1bf5211f1496f25b732d) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The admin reads the collection, Single and field group registry once, and then not again until it changes. Registry rows and listings were kept for a second and read again after it, so a dashboard, list or edit screen read the same rows over and over; they are now kept until the database's schema version records a registry change, which every registry write (a Schema Builder save, a rename, a delete, `nextly migrate`, a plugin install) now does. Another server sees such a change within the two seconds it already takes to reload its schema.

- [#4052](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4052) [`851df16`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/851df16df8526abe79f44ae9a0055ddbed830ef8) Thanks [@aqib-rx](https://github.com/aqib-rx)! - `nextly repair-columns --apply` now converts a lossy column, one holding
  values its new type cannot hold, when the data-loss consent names that column:
  `--accept-data-loss=<table>.<column>`, or `NEXTLY_ACCEPT_DATA_LOSS`. The values
  cleared, set to null, are exactly the rows the run's report names, and the
  repair record keeps the consent and the count. The consent without a list, or
  one naming only the table, does not cover a repair: the column is skipped and
  the report says which consent would.

  In a terminal, a run with no consent naming the column asks once per lossy
  column, naming the count and the first rows, and the table is never held while
  it waits for the answer. Whether a run may ask is decided before anything is
  asked; a run that may not (no terminal, `--non-interactive`, CI or `--json`)
  never reads standard input, and skips the column.

  On MySQL the clearing is a step of its own, committed with its record, so a
  stopped run resumes from it; a clearing still to run needs that run's own
  consent. A value that would be cleared where the column does not allow a null
  now blocks the conversion, since clearing it would need a value invented.

- [#4047](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4047) [`328af70`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/328af70ed2337de770723d48d5d6bfe0448d7619) Thanks [@zeshan-rx](https://github.com/zeshan-rx)! - In the admin, restoring a version now puts its values back into the editor rather than writing
  them. "Restore" in History lists every field the version holds differently, all chosen. A field
  you may not read or change, or one no longer in the content type, is listed unchosen with its
  reason. A field with an unsaved edit says the restore replaces it. The chosen fields come back
  as unsaved edits, and Undo takes them out again. A single changed field can also be restored
  straight from the version on screen. Nothing is stored until you save, and the save keeps the
  draft unpublished and records which version each restored value came from. A version is
  restored only into the editor of its own language, and on a translated document the list names
  that language.

- [#4094](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4094) [`d3cf486`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/d3cf486d31236bb619eb27c3c2353313258009c9) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Rich text HTML can now be styled by the site: pass `richTextStyles: "none"` to a Direct API read (or `?richTextStyles=none` over REST) together with `richTextFormat: "html"` or `"both"`, and the HTML carries no style Nextly adds. Every element has a class in the `nextly-rich-text-` namespace (`nextly-rich-text-paragraph`, `nextly-rich-text-h2`, `nextly-rich-text-link`, `nextly-rich-text-button--outline` and so on), and alignment is a class too (`nextly-rich-text-align-center`). Styles an author chose in the editor, a text colour or a button's colours, are kept. The classes are listed in the rich text field docs. Without the option, the HTML is exactly what it was.

- [#4087](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4087) [`28adb3d`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/28adb3dc3619c76f953b1564189665dc676ce23f) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - Plugin pages can draw the admin's own notice, side panel, in-page tabs, progress bar, action menu and hover hint through `@nextlyhq/plugin-sdk/admin` (experimental): `Alert`, `Sheet`, `Tabs`, `Progress`, `DropdownMenu` and `Tooltip`, with their parts and prop types. - [#4079](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4079) [`fbf4caa`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/fbf4caa83fe7ce9a5ff89074920d8043b5aa9c07) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - Plugins can now build their admin pages from the admin's own building blocks through `@nextlyhq/plugin-sdk/admin` (experimental): the list surface (`ListView` with its search, filters, columns menu and empty states, plus `useTableColumns`), `Breadcrumbs` for the trail in the top bar, `SegmentedChoice`, the setup `Checklist`, `SettingsRowGroup`, `Badge`, and a `layout="row"` settings row on `FieldShell`.

- [#4117](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4117) [`2051992`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/20519922a4979d81a3e0fb5273f30877a1ed082d) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The SEO plugin's address record moves from a collection to its own tables,
  `seo__addresses` and `seo__notes`, written on the save's transaction with
  `ctx.db`. Each claim, release and lock row is now one statement rather than a
  whole entry save, so an entry save on PostgreSQL issues about a tenth of the
  address bookkeeping it did. Run `nextly migrate` to create the tables; the
  first start afterwards moves the rows an earlier version kept, before the
  plugin answers any save, and leaves the old collection in place, unused.

  `ctx.db.select(...).lock("update" | "share")` (experimental) reads rows
  `FOR UPDATE` or `FOR SHARE` inside a transaction, which on MySQL also reads
  the latest committed rows rather than the transaction's snapshot. A public
  address participant's deadlock is reported as a conflict to try again, as
  core reports its own.

The admin entry still exports `SeoBulkPage` and `SeoReceivedPage`, now the screens that send an old bookmark on to Pages and Inspect, so a committed component map that names them compiles; in development the map is then rewritten with the current names (`SeoBulkMoved`, `SeoReceivedMoved`). The old names are deprecated.

Import's last step gives every title and description a result, "Nothing to import" where the source holds no value, in the table and in the downloaded report; a file's match table counts "Pages it changes", as the import does; the step labels wrap on a phone rather than being cut short, and the four counts sit two by two there. - [#4132](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4132) [`e772619`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/e772619d45a2019060ac2685348d5c2172d083ce) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - A choice card in the SEO plugin's settings now darkens its border to full strength on hover, as the admin's other choice cards do, instead of a faded border too light to see against the page.

  directory with the route's name, which Turbopack could not bound, so every source file and
  the `public` folder were deployed as server code: slower deploys, and a risk of a host's size

  draw the admin's drop area with `FileDropArea` from `@nextlyhq/plugin-sdk/admin`.

- [#4109](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4109) [`58781b8`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/58781b8a5e68e8e015ed6e820749dc803e41f625) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The SEO plugin's log of addresses not found counts only requests a route answered not found. Logging from the site's `app/not-found.tsx`, as the guide showed, counted every page view, since Next.js renders that page for every page. `notFoundLogged()` from the new `@nextlyhq/plugin-seo/next` answers not found and logs the address once the response is sent, once per request though the page and its `generateMetadata` both answer it; pass it as a content route's `notFound`, call it from a site's own routes, and from an `app/[...missing]` catch-all for addresses no route matches. The Proxy no longer passes the address on for a prefetch, so a prefetch is never logged. `logNotFound` keeps working. Remove any logging from `app/not-found.tsx`.

The SEO plugin's not-found log moves from a collection to the plugin's own table (`seo__not_found`) and counts a request for an address already logged in one statement, and a first request in at most three, where each was a whole entry save of about 80 statements before.
