- [#4097](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4097) [`a06eee0`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/a06eee006dd9ca38fe80b331b835672f0a3a23ac) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - The SEO Overview matches its design: the verdict on Search health has a dot in its colour and the error, warning and notice counts are written in their colours rather than as chips; Search health and Pages lead with a smaller figure; the setup steps sit in two columns with done steps crossed off.

  Plugin pages can draw these too (experimental, through `@nextlyhq/plugin-sdk/admin`): `Stat` takes `tone` (`success`, `warning`, `destructive` or `info`) and `size="compact"`, and `Checklist` takes `columns={2}` and `doneStyle="struck"`. Without them both draw as before, so the dashboard's setup card is unchanged.

  A plugin's own sidebar panel no longer repeats the plugin's name as a small heading under the panel's title; the menu is still named by it for screen readers.

- [#4035](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4035) [`0460128`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/046012897a4409141396b90a1658b5c7e66697cd) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - Bulk edit and the SEO import now reach Singles. Each Single the SEO plugin is added to is a content type of the Bulk edit screen with its one page, read and saved as the person asking at the version they read, and the import reads and writes it beside the collections, its existing field groups included (such as a `metaData` component on a homepage Single), with the same dry run.   The import's dry run now reports each page it read and each record it passed over: what it would set, what is already the same as the page's automatic value, what a person already typed and keeps, and why one is skipped. A second run after an import sets nothing.

- [#4048](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4048) [`74151e0`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/74151e09ec807f1ea7c3c4276b49247bf4c1e27e) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - SEO plugin fixes for titles, lengths, share images and installing:
  - A title pattern that goes on after `{Site name}`, such as `{Title} | {Site name} Blog`, now always keeps the site's name: "Why we chose Acme" gives "Why we chose Acme | Acme Blog" rather than "Why we chose Acme Blog". The name is left out only where the pattern ends with it and the title already ends with the name.
  - `metaTitle` and `metaDescription` save at any length. Search engines cut a long title or description to fit rather than refusing it, so the SEO tab and the problem list warn with the length (`68 characters, Google shows about 60`) instead of the save being refused. Pass `seoPlugin({ hardLengthLimits: true })` to refuse a title over 60 characters or a description over 160, as before. On a site that already has the plugin, the two fields' changed settings are a schema change like any other: run `nextly migrate:create`, and `nextly migrate` where you deploy, before a longer title saves there.
  - A share image in a format some networks don't show on a card (SVG, AVIF or WebP) is named in the problem list and the SEO tab, fixed by making a share image, which is a JPEG.
  - `@nextlyhq/plugin-sdk` is now a dependency of the plugin rather than a peer, so it is installed with the plugin and a site can no longer leave it out of a production install. A client secret wrapped by a site's own copy of the SDK is still read.

- [#3886](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3886) [`7e1c7a2`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/7e1c7a2885d4e34884596edff9aba42581a6e320) Thanks [@muzzamil-rx](https://github.com/muzzamil-rx)! - `nextly migrate:baseline` now compiles the app's extension schema, as `migrate:create` and `migrate:check` already do. Adopting a database built by `db:sync` records the tables an app declared through `db.schema.extend` and names the elements it contributed to other owners' tables, so the first `migrate:create` after graduating no longer re-creates a table that is already standing or re-emits an index the database already has.

- [#4044](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4044) [`e5f78c1`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/e5f78c1aa697a80e9c24b0430eb5e51e4a0b33fe) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - The admin's sign-in page offers "Sign up" only when `auth.allowRegistration` is on, and `/admin/register` says registration is closed, with a link back to sign-in, while it is off; `GET /admin/api/auth/setup-status` now reports `allowRegistration`, and every signed-out admin screen has a `main` landmark. A hand-named migration without a timestamp (such as `get_started_only.sql`) no longer counts as the newest, so the schema version a production start checks names the newest timestamped one. `--help` after a command name the CLI does not have (for example `nextly events abandon --help` on a release without `events`) is refused as an unknown command, rather than printing the parent's help.

- [#4068](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4068) [`1c9568c`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/1c9568c6a8783d880628e20af3c7d0fcc5ca378e) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Form submissions keep the page they were sent from: the origin and path of the
  browser's `Referer` (never its query or fragment, and only for `http`/`https`
  pages), shown on each submission's page under Details › Page. The plugin adds
  one field to the submissions collection, `page` (long text), created on the
  next schema apply; earlier submissions keep none.

- [#4089](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4089) [`684c0be`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/684c0be6c9365e928012eb15955dd895d1f6374f) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The Form Builder's submissions lists fit their box and wait for what they need. A form's Submissions tab no longer shows every form's columns for a moment before its own: the list stays loading until the form and the person's rights are known. A list too narrow for its columns, as on a laptop beside the Forms panel, leaves some out instead of scrolling sideways: every form's list gives up its Summary, then names the form under the sender, and a form's tab shows fewer of its first fields until the person picks columns themselves. Someone who can only read submissions gets no tick boxes, since a ticked row would offer them nothing, and the delete question answers "Keep it" for one submission.

- [#4118](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4118) [`3d0f23c`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/3d0f23c2310ba33810fc73ee73a212b33926b350) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The admin's startup request now leaves as the browser reads the admin page, before the admin's main code has loaded. A small script in the prebuilt page sends it, and the admin takes that request, and the paths it named, instead of sending its own. The script is written from the admin's own code when the page is built, so it sends exactly the request the admin would; it carries nothing about the visitor, so the page stays the same for everyone. Where the script does not run, the admin sends the request itself as before; where its request fails or its answer cannot be read, the admin sends it once more without showing an error. `RootLayout`'s `nonce` now covers this script too, for a site that renders the admin with a nonce-based Content Security Policy.

- [#3574](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3574) [`d3fc9a0`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/d3fc9a06bd103a3b0a5a04c80ae73abfd4801332) Thanks [@zeshan-rx](https://github.com/zeshan-rx)! - Under `experimental.perLanguageStorage`, a document keeps one pending change for its shared fields and one per language: an edit to a shared field, made in any language, is held in the shared draft and reaches every language; an edit to a translatable field is held in that language's draft only. Every language's editor read reports `_sharedChangesPending`, and the language panel says when shared fields have unpublished changes.

  Publishing a language puts its draft and the shared draft live. With the setting off nothing changes.

- [#4058](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4058) [`5af3565`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/5af3565003e86a2035e8cb728ec51ef9d2a0cfb5) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - A Next.js site deployed on Vercel no longer answers 500 on every unknown address. On the server Nextly loaded the client `next/navigation` for `notFound()` and redirects, which Next's require hook sends on to the pages router's runtime, `react-dom`, `styled-jsx` and `client-only`, files a deployment that ships only traced files does not have. It now loads Next's server build of `next/navigation`, which needs none of them, by a literal specifier a tracer can follow. `withNextly()` also adds the Next.js files Nextly loads at request time (from `next/cache`, `next/headers`, `next/server` and that entry) to every route's `outputFileTracingIncludes`, and `nextlyTracingIncludes()` from `nextly/next` gives the same list to a config not wrapped in it; new projects from `create-nextly-app` include it. Where a file is still missing, a not-found page answers 404 and a permanent redirect answers 308 with Next.js's own errors, cached reads run uncached, and the media revalidation after an upload is skipped, each named once in the log, instead of a 500.

- [#4090](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4090) [`2692bca`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/2692bca5ee516b54cdda6589ac74f654fca31467) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A `Date` written inside a transaction to a column the table model does not declare now stores the same instant as one written to a declared date column. On PostgreSQL it was bound by node-postgres in the app server's own time zone, and a `timestamp` column drops the offset, so on a server not running in UTC the value was stored shifted by the server's offset. Each adapter now spells such a `Date` as its date field columns do. MySQL (since its sessions were pinned to UTC) and SQLite already stored the right instant and are unchanged. Rows written that way before this release keep their shifted value: on PostgreSQL with a server not in UTC, a date written through an undeclared key inside a transaction may need checking.

- [#3817](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3817) [`9768bd0`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/9768bd0828e0e72c533071790363f35ab7277f0c) Thanks [@zeshan-rx](https://github.com/zeshan-rx)! - Every workflow move now reaches webhooks and history. Whenever a part of a document (a language, or the shared fields) changes review stage or loses its approval, Nextly records one `workflow.stage_changed` webhook event for that part, in the same transaction as the move, and delivers it after the move is saved. This covers a step, an edit or a deployed change of workflow definition that withdraws an approval (also when the part stays in its stage), a deploy that renames a stage, redirects a removed one or detaches the workflow, discarding a working draft, and the `workflow:move-stranded` command. The event's `data` names the document (`collection` or `single`, its slug and id), the part, `from` and `to` (`to` is null when the part's review state was removed), the `cause` (`step`, `edit`, `definition`, `rename`, `redirect`, `detach`, `discard` or `recovery`), `approvalWithdrawn` and the hash of the workflow definition it was made under; its `actor` is the person or API key who acted, or the system. Endpoints can subscribe to `workflow.stage_changed`, or receive it through "all events". A comparison of versions can now start from `since-submitted` (the version a part last entered review at) or `since-approved` (the version its last approval named); a part with neither is refused with the reason, and the comparison view says which baseline it compares from. Known limits: publishing does not yet record this event when it closes a part's review; the admin's webhook form does not yet list `workflow.stage_changed` on its own (choose all events, or create the endpoint through the API); and history shows a workflow's events by their kind's name ("Workflow submit · English").

- [#3816](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3816) [`053b304`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/053b30400133794f28d18091de254ef8ad4565ed) Thanks [@zeshan-rx](https://github.com/zeshan-rx)! - A workflow now tells the people it names. When a part of a document is assigned to a person (directly, or as a stage's default reviewer when the part enters that stage), that person gets a notice in their list of notices. When a part is approved or sent back with requested changes, the person accountable for the stage it left gets one: whoever brought it into review, by a step or by an edit, including on a workflow with no submit step. Each notice names the collection, the document's title, the language (or the shared fields), the step and who acted, and links to the document's edit page; once the document is deleted it says so and has no link. Where the site sends email, the notice is also emailed, unless that trigger's email is switched off in the workflow's settings (`emails.assigned`, `emails.approved`, `emails.changesRequested`); the notice itself is always given. Work assigned to a role tells no one, nor does a part no one is accountable for, and nobody is told of their own act. Release notice emails look and behave as before.

- [#4023](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/4023) [`797d608`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/797d6088285fd6a7fe9655cda5b3b48731687abe) Thanks [@zeshan-rx](https://github.com/zeshan-rx)! - A production start no longer reads the review-state table's shape: bringing review state into line with changed workflows (renamed, removed and detached stages, and approvals given under an earlier definition) now runs at a development start and in `nextly migrate`, the deploy step, instead of at every start.

## 0.0.2-alpha.75

### Patch Changes

- [#3940](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3940) [`a48148e`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/a48148eb96ba786cf737e04da3a64e1a2955eb64) Thanks [@faisal-rx](https://github.com/faisal-rx)! - A Schema Builder save's migration checks judge the saved entity by its kind as well as its slug, so a collection, a Single and a field group that share a slug are told apart. The writer behind a Builder save now reads what tells the kinds apart from one table; collections are saved exactly as before.

- [#3896](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3896) [`f23fc5d`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/f23fc5df792e8b75bcde99122c59e8c0b75027e0) Thanks [@faisal-rx](https://github.com/faisal-rx)! - A Schema Builder save no longer reports a change to a field that did not change. A field made through the REST API, the Direct API or code may store no `required`, `unique` or `hasMany` setting, while the Builder always sends each one, so every save of such a field, even one that only changed its label, asked to confirm a schema change. A missing setting now counts as off.

- [#3812](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3812) [`5ab427d`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/5ab427d8063b2ffd96946bfa9bb45e3a444f943d) Thanks [@faisal-rx](https://github.com/faisal-rx)! - A code-first collection whose `dbName` moves it to a table that is already there is refused
  at start and by `db:sync`, naming both tables, and keeps its old table: before, the sync only
  warned and recorded the new table, so the collection was served from a table that did not
  hold its entries. The same holds when the database refuses the table rename, or the tables
  cannot be read to decide. The collection is reported among the ones not set up, and serves
  from its old table until the configuration or the tables are put right.

- [#3793](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3793) [`c8470d1`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/c8470d14a59163834debdc13e70a7753e8384323) Thanks [@faisal-rx](https://github.com/faisal-rx)! - A field group or Single something depends on can no longer be deleted. While a field of a collection, a Single or another field group places the field group, a foreign key a plugin or the app declares points at its table, or a plugin or the app has added a column, index, foreign key or check to it, the Schema Builder's delete, the schema API and the Direct API's `fieldGroups.delete()` refuse before anything is removed, naming each with its owner and table and saying what to do. A Single is refused the same way, through the Schema Builder and the schema API, for a foreign key into one of its tables or another owner's element on one. Where those cannot be read the delete is refused rather than going ahead; before, a field group's refusal named nothing, and a registry it could not read was taken for one that held no use. A field group's delete now holds the schema lock from its check to its last drop. `FieldGroupRegistryService.findComponentReferences` is deprecated, and now throws when a registry cannot be read instead of returning the references it could read. Fixed: a relationship or upload inside a group with no name was not counted as pointing at its collection, so that collection could be deleted while still pointed at; it is now found and named at the level it is stored, and so is a field group placed inside one.

- [#3926](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3926) [`7de0c60`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/7de0c6008376175799f55f5d116295f89c576f1b) Thanks [@faisal-rx](https://github.com/faisal-rx)! - A field group's table now has one shape whoever builds it, and a Schema Builder save no longer rewrites columns it does not change.
  - The table the Builder's create makes and the one a `migrate:create` file makes now agree. The first Builder save of a field group used to drop the `_order`, `created_at` and `updated_at` defaults and add a `created_at` index. On MySQL a save could also turn a text field's `text` column into `varchar(255)`, which MySQL refuses once a value is longer, and `created_at`/`updated_at` from `datetime` into `timestamp`.
  - When upgrading: a field group made by a migration file gets those three column defaults with its next migration (no data changes), and one made by the Builder gets the `created_at` index with its next save.
  - `migrate:create` describes a Builder Single's or field group's table as the Builder made it, so on MySQL its unbounded text stays `text`.
  - On MySQL a migration that sets a column's default to a function, such as `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`, now runs; it was a syntax error.
  - A development save no longer loses a unique index that holds a field's uniqueness under a name other than the one the schema declares.

- [#3923](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3923) [`8dd9dfa`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/8dd9dfaf4dd4057962f727ec59c0994b16b36f4a) Thanks [@muzzamil-rx](https://github.com/muzzamil-rx)! - A fractional price is refused once, not twice. The write gate's whole-number rule now answers for every integer-backed number field, so the commerce plugin's own whole-number validator on `price`, `stockCount` and `maxPerLine` reported the same mistake a second time, beside it; the plugin's rule is removed and one refusal names the field.

- [#3600](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3600) [`c4d4b6c`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/c4d4b6c36fd09d5bcd35d74debf0e98f97030a13) Thanks [@aqib-rx](https://github.com/aqib-rx)! - A hasMany relationship, or one naming several collections, that the Schema Builder creates is now stored as a list, with no foreign key to one row, so saving and reading several related entries works on PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQLite. Switching a relationship from one related entry to many keeps each value as a one-item list: on a collection or a Single through a Schema Builder save, a configuration reload, `db:sync`, a development start or a generated migration; on a field group or a translated field's translations through a Schema Builder save, a configuration reload or a generated migration. Switching from many to one converts when every row holds at most one, and is refused, naming the field and the rows, while a row holds more, or, for a required field, none. Switching to or from naming several collections is refused while a row holds a value, by the apply before anything changes and by a generated migration before any DDL. A change no road can carry is refused rather than leaving values in the old shape: a switch made while the field starts or stops being translated, a switch made in the same change that renames the field, a field group's switch through `db:sync`, and any switch when the registry recording what the field was cannot be read.

  Migration snapshots now record each relation column's storage shape (`referenceShape`), which is how a generated migration sees a switch on SQLite, where every shape is text. The key is optional: a snapshot written before it plans what it planned before, so a switch made across such a snapshot is not converted by the file.

  On PostgreSQL and MySQL, a hasMany column an earlier save created as a single reference, with a foreign key, is converted to a list by the next schema apply or by the next migration `migrate:create` generates.

- [#3919](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3919) [`beb6028`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/beb60288a87145fd96023d0a9ccba446a7066361) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - A published page whose address changes now leaves a permanent redirect from its old address, in the save or, after a deploy, at the next start, stored to the end of its chain and never in a loop. A page taking a redirect's address replaces it, and a redirect that cannot be saved refuses the save with the reason. The SEO plugin answers redirects from the site's Proxy before the page is served, exact addresses before `/old/*` patterns, and keeps a bounded log of the page addresses that were not found, written by `logNotFound` from the site's not-found page. `addressOfRequest(url)` from `nextly` and `@nextlyhq/plugin-sdk` answers the language and kept path a request asks for.

- [#3985](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3985) [`561ebcf`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/561ebcf15ea270ec14715b3c63507f3bba7cdacd) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - The SEO tab, the problem list and the check of what search engines received now see what a Page Builder design sets for a page. The Page Builder offers a page's design level as a service (`designSeo`), worked out by the route's own derivation (`designMetadataFor` from `@nextlyhq/blocks-react/next`), and the SEO plugin reads it where the Page Builder is installed: a description only the design sets is no longer listed as missing, and the SEO tab says a value comes from the page's template.

- [#3842](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3842) [`092ba3c`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/092ba3ca05d604424e7db144c9221fd8962fbf54) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - A collection or Single can declare where its pages are served with `publicAddress` (`"/blog/{slug}"`, or `"/about"` for a Single), judged by one rule when the configuration loads. `publicAddressOf(type, entry, locale)` answers an entry's address from that declaration, and `typesWithoutAddress()` lists the types with none yet. A type made in the Schema Builder has its address supplied by a plugin through the `publicAddress.template` filter, judged by the same rule; a type declared in code never asks a plugin. Both functions are experimental.

- [#3988](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3988) [`f509da8`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/f509da8e03ffd2e29bdf736ddfcce55a7c86370b) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A permission is now marked as no longer declared only by `nextly migrate`, as it applies the recorded migration whose snapshot drops it: an app permission, or a plugin's permission whichever writer added it, for each owner the migration's snapshot or the one before it records (for the first migration after the registry record, each plugin the registry baseline held). Every grant of it is kept and the log names the roles holding it; a later migration that declares it again clears the mark. A plugin a migration knows nothing of keeps its permissions, Nextly's own are never marked, and a snapshot without the registry metadata or the permissions marks nothing. No server start marks a permission any more, in production or in development: a build that stops declaring a permission, an older one included, leaves it as it is.

- [#3806](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3806) [`937f4a9`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/937f4a9c0fd64c3c474de216f08e0d6d39f28771) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - A plugin can add fields to every collection and Single a site defines without naming them. `contributes.extend` takes a scope as its target, `{ every: ["collection", "single"], except: [...] }`, which reaches the site's own types, including those made in the Schema Builder, and never a plugin's own types, Nextly's system types or field groups. A type the scope reaches that already has a field of that name is left as it is and named in a warning at startup. `typesReachedBy` and the `ContentTypeScope` type (`@experimental`) give the same answer to anything else that needs it.

- [#3797](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3797) [`ae01bc5`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/ae01bc51ac7bcebf1a309cac355ccd37a8f4704c) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - A plugin can now work out the head of every page the site serves. - [#3995](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3995) [`47bcd6d`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/47bcd6da1932297f377dd5c432ac492ed42553e1) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - `nextly plugins install` now adds the permissions and roles the plugin declares and sets every preset role's grants, with the record of the Nextly release that set them, as `nextly migrate` from the same release does, in the same transaction that records the plugin installed. A plugin a production start serves therefore has its access whether or not a `nextly migrate` follows, and an install that stops part-way, or cannot set the preset grants, records nothing. `nextly plugins uninstall`, with or without `--keep-data`, marks the plugin's permissions as no longer declared in the transaction that records it uninstalled, keeping every grant and logging the roles that hold each; installing it again clears the marks. A `nextly migrate` run with an uninstalled plugin still in the configuration no longer declares that plugin's permissions again, so their marks and grants stay as the uninstall left them; a plugin with no install or uninstall recorded is declared as before. In production, both commands refuse before changing anything when run from a Nextly release older than the one that set the preset grants, naming the release to run them from.

  - `useDocumentValues(paths)` answers the named fields of the document being edited, by their dot paths, before any save, and draws again only when one of them changes.
  - `useDocumentField(path)` answers one field's value, whether it may be written now, and `set(next)`, which writes as the author typing would and marks the document changed.   - Both work in any component a plugin draws inside an edit page, on an entry, a new one or a Single. They read the editor's own form, so a component with a form of its own still reads the document. Outside an editor they answer `null`.

  It used to read every collection's table on each start through `getNextly()`

  columns, core tables and retired auth tables or image sizes, and the indexes of

  missing. Those reports are now a development start's (`NODE_ENV` set to `development`). Run

  names what it finds.

  A production start still names the rules left in the retired `access_rules`
  column of the registry tables, which this release no longer enforces, and
  still refuses a database laid out for the other choice of
  `experimental.perLanguageStorage`.

  A dry run names each file from the project folder with `/` between its parts on every operating system, Windows included.

Either way the app keeps serving and nothing is written. `nextly migrate`, `migrate:down`, Schema Builder saves and plugin installs and uninstalls now store that version in the same transaction as the registry rows they write.

  or Single already holds is refused with `SLUG_SAME_SNAKE_CASE`, as creating one already was:
  `team-updates` beside `team_updates` reads as one address. A collection rename is now judged
  by the same address rule every other road applies (reserved names, routes, a taken slug and a
  same snake_case form), where before it compared the exact slug alone and threw a plain error.

  or renamed onto the same form at the same moment is seen and refused, rather than both
  succeeding.

A rename is refused, naming the fields, while a relationship that can point at several collections lists it, while a relationship defined in code points at it, or while a relationship already points at the new name. A renamed collection keeps its table, and a key to it, added or changed later, references that table. A schema the rename rewrote moves to a new version, so an editor still holding it from before the rename cannot save the old target back.

  with `RENAME_TARGET_TAKEN` naming the table and both columns, on every road that applies a

  every dialect. This holds for a translated field's companion table too. Before, on MySQL, the
  database's "Duplicate column name" was passed over as a step an earlier run had made: the

  Saving a translated collection again, after an earlier change that made a field translated did not finish, is now judged by the migration the Schema Builder writes as it is by the save itself.   and loop items are left out. It lists those not yet declared, with a Declare

  Paging forward and back keeps working past 1,000. The pager offers the next page, but no jump to a last page that hasn't been counted. With 1,000 entries or fewer, the list shows the exact total as before.

  decided by the database: MySQL silently rounded it, PostgreSQL answered a
  500, SQLite stored it as written. The entry write validation now refuses
  the fraction with a validation error naming the field — before any write,
  identically on every dialect, on create, update and bulk, and on hasMany
  list elements. Fields declared with `dbType: "decimal"` or the float format

  fractional row keeps reading and publishing unchanged.

  correctly, and after this change the same write is a 400 validation refusal.

  value before saving.

Before, MySQL refused such a save with a database error, or cut the value short. The limit now holds on every dialect: PostgreSQL and SQLite, which kept a longer value before, refuse it with the same message, so the same request gets the same answer everywhere.
  - The account page sends only the fields you changed. A picture address stored before this limit, longer than 255 characters, is not sent again when you change only your name, so that save still goes through.

  - Settings, a user's detail page, the entry form (in both the collection entry and the Single editor) and the login page draw the blocks sent to them, in the order sent, each behind its own error boundary, and settings and a user's detail page draw contributed tabs after the page's own content.

A screen's still outline appears from 0.4 s in the place its parts will take (the dashboard's cards, a list's table, an editor's fields and side panel, and the other main screens), a thin line moves under the bar from 0.5 s, and from 5 s one line says the server is starting; none of them appears when the data arrives sooner, and under reduced motion nothing moves. The outline gives way to the screen without moving the frame, an editor's bar keeps its buttons in place while the document loads, and the rail holds neutral shapes until its entries are known. A browser that has never signed in here opens on the real sign-in form at once: it takes typing while the server starts, says it is connecting, and sends the sign-in once, when the server answers. Every screen still waits for the server to confirm the session before it draws any data. The outlines are still, never pulsing: `Skeleton` takes a `still` prop for an outline that does not move.

- [#3987](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3987) [`1002097`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/1002097dcfeb480692a1f95db9a459c2ea33cd8b) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The admin remembers the map of the site on each editor's device, so a new tab draws the real rail and Content panel at once, before the server answers, then replaces them with what the server sends. It keeps only metadata: the menu as that person sees it, the schemas of the collections, Singles and field groups they read (a later read of one asks "has it changed?" and is not sent again when it has not), the site's public logo and name, interface preferences, and a note that someone signed in here; never an entry, a media item, a user, a form's values, a session token or a permission list, and no form is ever filled from it. What it keeps is labelled with the person, the admin build, the schema version and the permission version, and is discarded when any of them changes. Signing out, or the session ending, removes everything about the person in every open tab, which signs out too; only the public logo and name stay, so the sign-in screen keeps the site's look. Remembering is on by default; set `NEXTLY_ADMIN_DEVICE_MEMORY=off` to keep nothing on the device, and each browser removes what it kept on its next visit. Plugins keep an author's choices by the same rules through `devicePreferenceStore` from `@nextlyhq/plugin-sdk/admin` (experimental), which the page builder's editor now uses for its panels, recent pages and icons, template previews and getting-started card; `userPreferenceStore` from `@nextlyhq/builder/shell` takes an optional opener for such a store. The startup request's answer now carries `X-Nextly-Device-Memory`, `X-Nextly-Schema-Version` and `X-Nextly-Permission-Version` (a hash of the permission version) for this.

The start marks
  the permission orphaned as before, but setting the preset roles no longer takes an orphaned
  permission away from them (or gives it to one that does not hold it), so the Admin role keeps its
  grant and has it as before when the plugin returns. The log line written when a permission is
  orphaned or declared again now names the roles that hold it.

A field group's resolved fields, which the server adds when it hands a definition out, are no longer written back into the field's options on save. Every field with an error is now marked, at any depth; a field without a name inside a group is refused at save as one at the top level is.

- [#3883](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3883) [`e50375b`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/e50375b6e1456f99fb8e4cd0be966414eab23623) Thanks [@aqib-rx](https://github.com/aqib-rx)! - A Schema Builder save that switches a relationship between one related entry and many, or to or from several collections, is applied by the push again, with its migration file recorded once the push has run: the switch is refused, naming the field and its rows, while rows would not survive it, its values are converted, and a column an older save left as one reference is repaired. Saves that write their migration had skipped all three.

- [#3888](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3888) [`dd6e1e4`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/dd6e1e4423920e02956106ed229bd9aab693e4f2) Thanks [@aqib-rx](https://github.com/aqib-rx)! - A Schema Builder collection whose group holds a group with no name, which only lays its fields out, saves again. The definition file now accepts a group without a name; every other field still needs one.

  A Schema Builder field change that removes a field and fills a new required field over existing rows in the same save is no longer refused with "destructive_drop:… is not a change to a field of this collection". The drop's confirmation is now matched against the fields the collection had before the save.

- [#3778](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3778) [`0545e6c`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/0545e6cf84b83b7b85c2aa852313e6b4b8ea07dd) Thanks [@aqib-rx](https://github.com/aqib-rx)! - A Schema Builder save of a collection now writes the migration and snapshot `nextly migrate:create` would write for that collection into your migrations folder (`db.migrationsDir`), after recording its whole definition in `db.uiSchemaFile`. In development the save runs that file the way `nextly migrate` does and records it applied with its checksum, so `nextly migrate` and `migrate:create` have nothing left to do. Outside development the save writes the definition, the file and the snapshot, runs nothing, and the deploy's `nextly migrate` applies them.
  - Every save of a collection does this: a create, a field change from the Builder's schema dialog, an update of its settings or fields through `updateCollection`, and a delete, whether made in the admin, through a plugin's `ctx.services.collections`, or through the `CollectionsHandler`. Nothing is written to `src/db/migrations/dynamic` any more. Files an earlier version wrote there are not read; delete the folder once you no longer need it.
  - A save first runs the checks `nextly migrate` runs before it writes anything. While an applied migration file is edited or missing, or an attempt is unfinished, the save is refused with `NEXTLY_MIGRATION_HISTORY_REFUSED` (409) and the text `nextly migrate` prints, and nothing is written. A delete is refused before anything is torn down.
  - The answers you give in the schema dialog are part of the file, so every database it reaches is settled the same way: a rename keeps the column's values; rows that do not fit a field made required are filled with the value you gave, or deleted where you chose that, before the column becomes NOT NULL. The preview names each fill and each delete, and `nextly migrate` asks consent (`--accept-data-loss`) before running such a delete on a database whose rows it would remove. A JSON field's fill may be any JSON value. An answer is taken only for a field the save makes required, named by the field's own name (a camelCase one too), and any other is refused with nothing written. A unique field takes no single fill value, and a delete of 10,000 rows or more is refused, as before.
  - An update through `updateCollection`, and on a translated collection a field change or turning translation on or off, keeps the development push it has always had; its migration is written as well and recorded applied once the push has run, and the save is refused, naming the file, where the database does not stand as the file says.
  - `nextly migrate:create` now writes a translated field's accepted rename as a rename of its column in the translations table, so its values stay under the new name; before, it added the new column and left the values under the old one.
  - The first save of a collection whose table no snapshot records (one an earlier version made) writes `<timestamp>_<slug>_adopt.sql`, describing the table exactly as your database has it and recorded applied without running, before the save's own file, so a fresh database replays the collection.
  - `nextly migrate:create` describes a Builder collection's columns as the Builder creates them: on MySQL a text field is `TEXT`, as the Builder has always made it, in its table and in its translations table, where a code-first collection's is `varchar(255)`. A project that already ran `migrate:create` on Builder collections gets a one-time migration widening those columns from `varchar(255)` to `TEXT`; `nextly migrate` applies it without asking for `--accept-data-loss`, since a widening deletes nothing.
  - `nextly migrate` and the other commands that ask consent before deleting data no longer ask it for a string column widened: `varchar(n)` to `text` or to a `varchar` at least as long, or the type restated, with no character set, collation or other conversion named, no nullable column made NOT NULL and, on MySQL, the column in its table's default character set. Every narrowing, `text` to `varchar`, a change that makes a nullable column NOT NULL, and any other type change still asks.
  - Where a table an earlier version made holds a column whose type differs from what its field makes now (on MySQL, a short text field stored as `TEXT`), a `<timestamp>_<slug>_convert.sql` converts it before the change. The preview names each conversion, and a save converts no column it was not shown: a save through the API or a plugin passes the confirmed columns as `acknowledgedConversions`, and is otherwise refused with `NEXTLY_SCHEMA_CONVERSION_UNCONFIRMED` (409). A stored value too long for the new type is refused by MySQL, and nothing is applied.
  - A many-to-many relationship's junction table, and a relationship column's foreign key with its `onDelete` and `onUpdate`, are written into the save's file as the Builder has always created them, so a deploy replays them too. Snapshots keep leaving both out, as before, so `migrate:check` reports no drift for them.
  - A save whose statements fail with nothing applied leaves no file and puts the definition back. One that fails part-way (MySQL commits each schema statement), in any table its file changes, keeps its files for `nextly migrate:resolve`, with `NEXTLY_MIGRATION_PARTIALLY_APPLIED`. Where an earlier file of the save applied and a later one then failed, every file and the new definition stay, and `nextly migrate` runs the rest once the cause is fixed.
  - The definition file (`ui-schema.json`) now holds a field's `options` exactly as the registry stores them, such as a relationship's `target`, `relationType`, `onDelete`, `onUpdate` and `junctionTable`, a text's `variant` or a number's `format`, beside `relationTo` and `hasMany`, and a number's storage (`dbType`, `precision`, `scale`). Every key is optional, so every existing file stays valid.
  - On MySQL, a migration that makes a column required needs `--accept-data-loss` on deploy, as any such file `migrate:create` writes does: its statement restates the column, and a server not in strict mode turns the column's NULLs into empty values.
  - A field's name in the definition file may be camelCase (`^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*$`), as the Builder accepts it.
  - On SQLite, `nextly migrate:create` writes a field's type change as a rebuild of its table, as it already does for a nullability change, instead of refusing it.
  - On MySQL, a save that makes a field unique where its column cannot carry a unique index (a `TEXT` column) is refused, as a code-first change is, and nothing is written.

- [#3939](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3939) [`5939d2d`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/5939d2dcfd8fde8f05ad7f7807770590784f2bf4) Thanks [@faisal-rx](https://github.com/faisal-rx)! - In the Schema Builder's outline, a blocks field now shows beneath it each registered block it accepts, named as the page editor names it, with that block's props, read-only and naming the plugin that registered it. An allow-list entry no registered block matches is said beside the field, and the row says when the blocks are still loading, could not be read, or need the Page Builder plugin. The Page Builder serves this from a new read, `POST /plugins/@nextlyhq/plugin-page-builder/blocks/accepted` with a field's allow-list in the body (a POST that changes nothing, since the list need not fit in a URL), open to any signed-in user and answering code-defined block metadata only. `@nextlyhq/blocks-engine` now exports `slotAdmits`, its one reading of a block allow-list, which the blocks field's validator now uses too; `@nextlyhq/builder/ops` offers `fieldLabel` and `propLabel` (experimental).

- [#3893](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3893) [`f39a908`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/f39a908e12c623bb28062178cdb7574f54608057) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - The SEO plugin's start-up catch-up records every page even while pages are deleted or made as it lists them: the listing of each type's pages now goes by id, so nothing moves an unread page behind it, and a page deleted after it was listed claims nothing.

- [#3825](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3825) [`d055874`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/d0558746a45d0d54f2a02f8ad5a10a5b059b09a6) Thanks [@faisal-rx](https://github.com/faisal-rx)! - Collection events (`collection.<slug>.created`, `.updated` and `.deleted`) now arrive when the write commits, before its `afterCreate` / `afterUpdate` / `afterDelete` hooks rather than after them: a listener that relied on the after-hooks having run should do that work in an `after*` hook instead. A write made inside a caller's transaction (`createEntryInTransaction`, `updateEntryInTransaction`, `deleteEntryInTransaction`), and each entry of `createEntries`, `updateEntries` and `deleteEntries`, now sends its collection event too: once the outermost transaction commits, after the after-hooks it runs inside that transaction, and never if the transaction rolls back.

- [#3634](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3634) [`d7b9565`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/d7b9565e6b093d2cc4eaf0f4a597a19902cfdedb) Thanks [@faisal-rx](https://github.com/faisal-rx)! - The admin component map now holds every collection view, and the admin no longer imports plugin modules by name at run time.
  - `nextly generate:types` and `--check` list the components a collection names for its own screens: its `Edit` and `List` views, and what is drawn before and after its list table and edit form. A plugin's collections and the site's own are both covered, and so does the development check that rewrites an out-of-date map, so it keeps them.
  - The admin's run-time `import()` of a plugin's admin module is removed. In a bundled admin it could not resolve a package by name, so a component missing from the map now draws its fallback, and `next dev` names it.
  - `registerKnownPlugin` is deprecated, and removed at the next major release after two minor releases. It still registers what it's given, now straight away, and says once that it is deprecated. Register components with `registerComponents` in your plugin's admin module instead. The plugin template and the first-party plugins now do.
  - The generated map now registers through `registerComponentMap` (experimental, from `@nextlyhq/admin`). It registers like `registerComponents`, then tells the admin nothing more is on its way, so a plugin's document action or panel section whose component is missing draws its fallback instead of Loading. Rerun `nextly generate:types`: a map generated before this keeps working, but a component missing from it shows Loading instead of the fallback.

- [#3803](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3803) [`231978f`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/231978faabcdc368c26a52dba7846e6e26710892) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - Search engines and AI crawlers now read each page's whole head in the first HTML they are sent.
  - `nextly/next` exports `nextlyHtmlLimitedBots`, for a Next config's `htmlLimitedBots`. It is Next.js's own list plus the main Googlebot and the AI crawlers and answer engines, such as GPTBot, ClaudeBot and PerplexityBot. Next.js streams a page's metadata to everyone else, after the head.
  - A new app's `next.config` sets it, and `withNextly()` sets it where the app sets no list of its own.
  - An app made earlier adds two lines to its `next.config`:

    ```ts
    import { nextlyHtmlLimitedBots } from "nextly/next";
    // in the config:
    htmlLimitedBots: nextlyHtmlLimitedBots,
    ```

- [#3924](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3924) [`c4d8dba`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/c4d8dba8e64b797453c95ab3fc00dbbc3bfc3a17) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Add widget is one list you can search. The drawer opens with focus in its search, then lists every widget you may add once, each with its icon, name, the plugin it comes from, one line about it, and Add. A one-card widget already on your dashboard says "On dashboard", and a widget that reads a collection says "Needs a collection you can read" when you may read none. The Suggested row, the Removed group, the filter chips and the step that asked for a collection are gone: Add puts the card at the end with its defaults and keeps the drawer open, a card that reads a collection starts on the first one no card of that widget uses yet, and Add on a one-card widget you removed puts that card back as it was. When every collection already has its card, the new card's settings open, and it is kept only once something tells it apart from the card it matches. The layout write refuses a card that reads a collection from a reader who may read none. The widget previews page is no longer served by the admin, on a development server or in production; its accessibility check of every widget's preview cases runs from a page of the end-to-end test app, and `@nextlyhq/admin/testing` exports the board it draws (`WidgetPreviewBoard`, experimental). Each core widget names an icon for the list.

- [#3849](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3849) [`6fb7e80`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/6fb7e80bc5f47f34c2ef923434a966c13da8586a) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Dashboard cards are as tall as their content, at rest and in Customize: no card is drawn at a fixed number of rows, nothing inside a card is cut off, and the cards that share a row are drawn as tall as the tallest of them. A chart over time is taller on a wider card. While a card reloads it keeps the height it was last drawn at, so the cards below it stay put. The card menu no longer offers a Height. - [#3943](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3943) [`ee53364`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/ee533648cd968fc9dabb124224804e8e6c41c86e) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - System health on the dashboard can now copy a diagnostics report. "Copy diagnostics", at the card's foot and in its Details drawer, copies a plain-text report ready for an issue or a chat: the Nextly, Node, Next.js and React versions, the environment, the database and whether its connection is encrypted (yes, no or unknown), migrations, storage, email, background jobs, each plugin with its version, how many collections, Singles, users and locales the site has, and how many server errors this server process answered in the last 24 hours. The report is built on the server from a fixed list of facts, so it never holds a password, key, token, connection string, host name, email address, person's name, entry content or environment variable's value. Details shows exactly what is copied. If the browser refuses the clipboard, Details opens with the report selected to copy by hand. Only super-admins can build the report (`GET /api/dashboard/diagnostics`).

- [#3902](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3902) [`fb0ee45`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/fb0ee45245e5fbe18daa2abb219a884345f6822d) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The dashboard's Count card reads well at any number. It shows what it counts, the number written whole ("12,480", never "12.5k"), and one line under it: by default the change this week ("+3 this week", "No change this week"). In its settings, "Count" chooses all entries, the published ones or the drafts, and "Under the number" chooses the change this week, a trend line over the last 8 weeks, a status split, or nothing. Every line counts what the number counts, so a Drafts card's change counts only drafts, and the status split is offered only with all entries. A reader who may read users can also set a Count card to Users, to count the people on the site; a reader who may not is never offered Users, and the server refuses a card set to it. Recent entries rows no longer start with a letter square: each row leads with its title and shows its status as a quiet chip with a dot. Upcoming releases keeps its date chip.

- [#3965](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3965) [`2fba917`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/2fba91717eeaa208e4a6eb25e250bf9734953b7f) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A final pass over the dashboard at phone, tablet, laptop and desktop widths, in light and dark. The settings drawer's short choices (Width, Number of entries, Row spacing) are one bordered row with the chosen option filled, and the Title field's hint reads "Leave empty to use the name shown." Team cuts a long role name short, with the whole name on hover, so the person's name keeps its room. A note's links are drawn in the text's own colour, underlined. In System health's Details, the report keeps phrases such as "24 h" and "3 locales (en, es, ar)" on one line where it wraps, without changing the text it copies, and a toast said while Details is open stands above its footer instead of over the Copy diagnostics button.

- [#3925](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3925) [`4ae9dcd`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/4ae9dcd7b87002490bd1cb260614ef0879da4958) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - System health on the dashboard now answers a developer's first questions. Under one status line ("Everything is working", or how many problems need attention and things to check), it shows the Nextly version and whether it is the newest in its release channel (or "Couldn't check for updates" when the registry cannot be reached), the environment, the database and its response time, whether the database connection is encrypted, migrations, storage, the email provider and background jobs. Details opens a drawer with the Node, Next.js and React versions and each plugin's version.

  Whether the connection is encrypted is read from the database session itself (PostgreSQL's `pg_stat_ssl`, MySQL's `Ssl_cipher`), not from configuration; once the session has answered, the site's own connection decides, so behind a connection pooler a plain session over the site's TLS connection counts as encrypted, and an encrypted pooler session over the site's plain connection does not. In production, an unencrypted connection to a database on another machine is a problem on the card and in Needs your attention, with a "How to fix" link to the new Encrypted connections page; a connection whose encryption could not be read is a warning, never treated as encrypted. The database adapters gain `inspectConnection()`, which answers this without throwing. System health's default width is now half the dashboard.

- [#3901](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3901) [`9a18e1a`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/9a18e1a00972f410dba323a28c722294c8edce81) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The dashboard's Team card lists the people on the project instead of two count tiles: each person's name, email, role and when they were last active, most recently active first. A role filter in the card's header, "All roles" by default, narrows the list and is also a setting, beside "Number of people" (5, 10 or 20) and "Show last active". The footer holds Invite, for a reader who may add people, and "View all (N)" when there are more people than the card shows, or "All users" when it shows them all. The card is now offered to every reader who may read users, not only to those who may also add or change them, and the server reads only the fields the card draws, filtered, ordered and cut in the database. Last active is the later of a person's newest session renewal and newest sign-in.

  change nothing. It opens the database read-only, takes no schema lock, asks

    appends anything to `nextly.config.ts`; it used to append the snippet and
    then be refused.
  - `nextly migrate` stopped because a migration file changed after its

- [#3878](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3878) [`ecdb521`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/ecdb521af5ec9abe4dbe008e4d632c9110e1576c) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - A site declares how each language's address is formed, under a prefix or on a domain of its own (`languageAddresses` in `nextly.config.ts`), and `languageAddressOf(path, locale)` answers the address a page kept in a language is opened at. Content and Single routes, the blocks routes included, placed under a `[locale]` segment read the language from it: one route serves every language, a segment naming none of the site's languages answers not found, and the addresses a route hands on are formed by the rule.
