Grouping, filtering and order stay keyed by the plugin, and a plugin no longer installed keeps its package name.

- [#3863](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3863) [`7aec2f7`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/7aec2f7a39787cc12b978d1192119b45d74c2cf3) Thanks [@faisal-rx](https://github.com/faisal-rx)! - The Builder's lists of collections, Singles and field groups now say what is true. A plugin's entries are listed under that plugin by name, folded by default and read-only (no selection, no delete), instead of among the site's own or as "Unknown". Each entry names its source: "Defined in code", "Made in the Builder", "Built in" or the plugin's name. The column reporting whether a schema is applied is called "Schema" and draws attention only when something is not applied. "View entries" opens the collection's entries; "Generate Types", which only promised a later feature, is gone; a code-defined entry offers no delete rather than a disabled one. Each field group shows how many fields use it.

  The list endpoints for collections, Singles and field groups accept `owner=site` or `owner=plugins`, applied in the query so a page and its count describe the same rows; without it they list everything, as before. The admin's plugin metadata names a plugin's collections, Singles and field groups by the slugs a host's rename registered them under. The field-group list now reads a 1-based `page` as well as `offset`, so its second page is no longer its first.

- [#3969](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3969) [`19b15aa`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/19b15aa488c6fb9ab90760c1dc5630fe248dc3d9) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Every running server copy now serves a schema change within a few seconds, with no restart. Each copy reads the database's stored schema version at most once every 2 seconds (one indexed read, shared by every request arriving meanwhile, and none while no requests arrive) and, when it moved, loads its collection, Single and field group definitions again from the registry, so a field added in the Schema Builder on one copy is written and read on every other. The first read after a start loads them once more, since the start's own load cannot be dated against the version.

  The `X-Nextly-Schema-Version` header now carries that stored version, one number for every copy, rather than a count kept by each process. `bumpSchemaVersion` (from `nextly/runtime`) keeps its signature and now asks the next request to read the stored version at once; it returns the version served until then. A registry write in this process does the same by itself.

  The admin's metadata reads (the collection, Single and field group lists, and collection and Single schemas) answer with an `ETag` that is a hash of the body sent, and answer `304 Not Modified` with no body to a request whose `If-None-Match` holds it: only when an ordinary request would receive the same bytes. `If-None-Match: *` is not honoured, and the startup request answers every part in full. Every admin API response to a signed-in request (one with a session cookie or an `Authorization` header) is now marked `private, no-store` and varies on the credentials, whatever its route asked for, so no shared cache keeps it.

- [#3915](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3915) [`73e415d`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/73e415dbf1ab9471c2c31e064339f76de9968573) Thanks [@faisal-rx](https://github.com/faisal-rx)! - A field group's editor in the Schema Builder now says which collections, Singles and field groups use it, each linked to its own editor, and that a change there reaches all of them; it says so when that cannot be read, rather than showing nothing. In the outline, a field that uses a field group shows how many places use it. The answer comes from a new read, `GET /api/field-groups/<slug>/used-by`, which lists each field that places the field group with the collection, Single or field group holding it; like reading the field group itself, it needs a signed-in user and no specific permission. The field-group list's use count is now the length of that same list.

- [#3799](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3799) [`f803856`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/f803856db7d6612f20bfb8ff611b45d9cb8ad25f) Thanks [@faisal-rx](https://github.com/faisal-rx)! - Field groups nest inside each other to any depth, and a field group placed inside itself is refused where it is written. The three-level limit `defineConfig()` enforced at start is lifted, so a configuration nesting deeper now starts. A field group placed inside itself, directly or through other field groups (including through a group, a repeater or a list of allowed field groups), is refused by `defineConfig()`, by the start when the cycle takes in a field group defined in code, and by every Schema Builder save, naming the field groups in the cycle. A cycle among Schema Builder field groups saved before this change does not stop a start: the start and CLI commands that load the configuration name it in a warning, and the next save of any field group in it is refused until one stops placing the next. Text values nested in field groups are sanitized at every depth, where they were reached only three field groups deep, and deleting a collection or Single removes its field-group rows at every depth.

  Text inside a group without a name is now sanitized like any other text. Before, a text or textarea field placed in such a group was stored with its HTML intact, while the same field outside the group was stripped.

  `MAX_FIELD_GROUP_NESTING_DEPTH` stays exported with its old value and is deprecated: nothing enforces it any more.

- [#3866](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3866) [`afa0ac6`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/afa0ac62dfbc78d28c599c14de601d92a2b6839e) Thanks [@faisal-rx](https://github.com/faisal-rx)! - A field group placed directly in another field group's fields is now stored, read and removed at every depth. Its values were refused before, with "not stored", and the admin left the field out of the form. Each level is a row of its own field group's table, pointing at the row of the instance that holds it. It is validated by its own rules, a required one is required, passwords in it are hashed, its fields' read and write rules apply, its translated values are kept per language, version restores and media usage include it, and deleting or clearing an instance removes everything placed in it. The Builder's form draws it, and the configuration no longer warns about it.

  A filter path that goes past a field group's own fields (`hero.cta.label`) is refused as a field that cannot be filtered on. It used to be read as a column named after the whole path, which answered with the wrong rows.

  A plugin's write to a field-group row nested more than eight levels deep now still expires its document's cached reads. Removing a field-group instance, or deleting the collection or Single holding it, also removes rows that a field group stopped placing in it after they were stored.

  A required field inside a group without a name is now enforced; a save that leaves it empty, accepted before, is refused. Existing entries with that field empty must fill it on their next save, as for any required field.

- [#3986](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3986) [`829113b`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/829113bbb362eb4c406c4e7168924c935a91c299) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - The entry's fields a surface draws beside a field that takes the form over (`useEntryFieldsPanel`) now leave out the fields a plugin's tab takes over, as the edit page's own content does. Such a field was drawn twice: in its tab and in the surface's panel.

- [#3984](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3984) [`7947190`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/79471906498aeb19feaf129a48f90393ff21b727) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A database's first `nextly migrate` on this release writes a registry record once, naming the newest applied app migration or the point before any, decided from the database and the migrations folder alone so a run that stopped part-way is finished by the next. Where no migration's snapshot carries the registry metadata, it applies the pending migrations, then writes the registry rows from the configuration it runs with (saying how many), adds the permissions and sets the preset grants, and writes the record with those rows and the live permissions kept as the registry baseline, all in one transaction. Where a pending migration carries the metadata, the record and the baseline (the registry as it stands) commit just before it applies. Where an applied one already carries it, the rows from its snapshot, the permissions, the grants and the record commit in one transaction before anything applies. Once the record exists, the rows come only from the migrations. A pending migration written by an earlier release's `migrate:create` is refused, naming it, when it comes after one that carries the metadata or after the record.
  A `migrate:create` for a configuration declaring no collection, Single or field group now records that it declares none, so its migration applies after the registry record instead of being refused.

- [#3850](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3850) [`5b2fba4`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/5b2fba42b28605fb2e1be4a5a371014c57e3aceb) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - The page builder's font catalogue no longer leaves its popularity read running when a daily refresh of the font list fails: the editor is answered with the last good catalogue once both reads have finished.

- [#3846](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3846) [`5ba640d`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/5ba640d4735b0866127881b4a9acdd20aaed4f76) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The Form Builder adds a field through the shared field picker (search, then a label that names the field) and edits it in the shared settings panel, docked beside the list on a wide window and opened in the field's card on a narrow one. The panel is configured for forms: a dropdown's and radio group's choices, a checkbox as one yes or no, the form's own settings for text areas, files, dates, numbers and hidden fields, only the validation rules a form's checks enforce, and the form's own show-or-hide conditions. A saved field's type is shown fixed, with the reason. Every setting a form stores is kept through an edit, and Move up, Move down, drag, Duplicate and the refusal to delete a referenced field are unchanged. `AddFieldDialog` and `FieldEditor` are no longer exported from `@nextlyhq/plugin-form-builder/admin`: they were the builder's own parts, and the shared `FieldPicker` and `FieldSettingsPanel` from `@nextlyhq/plugin-sdk/admin` replace them.

- [#3900](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3900) [`cdebd5d`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/cdebd5d818d8a5da4fb9c73a2d56569cc15c4220) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The form editor now sits in the admin's frame, with one bar and one header.
  - **Its controls are in the admin's top bar**, after the breadcrumb: the form's status as a menu (Live, Closed or Draft), the save state with Undo, the number of submissions (a link to the form's Submissions), More (Copy form ID, Delete form) and Save.
  - **The header** shows the form's name, its field count and API path, and a tab for each page: Builder, Preview, Settings, Notifications and Submissions.
  - **Each page has its own address** under the form's edit address (`/admin/collections/forms/<id>/settings`, and so on), so a reload or a shared link opens the same page. The edit address opens Builder.
  - **One save for the whole form.** Changes on every page are held together, counted in the bar, can be undone one at a time, and are saved once. Moving between pages keeps them, and leaving the form with any asks first. A refused save keeps them and says what to fix, with a link to the page that holds it.
  - **The Forms panel starts folded** on the form editor; the bar's toggle brings it back.
  - The editor's own heading, the name, slug and status box, and the footer are gone. The name and the form ID are edited in Settings, which also holds the closed message once the form is closed.
  - A new form, once created, stays open in the editor at its own address instead of returning to the list.

  For plugin authors (`@experimental`): a collection's custom edit view can have pages of its own. Declare a document view on the collection whose `component` is the edit view itself; the admin draws the edit view at that address, passes the page's path as the new `view` prop of `CustomEditViewProps`, and keeps it mounted while the address moves between its pages. A custom edit view can now also report unsaved work with `useReportUnsavedWork`, and the admin asks before leaving the document while it holds any.

- [#3865](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3865) [`f5623d0`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/f5623d0cd1bbef2382ab0d0e28d1713ae70f11fd) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Form Builder notifications are queued through the queued email send once a submission is saved, instead of being sent once: the first attempt is made at once, and a failure a retry can help is tried again through the job queue until it is sent or fails for good, so a provider outage no longer loses a form's emails. Every notification setting is kept (provider, sender, static or field recipients, cc, bcc, reply-to, condition, template, attachments), the `form-builder.beforeEmail` filter still runs once before queueing, and each email carries its own idempotency key, from its submission, its place and its notification. Retries need the jobs trigger (`POST /admin/api/jobs/run`) to run. A queued email that fails for good is now logged with its reason (`queued-email-failed`, with its `queuedId`), so the Form Builder's own failure line can be matched to why.

- [#3957](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3957) [`f513799`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/f513799537a07ab7b5e11406df098a2bea85e6c8) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Form bot checks are verified on the server. A form's bot check (Site default, Off, Google reCAPTCHA v3 or the new Cloudflare Turnstile) sends its token inside `data` as `g-recaptcha-response` or `cf-turnstile-response`, and the token is checked with the provider before the submission is accepted, wherever it is written. Keys go in the plugin's `spamProtection.recaptcha` / `spamProtection.turnstile` options, which are validated at start.
  - A token that fails, or a missing one, stores the submission flagged as spam.
  - A provider that cannot be reached leaves it unchecked, and logs a warning.
  - A form whose check has no secret key keeps accepting submissions unchecked, with a start-up warning and a note in Settings. Settings no longer lets a check without keys be newly chosen.
  - Settings shows the plugin's rate limit, read-only.
  - The public form read gives a visitor's form `botCheck: { provider, siteKey, field }` to render the widget with.

  Forms saved before keep their protection. The previously unused `recaptcha` option of `checkSpam`'s config is deprecated, and `SpamCheckResult.reason` gains `"turnstile"`.

- [#3933](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3933) [`1deea1e`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/1deea1ea763341aa38f29e7ceca36d95e3019cf8) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A form can close by itself on a date, or once it has a number of submissions. Both are set in Settings › Availability. Past either, a submission is refused with the form's closed message, the one it gives when closed by hand, and `GET /api/forms/:slug` answers as for a closed form. Spam does not count towards the limit. Submissions racing for the last place cannot take more than there are: the limit is held inside the transaction that stores a submission, whatever stores it.

- [#3930](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3930) [`7d2d330`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/7d2d330958b317b2016ddaaf10cfb769e3f89ecd) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A form's notification rules, which name the addresses each submission is emailed to, are no longer returned to visitors by the public form endpoints (`GET /api/forms` and `GET /api/forms/:slug`) or to staff who can only read forms. Staff who can update forms and super-admins still read them, and submissions still send every notification. The form's internal note follows the same rule, and super-admins now read it too.

- [#3911](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3911) [`1e170ad`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/1e170add06db61e473aba37360480b72ac5c98e6) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The form builder's fields are one outline, with the selected field's settings docked at the window's edge.
  - **One row per field**: its label, its type and stored name, and badges for what you would otherwise open it to see (Required, a width other than full, "Shown if…" with the fields its condition reads, and its default, by the choice's label).
  - **The settings panel docks** as a column against the window's right edge, as tall as the window, from 1024px wide; below that it opens under the row.
  - **Add a field where it belongs**: from the toolbar, from "Add here" between two rows, or with "/" on a row, which adds it below.
  - **A saved field's name is fixed**, with the reason, as its type already was: its answers are stored under it.
  - A rename finished after visiting another page of the form still moves what refers to the field (conditions, notifications), even when the name was cleared on the way.
  - Every submission's own stored values (submitted at, status, notes, IP address and browser) are named under the list.

  For plugin authors: `FieldCards`' `onAddField` callback gains an optional third argument, the place in the list a field was asked for; `generateFieldName` now lives in its own module and is still exported from the same place.

- [#3992](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3992) [`ebeda5c`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/ebeda5c23bfc7999545f6ff9c0d9fb89d585af01) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Settings offers one response per email address, comparing a chosen Email field that must be required and not hidden by a condition. The builder will not delete that field, make it optional or give it a condition while it is chosen, saying why each time, and an Email field can be chosen from its own panel. Saving a form through any door is refused when its one response per email has no such field. A field renamed before it is saved keeps the choice.

- [#3970](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3970) [`393e5d7`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/393e5d796ccea9666862779236f3d0e5f8c51f0f) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Forms can take one response per browser. The form's script keeps a random token in the visitor's browser and sends it as the `nextly-browser-token` answer; the server keys it with the plugin's keyed digest, never stores the token, and refuses a second response from the same browser atomically. The public read of a form that compares browsers names the answer to send the token in (`oneResponse`). A submission without a token is accepted unchecked, with a warning. Settings offers "One per browser".

- [#3946](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3946) [`4253d8e`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/4253d8e68665c02bd89e1f514219a44f1cfd656c) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - One response per person is held by the database. A form that takes one response per network (IP address), or per email address with a chosen Email field (compared ignoring case), stores a keyed one-way digest beside each non-spam submission, never a second copy of the address. A unique index on the form and the digest refuses a second submission with the same value, even when several arrive at once. The digest is made by the plugin wherever a submission is written, and is never taken from the caller. A form that allowed one submission per IP before this change still refuses a network that submitted then.

  Existing installations receive the new `responseKey` column and its unique index on the submissions collection through their own migrations: run `nextly migrate:create` and then `nextly migrate` (or `nextly db:sync` in development).

- [#3972](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3972) [`5ee5f16`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/5ee5f16d6bf0542978090c7b9747a518859c32ea) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Changing a form's one-response setting now counts its earlier submissions. Keys carry the form's one-response version, which a change of mode or Email field moves on, so earlier keys stop matching at once. A form with up to `oneResponse.keysInSave` submissions (default 200) gets keys for the new version inside the save; a larger one is finished by a sweep (`form-builder:one-response-keys`), and until then a new submission is compared with the earlier ones directly. The earliest of several with one value keeps it, and when the holder is deleted, marked spam or edited, the next earliest takes it. A key made for a version the form has since left is refused where it is stored. The form editor saves on through a revision moved on only by the plugin's own record that keys are made.

- [#3916](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3916) [`5f01c0a`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/5f01c0a4865644c8a7bf398d0394b833828ad2cb) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A form's Preview runs the form as a visitor meets it.
  - **The site's own checks**: a submission in the preview is refused for exactly what the site refuses (a malformed email address, a length or number limit, a required answer left empty), checked over the fields a visitor sees, with the reason under each field.
  - **Show hidden fields** shows hidden fields and fields a condition hides, each saying why it is hidden.
  - **Desktop and Phone** widths, and **Reset**, in the preview's toolbar.
  - Submitting shows what the visitor would see next (the message, or where they would be sent), and saves and sends nothing, as the note under the preview says.

  **Fix:** a submission is no longer refused for leaving empty a required field that a condition hides. The field was never on the visitor's page, so such a form could not be sent at all. Only the fields a visitor is shown are checked; what is stored is unchanged. The site and the preview decide which fields a condition hides with one shared function.

- [#3997](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3997) [`0cf934d`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/0cf934d7519fa4b6e22887fd37fc95ef936713e7) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A form can stop keeping the IP address and browser of new submissions (Settings › Privacy › Store IP address and browser). One per network still works on such a form, by the keyed digest made before the address is dropped, and the builder's note on what every submission stores says what the form keeps.

- [#3927](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3927) [`561d6fd`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/561d6fd0d5765bfd1150928cd4ee3d7fe3a144c4) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Form settings are one page in sections: Form, After someone submits, Availability, One response per person and Spam protection. The form ID is fixed once the form has been live, a form can carry an internal note that only people who manage forms can read, and the closed message is always at hand in Availability. Settings now stores `oneResponse` and `botCheck` in place of `allowMultipleSubmissions` and `captchaEnabled`; forms saved with the old keys read as before, and the old keys are still accepted. The per-form reCAPTCHA site key is no longer offered, since a key works only with the site-wide secret.

- [#3872](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3872) [`a72f5c1`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/a72f5c13b71d14fec10df9690eeb16b991ffb160) Thanks [@faisal-rx](https://github.com/faisal-rx)! - `nextly migrate` checks each pending file's renames before the run's first statement: a file that renames a column or a table onto one that is already there, while the one it renames still is, is refused, naming the file, the table and both names, and nothing of the run is applied. - [#3887](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3887) [`49a15e7`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/49a15e7013d295a3514c70beba7636767d34a67e) Thanks [@aqib-rx](https://github.com/aqib-rx)! - `nextly migrate` now writes the registry rows of collections, Singles and field groups from the migrations, under the schema lock, after its migrations apply. Each row is brought to the newest applied snapshot that records every entity's declaration, whether the entity is defined in code, in the Schema Builder or by a plugin, and a row that already matches is not written. A field added in code therefore reaches the registry when `nextly migrate` ends, before any start. Rows of entities that snapshot does not record, and fields the running configuration lacks, are left as they are; a run whose later migration fails still writes the rows of the ones that applied. A snapshot written before declarations were recorded is read as saying nothing, so it rewrites no row. The development boot keeps inserting only missing rows, since its start keeps them in step with the code.

  A field group whose label, description or admin options alone change now has that change written, as collections and Singles already did; a description or admin block the declaration no longer has is cleared.

- [#3876](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3876) [`1369c15`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/1369c15b8dc8fe1d54b8d76742bb61af7e6f0c20) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - Making a field required, or renaming one, on MySQL now migrates with the right checks. `nextly migrate:create` writes these changes as a prepared statement built from the live column, and `nextly migrate` used to read that as a statement that could delete anything: it refused unless you passed a blanket `--accept-data-loss`, and it never checked for rows with no value before making the column required. `nextly migrate` now reads the prepared statement as the change it makes. A rename needs no consent. Making a column required asks consent for that column only (`--accept-data-loss=<table>.<column>`), and is refused before anything runs while any row holds no value in it.

- [#3391](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3391) [`1d32a40`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/1d32a401f0550762b978f5eef95ad245f56095f9) Thanks [@aqib-rx](https://github.com/aqib-rx)! - `nextly migrate` and every other migration command now ignore the `.sql` files an earlier Schema Builder wrote into your migrations folder, where `nextly migrate` used to refuse them, or, at a development start, apply them as written.

  A file is ignored only when it carries the whole signature the Builder left: a name like `1730000000000_create_posts.sql` (13 digits, then `create`, `update`, `i18n`, `status` or `drop`, then the entity's name), no snapshot beside it in `meta/`, none of the lines `migrate:create` writes (`-- UP`, `-- DOWN`, `-- Collections:` and the other entity headers), and statements that change only that entity's own tables, or its own registry row. Such a file is never applied, listed, counted or compared, and its ledger rows play no part in any check.
  - `nextly migrate`, the boot migrate step, `nextly migrate --dry-run`, `migrate:check` and `migrate:status` name each ignored file with "ignored: written by an earlier Schema Builder". It is information: the exit code is what it would be without the file. `migrate:status --json` lists them in a new `ignoredOldBuilderFiles` field and writes the line to standard error, so standard output holds only the document.
  - A delete the Builder wrote for several collections, `<13 digits>_drop_<N>_collections_<hash>.sql`, is ignored only when every statement is a `DROP TABLE` of a Builder collection's table; the same holds for a single collection's, a field group's and the user-field table's drop files.
  - The first `nextly migrate` of this release records, for each ignored file a ledger row names, that the row is an old Builder file's, with the file's checksum. A file edited later within the signature has its new checksum recorded.
  - If such a marked file later stops carrying the signature, every command refuses before changing anything: with exit code 2 (`MIGRATION_TAMPERED`) where its content changed, or with the new code `OLD_BUILDER_FILE_SNAPSHOT_ADDED` where a snapshot now stands beside it. Put the file back, remove the snapshot, delete the file, or accept it with `nextly migrate:resolve --applied <file>`, which withdraws the record.
  - A file with the Builder's name and no snapshot that does not carry the rest of the signature, for example one that changes another collection's table or a table nothing declares, is still refused, with `BUILDER_MIGRATION_SNAPSHOT_MISSING`: the refusal now names the part of the signature it lacks, and the fix is to replace it with the migration `nextly migrate:create` writes, or to delete it.

  **Before upgrading:**
  - Keep the old Builder files in your migrations folder until the first `nextly migrate` of this release has run: that run records which ledger rows are theirs. You can delete them after it.
  - `nextly migrate --dry-run` or `nextly migrate:check` names any file with a Builder name that is not recognised as an earlier Builder's, with the part of the signature it lacks. Without a snapshot it is refused, as before; replace it with the migration `nextly migrate:create` writes, or delete it.

  They keep working unchanged, with the same props, until they are removed. The deprecation is in the published type declarations, so an editor marks each use; nothing is logged at run time.

- [#3948](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3948) [`1a076cb`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/1a076cbaa53ffa744e7d47d663721b97017f8449) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - Turning on `experimental.perLanguageStorage` no longer stops `nextly db:sync` or `next dev` to ask consent for deleting a translatable field's main-table column: its values move to the default language first, so nothing is deleted. - [#3870](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3870) [`3dbf39d`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/3dbf39d7287f7089aed7dacb0f64dcbf2049a2e5) Thanks [@faisal-rx](https://github.com/faisal-rx)! - Plugins can emit durable events: `ctx.events.emitDurable(name, payload, { tx }?)` records an event the plugin declares `durable: true` in `contributes.events` with the work that emits it, by the same rule as `emit` (the plugin's transaction, else the one the calling code is in, else one of its own), and `ctx.events.onDurable(name, subscriber, handler)` subscribes under a name unique within the plugin. Every subscriber registered when an event is dispatched receives it at least once, retried with backoff across restarts, on the `events:dispatch` job, and promptly after the emitting work commits inside a request (one dispatch at a time per process, never delaying the response). `DurableEvent`, `DurableHandler` and `PluginDurableEvents` (the type of the two methods; `PluginEvents` is unchanged, and `ctx.events` is both) are exported from `@nextlyhq/plugin-sdk`. A hand-written `PluginContext` double (a test mock or a wrapper) adds `emitDurable` and `onDurable` to its `events`, for example as `vi.fn()`, as it added `ctx.security` and `ctx.dialect` when they came. Experimental.

- [#3994](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3994) [`81789d0`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/81789d07693f0ce67408a72f16bca98ca04651c3) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Plugins can forget the email they sent about something they deleted: `ctx.services.email.forgetSends({ queuedIds, idempotencyKeys }, { tx })` (`@experimental`) cancels the plugin's own queued emails among the ids that are still waiting or retryable, clears the message and recipients of each, and erases the delivery records of the sends that carried the keys, in the caller's transaction when it passes one. `ForgetSendsInput` is exported from `@nextlyhq/plugin-sdk`.

- [#3822](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3822) [`2116214`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/211621483291750d79de653df7e98365e18a8789) Thanks [@faisal-rx](https://github.com/faisal-rx)! - `ctx.events.emit` now delivers a plugin's event once the work that emitted it commits. Pass `{ tx }`, the handle `ctx.db.transaction` gives, to tie an event to that transaction: it is delivered when the transaction commits and never if it rolls back. An event emitted inside a transaction the calling code is running in waits for the outermost commit; one emitted inside a savepoint that rolls back, or in an attempt that is retried, is dropped. Outside any transaction, as from a job or a route, it is delivered at once, as before. **Behaviour change:** before, `emit` delivered at once even inside a transaction that later rolled back; a listener now hears such an event only after the commit. `ctx.events` is typed `PluginEvents` (the event bus's methods, with this `emit`), exported from `@nextlyhq/plugin-sdk` with `PluginEmitOptions`. A value typed `EventBus` no longer accepts `ctx.events` as it is; type it `PluginEvents`.

- [#3802](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3802) [`2f58ae8`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/2f58ae826fc55a8d64d94c1889dd41eab31cbc61) Thanks [@faisal-rx](https://github.com/faisal-rx)! - A plugin field type can declare its own settings, and the Schema Builder's settings panel draws them for every field of the type. Each setting is a text box, a number, a switch or a choice, declared in `contributes.fieldTypes[].settings` with a `key`, a `label`, an optional `help` line and the tab it belongs in. Settings declared for General come first there, as the settings that make a field that type. Each value is kept in the field's `pluginOptions` under its key, which the Builder already saves and loads, so stored fields need no change.

  A malformed list now refuses boot with a configuration error naming the plugin, the field type and the setting: a choice with no options or the same value twice, a key used twice, a key that is not one name, or the reserved keys `type` and `name`.

  `PluginFieldTypeSetting` and `PluginFieldTypeSettingBase` are new, `@experimental`, exported from `@nextlyhq/plugin-sdk` and `nextly/field-catalog`, and `PluginFieldType` gains an optional `settings`. Nothing existing changes.

- [#3938](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3938) [`21eb915`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/21eb915465c7ed663cdc3bb820aa7a64933f0ae6) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Plugins get `ctx.security.digests` (`@experimental`): `digest(purpose, value)` returns a keyed one-way digest (HMAC-SHA256) of a value a plugin compares without keeping it, such as an email or IP address. Each plugin has its own random key, made once and kept in `nextly_meta` sealed under `NEXTLY_SECRET`. A secret rotation seals the same key again at the next start, so digests stored before the rotation keep matching once the previous secret is removed. The `KeyedDigests` type is exported from `@nextlyhq/plugin-sdk`.

- [#3974](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3974) [`2a9e051`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/2a9e051796d0c6cc902a8f0c860418ba1ab84d14) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A standalone plugin can name the page its rail item opens with `admin.landing`, one of its own pages or collections, and a site can override it in `admin.pluginOverrides`. Without one, the rail item now opens the first collection its panel lists for the reader, skipping a hidden or unreadable one, and with none, the first menu item its panel lists. A landing naming anything else is ignored, and a development start warns about it and about a standalone plugin with menu items but no collections and no landing.

- [#3786](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3786) [`109351a`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/109351a5ac920d88f353d363dac4e5c00cc4fe7f) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - A plugin's tab on an edit page can now work with the document (experimental).
  - A tab at `collection.edit` or `single.edit` receives `DocumentTabProps`: the place's `context` and `entry`, the document form's `control`, and the `documentLock` a side panel section is told. This holds on a saved entry, a new one and a Single. A tab reads what the author has typed and not yet saved, and what it writes through `control` is stored by the bar's Save and Publish with everything else.
  - Every contributed tab receives `setBadge`, which shows a count beside the tab's label (`PlaceTabBadge`: a count, what it means in words, and an optional `"attention"` tone), or none with `null`. The count is read out with the label, and a count past 99 is drawn as "99+".
  - A contributed tab stays mounted while another tab is open, so what it holds is kept and its count stays current.
  - The edit pages keep the open tab in the address as `?tab=<id>`, so a reload or a shared link opens it again. Switching tabs replaces the history entry, and the unsaved-changes warning no longer asks when only the tab changes.
  - `PlaceTabProps`, `PlaceTabBadge` and `DocumentTabProps` are exported from `@nextlyhq/plugin-sdk/admin`.

- [#3908](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3908) [`b7a1d39`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/b7a1d394054f00bb929f8da8ffb24cf8168651d1) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - Plugins can answer a request before its page is served, or add headers to every page, prerendered ones included. A site wires its Proxy once, `export const proxy = createNextlyProxy(nextlyConfig)` from `nextly/runtime` in `proxy.ts`, and each plugin contributes handlers under `contributes.proxy`; a handler may answer with a response such as a redirect, set headers on what is served, or pass headers on to the page's render. A handler that throws is logged and passed over, so the site keeps serving.

- [#3871](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3871) [`0fec834`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/0fec834fabf7f06d0677a06d915c8b0ff01125de) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - `withNextly()` rewrites `/robots.txt`, `/sitemap.xml` and `/llms.txt` to the API handler, so a plugin route mounted at the root answers them at the site root. The site's own files, routes and rewrites still win. A second argument names more root files, or a handler mounted somewhere other than `/admin/api`.

- [#3602](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3602) [`51307f8`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/51307f8748c380563c211d8a5860e7cb786135ae) Thanks [@faisal-rx](https://github.com/faisal-rx)! - A plugin can claim each webhook it receives once, with `ctx.security.webhooks.claimDelivery(verified, { provider })`: once per plugin, provider and delivery id (or body, for a scheme with no id). A retry or replay of a processed delivery is answered `duplicate`, for the 30 days its record is kept, which is how long a timestamp-less scheme is safe from replay. In the plugin's transaction (`tx`) the claim commits or rolls back with its writes; without one it is a lease (5 minutes by default, `leaseSeconds`) the handler ends with `complete()` or `release()`, and a retry during it is `in-progress`, so a handler that fails never loses the delivery. Only the answer `verify` returned is accepted. Claims live in a new core table, `nextly_received_webhooks`, which `nextly migrate` adds to an existing database; no payload is stored, and claims are pruned on the retention runner and the scheduled drain. Experimental.

- [#3777](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3777) [`a871f4e`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/a871f4e14505383383024c0d6d49416dc89c881a) Thanks [@faisal-rx](https://github.com/faisal-rx)! - Core now dispatches durable plugin events: a built-in `events:dispatch` job, run with the other jobs, fans each recorded event out into one delivery per durable subscriber registered at that moment, then runs each delivery until its handler succeeds, retrying failures with the jobs runner's backoff across restarts. Two dispatchers at once still make one delivery per event and subscriber. A delivery whose subscriber is no longer registered is held for it, never given to another, and looked at again every quarter of an hour; one that runs out of attempts (10) is kept as failed. A failure is kept with any credential in it taken out. Subscribing comes in a later release. Experimental.

- [#3781](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3781) [`0247d05`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/0247d05807b907f3f194d0d13e8b7c6d6afa770d) Thanks [@faisal-rx](https://github.com/faisal-rx)! - Durable plugin events can now be inspected and settled. `nextly events report` lists every delivery that needs an operator: held for a subscriber that is not registered, or out of attempts. `nextly events abandon <delivery>` or `--subscriber <key>` gives deliveries up, keeping their attempts and last failure; `--dry-run` names them first. The dispatcher warns in its log when a subscriber's deliveries become stuck, and again at most once an hour while they stay so. A delivery whose subscriber is not registered is now marked `held`, and keeps its last failure; it runs again as soon as its subscriber is registered. Finished events are removed 30 days after their last delivery settles, with their deliveries, by the retention passes and the scheduled drain; an event with a delivery still owed is never removed. Experimental.

- [#3796](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3796) [`6ccfea1`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/6ccfea16b48e63b5636ea77935a2cfeca76ed185) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - A plugin can now expire the cached pages built from its own data. `ctx.cache.tag(part)` names the tag a read of the plugin's settings or other data carries, and `ctx.cache.expire(...parts)` clears every cached read carrying it, on every instance that shares the database, as a content write does for content. A plugin names and expires only its own tags (`nextly:@plugin:{plugin}:{part}`), never a collection's, a Single's or another plugin's. `pluginCacheTag` from `@nextlyhq/plugin-sdk` spells the same tag for code outside the plugin's context. Both are `@experimental`.

- [#3852](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3852) [`90816a2`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/90816a2047977406512d5d6c83415f83f2bd3b9c) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - A plugin that keeps a record of who holds each public address can take part in keeping every address to one page, through `ctx.publicAddresses`. Nextly asks every participant inside each save whether another page holds an address the saved document now holds, and refuses the save with `DUPLICATE`, naming both pages, if one does. A plugin that moves addresses itself asks the same way with `move`, and `held` and `fingerprint` let a participant catch its record up at start. Nextly keeps no record of its own, and a site with no participant does no address work. Experimental.

- [#3976](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3976) [`11d4a59`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/11d4a59995eb669a6f546fa3b8a169453a821e26) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - `nextly migrate` now records the Nextly release that set the preset roles' grants (Admin, Editor, Author, Viewer), keeping the newest, and writes that record in one transaction with every preset role's grants, so a run that stops part-way leaves all of them and the record as they were. A `nextly migrate` from a release older than the recorded one adds and removes no preset grant and says which release set them; the rest of its run is unchanged. This covers releases from this one on: moving a site to an older release that carries it leaves the preset grants as the newest release set them, while a release from before it reads no record and sets the grants to its own presets. A preset role that cannot be created or set now leaves every preset role's grants unchanged, with a warning, rather than setting the others. Starts still set the preset grants as before and neither read nor write the record.

- [#3884](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3884) [`71dee01`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/71dee01451c4dae0515205994bb4ad48e1fdd97c) Thanks [@aqib-rx](https://github.com/aqib-rx)! - `nextly repair-columns --apply` converts each column whose stored values all convert exactly, and records each repair. It takes the schema lock (waiting about 60 seconds for another schema change, then stopping with exit 1 and naming what holds it), classes every column again from the rows it holds now, and converts the safe ones towards their field as last migrated. A column that is pending a migration, owned by a plugin, blocked or lossy is left unchanged and reported with its reason, and one column's failure stops neither the others nor the report.

  On PostgreSQL and SQLite each column converts with its record in one transaction, judged again after its table is closed, so it is converted whole or left exactly as it was. On MySQL each statement runs in strict mode and states how it runs while others use the table (`ALGORITHM` and `LOCK`), so MySQL refuses a change it cannot run as the report said; a conversion of several steps records its progress, and the next `--apply` finishes it from the step the live column has reached, which a dry run also reports. A conversion waits about 5 seconds for a table another session is using, then leaves the column as it was and reports it as unavailable, locked. Repairs are kept in a new `nextly_column_repairs` table, which only the first `--apply` that converts a column creates.

  turns the builder off, as before.

An upgraded site keeps every value its `seo` group holds; on a translated content type the group's values become the default language's. - [#3942](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3942) [`d29d853`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/d29d8532ed7187de3637bb8f3317f026f5c2d252) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A fresh admin tab now asks for what every screen needs in one request, and sends it before anything else.

  **How it works.** The admin sends `GET /admin/api/startup?path=…` with up to 16 of its own read paths: the session, setup status, admin metadata, the workspace, the person and their permissions and capabilities, General settings, and the menu's collections and Singles. The server answers each part exactly as a request to that path would. Each part goes through the same security checks, rate limits, route and permission checks, and comes back with its own status, so a part the person may not read keeps its own refusal. The screens take their data from that answer instead of each asking on its own, so a fresh tab waits through fewer round trips before it has data.

  **Fewer reads of an entry.** An entry's edit page now waits for its collection's schema before reading the entry, so it reads the entry twice instead of four times.

  **Other callers.** The separate endpoints are unchanged.

- [#3790](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3790) [`130edf5`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/130edf59d9e30dd1a33b0b14667c63d486995caf) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - The admin is served as not listable by search engines, with or without a plugin that manages search.
  - `nextly/config` exports `adminMetadata` (and the `ADMIN_ROBOTS` value it carries). New apps' `app/admin/[[...params]]/layout.tsx` exports it as the layout's Next.js `metadata`, which puts `<meta name="robots" content="noindex, nofollow">` in the head of the first HTML the server sends.
  - An app made by an earlier release keeps working: the admin adds the same tag to the head in the browser where the page has none, so a crawler that runs the page still reads it. To have it in the first HTML too, add two lines to your admin layout:

    ```tsx
    import { adminMetadata } from "nextly/config";
    export const metadata = adminMetadata;
    ```

  - A robots tag the page already has is left as it is, so no admin page carries two.

- [#3899](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3899) [`1525ac6`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/1525ac66d8f42cd92b47284ef4d25a1beb6775a7) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The admin page is now prebuilt: the same page for every visitor, built with the app and served at once, even while the server is still starting Nextly.

  Before, the admin was rendered for each request and marked `private, no-store`. Now it is served from the build with headers a CDN or the browser may keep. Nothing about the person is in the page, and it reads nothing from the database. Everything about them still comes from the admin's own requests once it loads.

  The logo, name and favicon set in `admin.branding` are written into the page, so they show from the first paint with no swap after it loads. The favicon's link is in the first HTML. Branding set only in General settings still arrives with the admin's first requests.

  Nextly's cache handler now serves the pages `next build` prerendered. Before, it kept entries only in memory, so a new server process (every cold start) found none of them and rendered every prerendered page again on its first request. Now a miss is answered from the build's files, which are judged by the same tag expiries as any other entry, so a write made since the build still expires them. Every app using `nextly/cache-handler` gets this.

  New apps get this from `create-nextly-app`. To update an existing app's `app/admin/[[...params]]/layout.tsx`:
  - export `metadata = adminMetadataFor(config.admin?.branding)`, which replaces `adminMetadata`;
  - add `generateStaticParams` returning `[{ params: [] }]`;
  - render the branding element from `adminBrandingJson`, all three from `nextly/config`;
  - move any per-request work into development-only code, as the installation guide shows.

  A layout that keeps a request-time `connection()` around the admin keeps working, but is rendered for each request as before.

- [#3858](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3858) [`a61207a`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/a61207afef5fe9dfaa06757200deb02cd7c85eef) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The server no longer waits for Nextly to start before it answers requests.

  `createRegister(config)` in `instrumentation.ts` now begins Nextly's start and returns at once. Before, Next.js served nothing, not even the admin page or a static file, until the whole start had finished, which took over a minute against a database far from the server. Pages that need no database are now served straight away while Nextly starts.

  Anything that needs the database waits for that one start instead of beginning another. That covers Nextly's own routes, the health route, `getNextly`, `getCachedNextly`, the `nextly` object and the content routes. Whichever starts Nextly first (the start-up hook, a request or the Direct API), the others now join the same start, so the permission and role seeding and the email templates no longer run twice when a request arrives while the hook's start is still running. A start that fails is logged, and the next request that needs the database starts Nextly again.

  What to check in an existing app: code that calls `requireNextly()` (from `nextly/runtime`) synchronously in a request can now run while Nextly is still starting, and it throws until the start has finished, as it always has when nothing had started. `await getNextly({ config })` or `await getCachedNextly()` first, or use the `nextly` object, which waits. `shutdownNextly()` now waits for a start still under way before it shuts Nextly down.

- [#3937](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3937) [`43b11cb`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/43b11cb0cc5fb718ce41aa2ed451f82255b7718a) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The site's Proxy (`createNextlyProxy`) no longer holds a request while Nextly starts. The save writer refused every such field as "cannot enforce uniqueness on a text column", judging its value by the main table's rule, though the value lives in the per-language table, where each language's uniqueness is an index MySQL can create. Shared fields are judged as before.

- [#3829](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3829) [`1a48295`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/1a482956abb877f9387fe3cb5a933e36255b1b6c) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - A translated field a plugin holds back from a type switched off keeps its values when the type stops being translated: in development, they go back to the type's own table with its other translated values, so switching the field on again brings them back instead of an empty column.

- [#3582](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3582) [`a5db931`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/a5db931030953be9419caa0423d9d7dca4819493) Thanks [@zeshan-rx](https://github.com/zeshan-rx)! - Under `experimental.perLanguageStorage`, every remaining path that asked whether an entity is translated where it meant "where are its values stored" now follows where they are stored. An untranslated collection, Single or component keeps its translatable values in its per-language table everywhere: Schema Builder saves and the translation toggle, the dev build and reloads, `migrate:create`, boot, restoring a version, column repair, previews, version history, publishing, and plugin fields extended onto Builder entities.

  Turning translation on for an entity on such a site adds a per-language publish state, seeded from the entry's state in every language. Turning it off removes that state, and is refused with a conflict while any language's publish state differs from its entry's.

  With the setting off, nothing changes.

- [#3954](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3954) [`900a3b0`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/900a3b0a914cc2c3214e952ccb2b7a080b3bf65a) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - `nextly upgrade` now tells running instances when it converts roles holding a retired `manage-` permission, so they stop answering from the old grants straight away. It no longer logs "Emptying the retired stored permission answers failed ... Service \"adapter\" is not registered".

- [#3880](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3880) [`9478102`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/9478102ce084529954d81cbc1c9fd645576f2b39) Thanks [@faisal-rx](https://github.com/faisal-rx)! - User fields keep the values they are given, whichever database stores them.
  - On PostgreSQL, a user's date fields are read at the instant they were written. They were read as plain timestamps, so a database whose sessions run outside UTC handed each one back shifted by its offset. The table's own `created_at` and `updated_at` were read the same way.
  - On SQLite, a multi-select user field (`select` with `hasMany`) is stored. It was declared as plain text, so writing a list failed, and creating that user went ahead with every custom field left out.
  - New PostgreSQL user number columns are `DOUBLE PRECISION`, as collections' numbers are and as MySQL and SQLite already store them; `REAL` rounded past seven significant digits (1234567.89 read back as 1234567.9). An existing `REAL` column is left as it is and keeps being read and written as before; `nextly repair-columns` reports it as differing.
  - A user field's value that its column cannot take now fails the create or update that sends it. Before, any failed write of the custom fields went ahead without them and turned them off until the next start; that now happens only where the user fields' table does not exist yet. On PostgreSQL and MySQL, a URL, email, select or radio value longer than its 255-character column is refused as a validation error naming the field, as a text with a length already was.

- [#3853](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3853) [`1a8b228`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/1a8b22817852a04d74401193f2f08e215ac3d2a9) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - User custom fields are added through the shared field picker (search, then a label that names the field) and edited in the shared settings panel, configured for user fields: a dropdown's and radio group's choices, a checkbox as one yes or no, a default typed as text for URL, phone and plugin types, only the bounds a user field stores, no conditions, and the name, type and a dropdown's "several choices" shown fixed once the field exists, with the reason. Before a new field is created its type can still be changed. The pages keep their own save, the reserved-name and choice checks, the Active switch and the list's reordering. The shared settings panel gains two surface options, `widthSetting: false` and `pluginSettings: false`, for a surface that stores no width or no plugin settings, so neither is offered there; a choice field's default can be cleared with "No default"; and the field picker can start its label step with a field's current label (`initialLabel`).

- [#3962](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3962) [`bcf98d3`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/bcf98d3642760f48d0f935ef44a9bf6a8673caf0) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - The dashboard widget card draws its load-error icon in the danger status text colour, which stays readable on every page surface, instead of the solid fill colour.

- [#3815](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3815) [`d5675fb`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/d5675fbd1369e9bdf5c2f11b25202e7f4b0bee31) Thanks [@zeshan-rx](https://github.com/zeshan-rx)! - Changing a workflow in code no longer strands a document. A stage can record the name it had with `renamedFrom`: the next deploy moves documents still in the old name to the new one, records the move in each document's history, and keeps their approvals when the rename was the only change. A stage listed in `removedStages` has its documents moved where the definition says, recorded, with their approvals withdrawn. A stage removed with nowhere named leaves its documents where they are: they read as the first stage, `nextly workflow:stranded` lists them ("Stage 'legal' no longer exists"), and the `_strandedStage: true` list filter keeps them, so a count and its list agree. `nextly workflow:move-stranded --to <stage> --as <email> --comment "…" [--collection <slug>]` moves them to a stage of the workflow, recording one event per document with that person and the comment; it refuses an unknown or deactivated person, a stage the workflow lacks or one that allows publishing. A deploy that detaches a workflow from a collection or Single removes its review state and the versions held for review, all or nothing, recorded per document, so attaching it again revives no approval. Deleting a document removes its review state in the same delete, by every delete path, and discarding a working draft closes that part's review, recorded in its history. A definition is refused when a `renamedFrom` names a stage it still has, is claimed by two stages, or is also listed in `removedStages`. A part with no review state now stands where its content puts it: a part never published starts at the first stage, so attaching a workflow to a collection with documents starts each unpublished part there; a working draft over a live part starts at the workflow's `afterPublish` stage, also after an earlier draft was discarded; and a live part with nothing unpublished has no stage, so a step or an assignment on it is refused with `WORKFLOW_NOTHING_TO_REVIEW`. A part recorded in a stage the workflow no longer has reads as the first stage.
