## 0.0.2-alpha.74

### Patch Changes

- [#3728](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3728) [`0beb16e`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/0beb16e016c0ef99b6b2970adc4b6fee96722e3d) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A page binding that follows a relation into the media library, such as an image's alt text bound to `featuredImage.altText`, now shows that media item's field. The page's read-ahead reads the item through the media library, as the page's images are read, where before it asked for `media` as a collection, failed the read and showed the fallback. `BindingSourcesArgs` in `@nextlyhq/blocks-react/next` gains an optional `media` reader; without one, such a binding still shows its fallback.

- [#3616](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3616) [`0dc0951`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/0dc0951b44906061585d5b4676bf00e6cf689503) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A block gets a "Show when" group in its Content tab, under "Visible on": one group of conditions, each a field, an operator and a value, edited as a list's filters are. Only fields visitors can see are offered. A block inside a collection list checks the list's item, and every other block the entry the page shows. A condition the page can't check says so, since visitors then never see the block, and groups set through the API are shown as they read, with a way to keep the first. The page actions API gains `set-conditions`, which sets or removes a block's conditions with the same checks as the editor's save.

- [#3312](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3312) [`23e8831`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/23e8831661c55852b5d1173c69966be58ed78861) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A blocks field inside a field group was saved without the composition checks
  the same field gets on the page itself. The field group's write had no access
  to the component library, so a page could place a component past the depth
  limit through a field group and have it stored. A field group's blocks field is
  now judged with the write it belongs to, on that write's connection, for a
  collection entry and a single alike, repeatable field groups included.

  Locks in such a field are measured against the blocks a slot starts with
  alone. A field group's value has no stored copy of its own to compare with,
  and reading one by the page's id and the field's name would read the page's
  own field of the same name. So a stored
  field-group value whose `"contentOnly"` child kept an older value (an earlier
  default, say) is refused on its next save. Put that child back as the block
  now starts, and the save goes through.

- [#3333](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3333) [`9c6c948`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/9c6c9483806569b9759cd746ca3955ffd072a42e) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A blocks field inside a named group (`hero.body`) can be saved again when the page
  already stores a `"contentOnly"` value or a placement break it keeps. Its stored value
  was refused as "not a top-level field", which failed the save. A plugin field
  validator's `write.readStored` now reads a field inside named groups by its path.

- [#3583](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3583) [`369155b`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/369155bed9d7d65301b46a99b980b79cd91d99c2) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Block visibility conditions now have a closed operator vocabulary and an evaluator in the blocks engine. A condition uses `equals`, `not_equals`, `contains`, `not_contains`, `greater_than`, `less_than`, `exists`, `not_exists`, `is_true` or `is_false` on one field of the entry, or of the list item for a block inside a list. The older spellings `eq`, `ne`, `neq`, `gt` and `lt` are read as the operators they name, and `canonicalConditions` rewrites them for storage. `evaluateConditions` decides whether a block is shown. It reads only the fields the public may read, and it hides and reports any condition it cannot check: an unknown operator or field, a protected field, or a value of the wrong type. Saving a page now refuses an unknown operator, and, when the schema is known, a field that is missing or protected and an operator or value that does not fit the field. A problem the stored page already held is reported as a warning, so existing pages stay savable. The renderer still leaves every conditioned block out of the page until it starts asking the evaluator.

- [#3643](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3643) [`550f90d`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/550f90d2d397364a3d8915a3557bc4f77184a69c) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The page builder's "Visitors won't see this" mark now also covers a bound path into a related collection the public may read none of, such as `author.email` where `users` has no public field. Before, the canvas showed the author's value with no mark, while the published page showed the fallback. A badge near the canvas's left edge now stays wholly in view, as one near the right edge already did.

- [#3823](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3823) [`07cb43b`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/07cb43bcb0f11d319be7ba059e36810082fa775c) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - The count of what removing a breakpoint would drop no longer asks a second time for saved page titles after that read has run out of time. On a busy server its timer could fire a moment before the clock reached the deadline, so the locked-blocks list started a second read of the same titles after the first had been given up on.

- [#3563](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3563) [`82e2e22`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/82e2e22f96e6fa1e7048b1872b40049acb2f454f) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Settings no longer reports a breakpoint removal as done when it could not read the removal's status: it reads it again and keeps following the removal until it can. A removal found opened again at its end keeps being followed. The removal Settings makes at once (nothing was stored under the breakpoint) can no longer be cancelled once its save is out. An open Site tab now notices, within about ten seconds, a removal started from another tab, and holds editing the breakpoints while it runs.

- [#3566](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3566) [`f2d2cfb`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/f2d2cfb0299d297b4dc4401164b87fe5aa4b464d) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A confirmed breakpoint removal now keeps what it takes out of the site, so it can be undone: every stored value it strips (a page's live row or working draft, a component, a pattern, a Layout, an entry) has a row in the page builder's new `breakpoint_removal_fragments` table holding the styles and hides it lost, written before the strip itself, and the shared styles have one for what the set's write took out of them. A strip whose row cannot be written is not made. Rows are deleted by the removal job 30 days after they were kept. Existing installs apply the new table with `nextly migrate` before deploying (the page builder's schema version is now 6).

- [#3610](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3610) [`72007d1`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/72007d14062f746545633ae88ea34c27c223a6d8) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - An undo of a breakpoint removal now leaves the removal's claims on its breakpoints in place until its own set has been stored, so an undo refused by another save no longer lets pages the removal left (a pending draft) bring those breakpoints back early. An undo whose write cannot be confirmed stays preparing until its recorded set is seen stored, and is never walked unverified. What an undo could not put back counts each value once, however often the removal stripped it, and the values of a code-supplied shared style removed from the code since are reported as gone with it rather than as put back.

- [#3651](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3651) [`1f93392`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/1f933920eef1a0d548822859223e85b2908035bb) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Saving a document now checks its bindings against the declared fields of what they read, and refuses a binding to a prop the block does not have, a field the source does not have, a field whose type does not fit the prop, an invalid format or an invalid fallback. A binding a schema change broke after the document was saved is kept, so the document still saves. `nextly/runtime` gains `declaredFieldShapes` and `@nextlyhq/blocks-engine` gains `bindingSchemaIssues`, both experimental.

- [#3416](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3416) [`bdd9024`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/bdd9024c3b42ffd656002414322851831061f0e4) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The inspector names three more choices the way an author thinks of them. A
  button's "type" is now "Acts as", and it is offered only while the button has
  no link, to a URL a page can follow or to an entry, since a link is then what
  the button does. A component can still expose it, for pages that clear the
  link. A container's tag is now
  "HTML tag", each option named in words ("Generic box", "Main content") with
  the tag itself shown muted beside it, and the row is hidden where a block has
  only one tag to offer, unless what is stored is another one. A component
  field exposing a choice now offers it in the block's words too, read through
  `optionLabel`, which `@nextlyhq/blocks-engine` now exports. "Visible on" draws its three devices as separate
  toggles with a dot on the device being edited.

- [#3738](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3738) [`7d50d9d`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/7d50d9d5f1e3d1674e8a11be108c49d22ab5377d) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A public route answering a read the public is refused (an entry, a list or a Single it may not read) from the cache no longer fails to prerender under Cache Components with an error about reading the current time. `cachedFind` keeps the refusal and throws it again on every read of the entry; it now rebuilds that `NextlyError` without reading the clock. Its `timestamp` is the time the refusal was first made, kept with the cached entry, so logging or serializing the error reads no clock either, and its stack shows where it was thrown again. The thrown error is otherwise the same: its class, code, status, messages and data are unchanged. Cached refusals are now filed under a new key, so entries cached by an earlier version are read afresh once.

- [#3743](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3743) [`2ca423d`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/2ca423dc3ba092ae8187aabfc1e5fbebb5810449) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A library image chosen as an image binding's Fallback is named readably: the library button sits inside the chosen file's box, and a long file name in that row is cut in its middle with its extension kept. On the picker's tiles a name keeps its start and is cut at its end. The picker's search reads "Find an image, or paste an address".

- [#3406](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3406) [`ac6ba5e`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/ac6ba5e45eb83fe3a1d9874294e793c651dba21e) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - On a page the site serves, a click on the site's own page around the canvas, such as below a short page, now clears the selection, as a click on the canvas's own background does. The site's layout decides how tall the canvas is there, so the canvas can end at its last block, and the click an author makes below it to let go of a block used to do nothing.

- [#3551](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3551) [`7b7e00f`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/7b7e00ffe681fd6b1d3ca63fceafe2e4e6586bdf) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A collection list can now filter, sort and window its entries, and show a related list. Filter rows (is, is not, more or less than, contains, any of, none of, has a value) narrow the entries, several sort keys order them with empty values last and ties in a stable order, and a limit of 1 to 100 and an offset skip and cut them. A list can show a to-many relation of the page's entry or of the outer list's item, in the order the relation stores them unless a sort is set; a sorted relation of more than 100 entries is read in parts and kept in the database's order. A date filter compares whole days in the site's time zone, inside a component too. When nothing matches, or the read fails, the list draws its own empty state, and an author previewing a draft is told why. Saving refuses an out-of-range limit or offset, a filter or sort on a field the collection lacks or visitors cannot see, a filter on a field holding several values, a filter whose operator or value its field's kind does not take (an order on text, a day on a number), and a related list nested more than one level deep. The page actions API gains `set-list-query`, judged by the same checks. A list stored before this renders as it did; one whose sort names a removed or hidden field lists in id order. In the Page Builder, the block is now named Collection list (its stored type stays `core/collection-loop`, so saved pages are unchanged), and its Content tab edits all of this: Source (a collection, or the page entry's or each outer item's related entries), Filters as one sentence per row that opens into its field, operator and value, Sort rows with a drag handle, Alt+↑ and Alt+↓ and each direction in words (Newest first, A–Z, Highest first), Number of items and Skip the first, and Canvas shows: Entries or When empty. Under Number of items the selected list says how many entries match and how many show ("4 entries match, so 3 show."), taken from the list's own read on the canvas. Only fields visitors can see are offered. The canvas draws each list with the entries a visitor would see, in the language being edited and within a published page's read allowance, tags a list showing its empty state, and says when its sort fell back or its read failed; a fallen-back sort's note has a Choose a field button that takes the author to the sort. A save's refusal names the collection as authors read it ("which Posts doesn't have"). Layers shows a list's Each entry and When empty regions.

- [#3576](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3576) [`0473854`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/04738540f028b90223c98c627dff0f2446598656) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - A collection list's query is now judged at save exactly as the page draws it and the editor offers it.
  - A list inside another list's "When empty" state shows the related entries of the item around that list, never of an entry the outer list did not find. The editor's Source menu offers the same.
  - A list of "this entry's" related entries is refused on a Single, whose page has no entry, and the editor says so.
  - A list's fields are judged in the language being saved, and the editor offers the fields visitors can see in the language being edited.
  - A filter or sort on a field the editor never offers is refused: a time of day, rich text or media, or a sort on a related entry.
  - A filter on a number field compares with a number, on every operator.
  - A list inside a placed component is judged as the page composes it, so a placement's value or variant cannot give it a sort or filter no list takes, or one on a field visitors can't see.
  - A component save is refused when it would break a list on a page placing it, such as by aiming a page's value at the list's sort. The server log names each page.
  - A list sorts by at most 20 fields, in at most 2,000 characters (`LIST_MAX_SORT_KEYS` and `LIST_MAX_SORT_LENGTH` in `@nextlyhq/blocks-engine`). The save, the canvas's read of a list's entries and the editor's Add sort all hold it to that.

  Pages already stored keep saving: a problem a stored page already had stays a warning.

- [#3605](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3605) [`0b82117`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/0b82117221f837790cd005f1fa151dff85ea2551) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - A collection list is judged the same way in the editor and at save in more cases, and a Layout's header no longer has its badge drawn over its links.
  - The editor gives a list's fields the kind a save gives them, so it refuses a sort on a time of day and takes a filter on a field type a plugin adds, as the save does.
  - A component's list of "this entry's" related entries is judged by its shape when the component is saved, since the entries are those of the pages placing it. Before, the save judged it against the component store and refused a list that works on those pages.
  - A save no longer refuses a list problem when the stored page can't be read, or when the stored page's components can only be composed in part: the problem may be one the page already had. The server log says when a placed component's list problem was kept this way.
  - Checking a page's lists reads the fields of no more lists than the check visits.
  - On the canvas, a Layout region's lock sits outside the region, below a header and above a footer, so it never covers the region's content. Hover or focus shows "Header · from Layout"; a click, Enter or Space opens the tag with Edit Layout beside it. The lock is the region's one focus stop. Escape, a click elsewhere or a new selection closes the tag. Where outside has no room on screen, the lock is drawn inside, and at 100% it stays in the part of the canvas on screen.

- [#3202](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3202) [`a95deda`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/a95dedaa544e306b85bc97afe69a045468932796) Thanks [@zeshan-rx](https://github.com/zeshan-rx)! - A Schema Builder save of a collection now changes the database in development through the same schema apply as the schema dialog, under the schema lock. What changes for a save:
  - **The lock.** A save while `nextly migrate`, `db:sync`, a rename or another schema change holds the schema lock is refused with nothing written. A save that only changes labels or admin options never creates the lock's table where it is missing, since that is itself a schema change. The schema dialog's apply now takes the same lock, so it too is refused, with nothing written, while another schema change or a migration holds it.
  - **The whole database.** The save compares every table the Builder owns with what was recorded for it, as the dialog does. A table changed outside the Builder refuses the save, naming that table and the step that brings it in step.
  - **MySQL failures.** A statement MySQL refuses part-way through a save is reported as `NEXTLY_MIGRATION_APPLY_FAILED` with the database's own message, rather than "The database refused statement N of M of this schema change". MySQL keeps the statements that ran before it; saving again finishes the change from what the database holds. A failed apply from the schema dialog now carries the same code and message rather than a generic error.
  - **Filling a Required field added over existing rows.** The rows get the field's default where it has one, and otherwise its type's empty value, written as a bound value rather than spliced into the statement. A date or date-time field takes the moment of the save, read once for every row, rather than the database's own clock. A plugin field type takes the empty value its plugin declares. The column keeps no default afterwards.
  - **Unique turned off** drops the single-column unique index the field had, including one adopted from an earlier install.
  - **An index name already taken** by another index on the table refuses the save before anything changes, naming that index, rather than leaving the field recorded unique with nothing enforcing it.
  - **SQLite.** A table rebuild a failed save left part-way (a `__new_<table>` beside or instead of the table) is finished or undone before the next save.
  - **MySQL indexes on long text.** An index added to an existing table on a TEXT column is keyed by its first 191 characters, as a new table's indexes already were, so MySQL accepts it. This applies to the schema dialog and to `migrate:create` files too.
  - **Many-to-many junctions on MySQL** are created with their indexes inside the one `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`, so a junction lands whole and a save retried after a part-way failure passes over it. Names are unchanged.
  - **A column added outside the Builder** is no longer dropped when a save adds a field it could be mistaken for: the save is refused instead.
  - **Schema version.** A save moves the collection's schema version on, so a schema dialog open beside it sees the change.

  Production is unchanged: a save writes the migration file and runs nothing. On SQLite, that file still does not make a field leaving translation NOT NULL when it is Required or Unique, although the database in development does. A save's migration file stays one combined file with no localization intent header, so history inference and `nextly migrate`'s header-keyed checks don't read it.

- [#3317](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3317) [`72f9277`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/72f9277fa29e48b6a6ba5312741340a72e0fa5de) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The page builder refuses unpublishing a component that a Layout uses, as it already refused deleting one, and the refusal names the Layout. Unpublishing it would take it off every page drawn inside that Layout.

- [#3606](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3606) [`b13a66d`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/b13a66dc888c5d37f49db0b52e56c42cc851308c) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A component delete's rewrite now asks the person who started it only for what their own save would need. Each copy is written as that person, under every rule their update meets (update access to the entry or Single, the field's update rules, and the publish permission where the write publishes), and what the write expects to find is judged as the system that read it. A starter who may update a page but not read it, or whose field read rule closes the blocks field to them, no longer has the rewrite refused or stopped; one who may not update it is still refused.

  The rewrite also no longer saves a page's live content as a draft when the author discards the draft while the page is being read: the page is read again and written as it now stands. The same holds when the draft is published and a new one saved between the two reads: the row's version is compared across them.

  `updateIfUnchanged` (`@experimental`) takes a new identity, `{ caller, checkedBy: { overrideAccess: true } }` (`PluginSystemCheckedWrite`, in `PluginConditionalWriteIdentity`), for a write whose expectation the system read: the update is the caller's and the expectation's read is the system's. Made as a caller alone, it still refuses a field they may not read, so nobody learns whether a value they supplied matches one.

  A person's conditional write is now refused with `FORBIDDEN`, writing nothing, when what it would persist, after every hook, does not hold each field it writes exactly as sent, or the field-access pass took one out (a field update rule refusing it, or a hook changing or putting back its value). An ordinary update drops such a field silently and writes the rest, so a conditional write could have been reported as made while its field never changed. A component delete's rewrite reports such a document as not permitted.

- [#3260](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3260) [`f48b906`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/f48b90635bb9efb60cba355bd16fe3db08974d47) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A designer exposes a component's fields in the component's own Page Builder
  view.

  Each property of a block inside the component has an "Expose to placements"
  switch and a name, and each block a "Let placements hide this" switch. With
  nothing selected, the inspector lists the component's exposed fields and slots
  to rename or remove. A removal asks first, naming every variant that loses a
  value. A property placements could not set, or one inside an area locked to its
  content, is refused with the reason.

  The engine gains an `envelope` op, so an exposure edit is one undo step like any
  other edit. `BuilderOp` (published by `@nextlyhq/blocks-engine` and re-exported by
  `@nextlyhq/builder`) gains this fifth member: code that builds or applies ops is
  unaffected, and an exhaustive `switch` over `op.kind` needs a case for
  `"envelope"` or a default. A new field's id stays clear of every id the component's live
  definition still uses or has retired, read from a new `/component-facts`
  route, which also counts the documents that place the component directly.

A removed field's id is retired and never minted again. Its value is pruned from every variant in the same edit, and a type change gets a new id. A design prop inside a `contentOnly` area is refused when it is exposed. `stripRetiredExposures` takes a removed field's values and a removed slot's content out of any document that places the component. A variant left with no values is now a warning (`variant-empty`) rather than an error, and shows the component's defaults.

- [#3241](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3241) [`d252df1`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/d252df1462adaac2daae1b699fb0004b74999b51) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Page builder: a component save that narrows an exposed slot's allowed blocks is refused when a page placing the component already puts an excluded block in that slot, as a page save would refuse it.

- [#3244](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3244) [`ab2ba5d`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/ab2ba5d00fd99fb26c520b76bf416c947f8b8017) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The page builder remembers the fields a component stops exposing. When a component
  definition that drops an exposed field or slot is published, the field's id is
  retired: it is recorded in a plugin-owned table, never minted again, and every later
  write of a page, a Single or another component takes that field's placement values
  out before validation. A component save also drops its own retired fields from its
  `exposed` list, its slots and its variants, so restoring an earlier version cannot

- [#3618](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3618) [`e3f9ea5`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/e3f9ea5475fcdcff7193e94bada5f74efbd59013) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - `updateIfUnchanged` (`@experimental`) now refuses, with `INVALID_INPUT` and before anything is written, data naming a key no update stores: a system column no client writes (`updatedAt`, `createdAt` and the like), a column a schema hook contributed, or a field stored nowhere. A field group or a many-to-many, which an update stores in their own tables, is taken as before. The check runs in the update itself, once its access is judged and before any hook, so a caller who may not update the document is refused alike whatever the data names. A field kept in its own table is taken under its declared name only. An update drops such a key and writes the rest, so the conditional write would have landed in part while reported as made whole. The version (`_rev`) and overwrite (`_overwrite`) keys are still taken.

- [#3511](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3511) [`e099a0f`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/e099a0fd12a5df82ca5f3f2f0e22f6f236a530e5) Thanks [@faisal-rx](https://github.com/faisal-rx)! - A deprecated surface now tells its user once per process, through one notice. `nextly/deprecation-notice` publishes `noticeDeprecation` (experimental): it names what is deprecated and what replaces it, and optionally the release it is removed in, and says each surface once however many copies of the module a bundle carries. The admin's notice for a sign-in challenge view that posts its own answer with `pendingToken` now goes through it, with the same words.

  The published deprecation policy changes: a deprecated `@public` plugin surface now keeps working for at least two minor releases after the one that deprecates it, and is removed only at the next major release after those, rather than after one major version.

- [#3237](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3237) [`1eee856`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/1eee8561aa39b359947188dda9768c1db8531248) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A plugin's document view, the Page Builder among them, now fills the entry page's content area at every width. Below the desktop breakpoint the view was the window's height while the admin keeps its mobile header above the content area, so the view ran 56 px past it and the page scrolled underneath. `PreviewSplit` and `PreviewPanes` take a `fill` prop that hands a full-height screen the content area's height while the preview is closed.

- [#3774](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3774) [`738e6f4`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/738e6f4b7bb15d6012d1374d3f9904c4dc22d58d) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - On Windows, `nextly build --dry-run`, `nextly migrate:create --dry-run` and `nextly migrate:baseline --dry-run` now name the files they would write with forward slashes, such as `src/types/nextly-types.ts`, as every other dry run and every other system already did.

- [#3217](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3217) [`462d94b`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/462d94b24749b369106870fd9a5e7f787c23b555) Thanks [@aqib-rx](https://github.com/aqib-rx)! - Duplicating a group or a repeater in the Schema Builder now gives the copy and every field inside it, at any depth, ids of their own. Before, the fields inside the copy kept the originals' ids. Because the Builder edits, deletes and adds by id, renaming or deleting a field inside the copy also renamed or deleted the original's field, and Save then saved the original with that change, so its existing entries stopped reading that field's values. Adding a field inside an inner container of the copy added it to the original too. The copy is now a field of its own all the way down.

- [#3324](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3324) [`d622214`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/d622214812e9c46c957b78515811090d981bee33) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A plugin field validator inside a field group is handed the write as it was sent, as its own copy: an earlier field group's instance, prepared for storage in place, no longer shows through to a later one's validator, and a Single's publish-all no longer hands it the internal markers of its pending change.

- [#2994](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/2994) [`3780014`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/3780014e53b4dece766a132c330a48fcb306dd6d) Thanks [@zeshan-rx](https://github.com/zeshan-rx)! - A field moving between translated and shared keeps its values when the latest snapshot was written before snapshots recorded which fields are translated. Every snapshot now says that it records them (`translatedFieldsRecorded`), so one with no translated table is no longer mistaken for an older one. For an older snapshot, `nextly migrate:create` reads the translated fields from the localization migration files when they record them. When nothing records them, it refuses a change that could move a field, including a shared field added to a translated entity and turning a whole entity's translation off, names the fields, and writes nothing. The new `nextly migrate:create --record-snapshot` writes a migration that changes nothing, whose snapshot records the translated fields, so the change can go through after it. - [#3534](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3534) [`ea4db68`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/ea4db681aea0088f3f88cd217bf2017819d12e7f) Thanks [@zeshan-rx](https://github.com/zeshan-rx)! - A form submission saved inside a transaction sends its notification email only once that transaction commits.   Collection hooks gain an experimental `afterCommit` on their context: the effect it is handed waits for the outermost transaction the write runs in to commit, is dropped if it rolls back, and runs at once outside a transaction.

A page that newly places a component stored with a condition operator that conditions do not have is refused, naming the component.

- [#3418](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3418) [`256d09f`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/256d09fd0310b013210943bb25622c0b139a4ab6) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A held save of a field-group instance in a document with no languages of its own is judged in the language the save names, as an ordinary save is, rather than in the default.

- [#3499](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3499) [`2177bfa`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/2177bfa1260c1d50bdd518007436c4fa3b0788a5) Thanks [@faisal-rx](https://github.com/faisal-rx)! - An editor holding a document is told when someone else changes it, naming who and when, within one heartbeat and before they save. The document lock's claim and renewal accept the version the editor's copy started from (`_rev`), and answer `changed` when it moved, with the same rules as a refused save: who and when only to a caller who may read the document. With no unsaved edits the editor loads the current version at once; with edits it offers to load the current version, keeping the edits as a recovery point, or to keep editing. Taking a document back after it changed loads the current version before the form unlocks, and keeps the edits recoverable.

- [#3290](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3290) [`db5abc8`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/db5abc88e603e7e51d89e7e21dd4c27249cecc81) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A block locked in Layers now refuses every change to itself and to everything inside it, at the data layer. `applyOp` refuses updating a locked block or a block inside one (renaming included), removing or moving a block out of a locked one, and putting a block into one; changing only a block's lock is always allowed. A blocks field's save now judges the write against the stored document as well: a write through the API or by an agent that changes, moves or removes a block locked in what is stored is refused with the code `layers-lock-changed`, naming the block, unless the same write unlocks it; a locked block, or a block holding one, can't be deleted in the save that unlocks it. A write that sets a blocks field to `null` while the stored page holds a locked block is refused the same way, judged on the data every `before*` hook leaves, on Singles and imports too. A block locked inside a component holds on every page that places it: a placement's value for an exposed field, or its content for an exposed slot, that changes it is refused with the same code, naming the block, while a value the page already stores is kept. In `nextly`, a plugin field type can set `validateEmpty: true` (experimental) to have its `validate` handed a value a write empties (`null` or `""`), which otherwise never reaches it. A translated field whose language store is not ready yet, and a blocks field inside a group or repeater, are saved unjudged and logged. The lock stays a convenience anyone who may edit the page can lift, not a permission. `@nextlyhq/blocks-engine` also exports `layersLockBreak`, `lockedAncestorOf`, `layersLockChanges` and an `ApplyOptions` type whose `layersLocks: "ignore"` is for system transforms (experimental). In the editor, every path refuses a locked block, a block holding one and a block inside one before it acts, and says why in one wording: Layers, the canvas drag and drop, the block toolbar and menus, the keyboard and the inspector, where a block inside a locked one is read-only and its rename is withheld. Layers rows and the block toolbar show "Locked" on a locked block and "Locked by" its name on every block inside it. A block the saved page still holds locked can't be deleted until its unlock is saved, and Delete says to save first. In `@nextlyhq/builder`, `lockBlockingMove` and `lockBlockingDelete` now also answer for a block that holds a locked block or sits inside one, and an editor's `lockRefusalFor` answers for a Layers lock too: its result is now `LockRefusalFacts`, a union of `SlotLockRefusalFacts` and `LayersLockRefusalFacts`, all exported from `@nextlyhq/builder/shell`. A consumer reading `lock`, `holderType` or `code` narrows first with `isLayersLockFacts(facts)`, also exported there: true for a Layers lock (`label`, `relation`, `verb`), false for a slot lock as before. A block inside a locked one can be locked from the inspector, as from a multiple selection.

Turn on **Split into pages** in the list's How many group, or send `paginate: true` with `set-list-query`. `/page/1` redirects permanently to the list's own address, a page past the last or a number spelled any other way is not found, the stored offset applies once before paging, and each page has its own canonical URL and is pre-rendered on a public route within `staticParamsLimit`. At depth 2 or more, a post's related author comes back with its own upload (an avatar, say) as the media object rather than a bare media id, and with its own relationships expanded to the remaining depth, each related entry still judged by its own collection's access and field rules. The list still reads each related collection once per level, whatever the number of entries. An unset to-many relationship still reads as `[]` at the top of a list, as before.

A page past its read limit still renders: a list it could not read draws its empty state, and the server logs one warning naming the page, the limit and the blocks drawn without their data. `QueryBudget` reports what a render read, by kind, for the editor.

An image's loading is now one switch, "Load immediately"; its source is one "Library | URL" choice showing only the chosen side; and its alt text is one "From library | Custom | Decorative" choice, with the library's words shown and a Custom field that grows with its words. Stored values do not change: a loop still stores the slug and the `field` or `-field` sort string, further sort keys are kept as stored, and a stored collection, field or image state that fits no option is still shown as it is.

The editor's query listing and the composition manifest list a group's own row fields, however deep. Each segment is normalised as a one-segment slug is, and an address with an empty part, a `.` or `..` part, a part with nothing left once normalised, and any address naming a reserved path or longer than 255 characters, is refused at save with the reason on the slug, never rewritten. It is an experimental per-collection option, `db: { slugPaths: true }`, which the page builder's Pages collection sets: a rule about the stored value only, with no schema change or migration, so every existing one-segment address is kept and other collections still strip `/`. `previewUrlFromTemplate` takes an experimental `pathFields` option naming the fields whose values are such paths: their slashes are kept and each segment encoded, so a nested page's Preview and address name its real address; every other value is encoded whole, as before. In-transaction hook handlers receive an experimental `transaction` token for the collection service's in-transaction methods, closed once the call settles, and an experimental `transactionKey` that every call on one transaction shares. A page's address follows the host's `pagePreviewPath` where it is set. `@nextlyhq/plugin-sdk` now exports `previewUrlFromTemplate` and `readableTitleText`, both experimental, so a plugin fills a path template and reads a title as the core does.

- [#3647](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3647) [`c29178f`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/c29178f7709f831db5198abb42a98f27ea9d1cde) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - A block page shows the site settings of the Nextly instance its route is given. `createBlocksPage`, `createPublicBlocksPage` and the Single page factories read a page's site name, address, logo and time zone, which its dates and day filters use, through their `nextly` option, as they read its content. One that does not keeps showing the process's registered instance's settings, so a single-site app is unchanged, and the route now warns once per reader, in every environment, that on a process serving several sites these are another site's.

  `nextly` adds `publicSiteSettings()` to the Nextly instance, and `readPublicSiteSettings` from `nextly/runtime` takes an optional instance to read from, with the `PublicSiteSettingsSource` type (all `@experimental`). Given none, it reads the process's registered instance as before.

- [#3635](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3635) [`dd237c9`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/dd237c945994bf9290aa623eba34190df1a592c1) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - A paginated collection list's page links register again: their parts are named `page-link`, `current-page` and `page-gap`, the lowercase slugs every block part must use, so a site using the page builder starts instead of refusing the collection list block at boot.

- [#3731](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3731) [`bd5217e`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/bd5217ea988a36ba4fda185c6994d3902ba5ece8) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Saving a page that holds a paginated list no longer stalls on a database pool of one connection while the site is still claiming its pages' addresses at start: the pages its later pages could fall on are read on the save's own transaction.

Its report of a change or a deletion refreshes only the document it was drawn for, and does not redirect away from the new one or treat the new document's next version as the author's own change: a newer version of the new document replaces its unsaved text as any other version would. The plugin SDK's stability notes now say advisory notices show on collection writes only, not yet on a Single's save.

Double-click the passage on a placement and type; the edit is stored on that placement only, as one undo step, exactly as the placement panel's field writes it. While the canvas has the passage open, the panel's field for it is held, saying it is being edited on the canvas.

- [#3537](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3537) [`6fb1da8`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/6fb1da8565d507874edd8db9346d8442bf7ffc4a) Thanks [@faisal-rx](https://github.com/faisal-rx)! - A plugin can declare webhook event types in `contributes.webhookEvents` (experimental), each in its own namespace. Startup refuses a type outside the namespace, one of core's, one declared twice, or a malformed one. An endpoint may subscribe to a declared type, a subscription is judged against core's and every enabled plugin's types when it is written, and `GET /admin/api/webhooks/event-types` lists them for anyone who may read, create or update webhooks. A plugin cannot yet send an event of its own type.

- [#3298](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3298) [`b370b9b`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/b370b9b14c5f00556e0bf0def23a258aa7585ffb) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A plugin field type can set the experimental `validateEmpty: true` to have its `validate` run when a write empties the field (sets it to `null` or an empty string), judged on the data the write's hooks leave. Without it, an empty value still never reaches `validate`, as before.

- [#3675](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3675) [`2016d1e`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/2016d1e37a6841b5c6464412d5c8f15592242402) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A plugin can find the host content that uses its field type inside a
  transaction it holds: `ctx.services.ownCollections.listHostTypesInTransaction`
  (experimental) answers each collection and Single holding a field of a type
  the plugin registered, at any depth, as `services.collections.listCollections`
  and `services.singles.list` list them. It reads on the transaction's
  connection, so on a pool of one connection it answers where those listings
  would wait for the connection the transaction holds.

- [#3681](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3681) [`145642f`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/145642f7356176196db7d9246702de9ed05242ef) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A plugin can read a collection's record inside a transaction it holds:
  `ctx.services.collections.getCollectionInTransaction` (experimental) answers
  what `getCollection` answers, on the transaction's own connection, so on a pool
  of one connection it answers where `getCollection` would wait for the
  connection the transaction holds. The page builder reads whether a collection
  has a Draft/Published lifecycle with it inside an entry's save and a
  template's publish, so a save in a collection served at a template address no
  longer waits for a second pooled connection.

- [#3666](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3666) [`dc43a78`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/dc43a786d589516ae242930fa86071fe8ad2ae8e) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A plugin can read host content that uses its field type inside a transaction
  it holds: `ctx.services.ownCollections` gains `listHostEntriesInTransaction`,
  `findHostEntryByIdInTransaction` and `getHostSingleInTransaction`
  (experimental). They read a collection or Single the plugin did not declare,
  only when it holds a field of a type the plugin registered, at any depth
  (groups, repeaters, components), decided at each call from the schema as it
  stands. They read as the own in-transaction reads do: on the transaction's
  connection, as the system, past that content's read hooks, with rows locked
  for share or, with `lock: "update"`, for update. Anything else is refused
  before its rows are read.

- [#3232](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3232) [`d44a678`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/d44a6788aa31bb4eb4424c3e76406c1817305ad6) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A plugin can read the collections it declared without the site's read hooks reshaping
  the answer, through `ctx.services.ownCollections` (`@experimental`). The read skips
  every configured read hook (collection `beforeOperation`, `beforeRead` and `afterRead`,
  including `*` globals and the plugin's own, stored hooks, field hooks set in config, and
  the `collections.listQuery` filter). It keeps what a field's type does to make a stored
  value readable. It runs as the system only, offers `listEntries`, `findEntryById`,
  `count` and `group`, and refuses any collection the plugin did not declare, a dependency's
  included, before anything is read. Related rows keep their own collection's hooks. Use
  it for a plugin's own bookkeeping; never return its result to a person.

- [#3659](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3659) [`ca9eaed`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/ca9eaed78e3b0a9b4a1c8fa81049fac68f0c0dca) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A plugin can read its own content inside a transaction it holds:
  `ctx.services.ownCollections` gains `listEntriesInTransaction`,
  `findEntryByIdInTransaction` and `getSingleInTransaction` (experimental).
  They take the token `collections.withTransaction` hands its work, or an
  in-transaction handler's `transaction`, and read on that transaction's own
  connection, so they see its uncommitted writes and no longer wait for a
  second connection on a pool of one. On PostgreSQL and MySQL the rows they
  read are locked for share until the transaction ends; a list's total is not.
  `getSingleInTransaction` reads a Single the plugin declared, past its read
  hooks, and writes nothing. The adapter's `select` takes `forShare`.

- [#3661](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3661) [`1371c6e`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/1371c6edbf33b9c3e2c52d04f56483f4b08d7bf8) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A plugin's reads of its own collection on a transaction it holds (`listEntriesInTransaction`, `findEntryByIdInTransaction`) take `lock: "update"` (experimental) to read their rows for update on PostgreSQL and MySQL, for a read that goes on to write them, so two transactions doing so take turns instead of one being refused.

- [#3695](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3695) [`cf30707`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/cf3070798c96cb9e66e0d96acff4b7e53872d210) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A plugin's reads on a transaction it holds (`listEntriesInTransaction`, `findEntryByIdInTransaction`, `getSingleInTransaction` and their host forms) take `lock: "none"` (experimental): a plain read on the transaction's connection that takes no row lock on PostgreSQL and MySQL, so a plugin holding a lock of its own can read rows another write is changing without the two waiting on each other until the database refuses one.

- [#3572](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3572) [`a74781c`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/a74781c0a800aa4c509176f323df6123d1db8a6f) Thanks [@faisal-rx](https://github.com/faisal-rx)! - A plugin records events of the webhook types it declares with `ctx.webhooks.record` (experimental), in its own transaction with `tx` or on its own, and they are delivered to the endpoints subscribed to them or to `*`. A type the plugin does not declare is refused by name before anything is written. The event is stored in the existing columns, as kind `plugin` with the plugin's admin slug, so no migration runs; the delivery log shows it as the plugin's, never as a collection of the same name.

- [#3352](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3352) [`7d25b54`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/7d25b54ced237fcace58ed2ce98df4e7f61b87cd) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A plugin route can now ask a type-level permission question: `ctx.caller.can(action, resource, { anyEntry: true })` answers whether the caller may perform the action on any entry at all. It is the same access decision as plain `can`, except that a rule limiting the action to the entries a row filter matches answers yes for a write as it already did for a read. Plain `can` still answers no there, since it names no entry. The option's type, `PluginRouteCanOptions`, is exported from `@nextlyhq/plugin-sdk` and `nextly`. It decides nothing about an entry: the write itself is still judged on its entry. The page builder's site style route uses it, so an author who may update only their own entries of a collection the builder opens can now draw the canvas.

- [#3536](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3536) [`5529dd8`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/5529dd8e3d0024b7f47ca0189ae29afb394e1deb) Thanks [@zeshan-rx](https://github.com/zeshan-rx)! - A plugin's `ctx.settings.set` inside its own `ctx.db.transaction` is now refused on every dialect, with an error naming the call and the fix: write the setting after the transaction has finished. Before, it committed on a connection of its own on PostgreSQL and MySQL and survived the transaction's rollback.

  This deliberately removes SQLite's former behaviour, where the setting joined the transaction as a savepoint and rolled back with it; a plugin that wrote a setting inside a transaction now writes it after. Outside a transaction a settings write is unchanged.

- [#3589](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3589) [`b2bbf33`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/b2bbf330f4d35e0543f7737a91d2eb3a90a53fbc) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - A plugin can now change one collection's document screen through `contributes.admin.views[slug]`, from `@nextlyhq/plugin-sdk`. `documentActions` hides the built-in Delete or Unpublish there, or keeps the action's row and opens the plugin's own component in its place; the permission it needs, a colleague holding the document and a past version on screen still hold it. `panelSections` adds sections to the document panel after Details, drawn under the panel's own heading. Both are experimental and apply to collections only. The app refuses to start on an action that cannot be overridden, an override or section with nothing to draw, or two plugins overriding one action on one collection.

  A save the server refuses with a reason about a field now shows that reason on the field, and keeps the author's edits. Reasons no field on the form shows are said in the toast, rather than a bare "Validation failed.".

  `recordAdvisoryNotice` is exported from `@nextlyhq/plugin-sdk` (experimental), so a plugin's hook can tell the person saving something true about what their write leaves behind; it is shown beside the save's success as core's own notices are.

  (experimental) says what the delete takes with it, which the admin's delete

  inside the delete's own transaction, so a plugin's throw refuses the delete

  `readStoredFields(identity, { ...document, fields, form, locale })`, where the document is `{ collection, id }` or `{ single }`, returns the values as stored, for the live row (`form: "published"`) or the working draft a preview shows (`form: "draft"`), in one language, with no `afterRead` hook of the collection or of a field and no population. It reads fields of a plugin field type stored as JSON, and refuses any other, and any field a field-level read rule governs. The person must be able to read the collection or Single; the draft form also needs them to be able to update the document.

  `updateIfUnchanged(identity, { ...document, data, locale, expect })` makes the ordinary update as that person, under access rules. `expect` names a field, the form it was read in and `storedValueHash` of the value read. The update reads the field again inside its own transaction once it holds the entry's row lock (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` on PostgreSQL and MySQL; SQLite's write transaction already serializes writers), and is refused with a `CONFLICT` error, changing nothing, when the value no longer hashes to what was read. With `noPendingDraft: true` it is refused as well when a working draft is pending, which a publish would otherwise put live. The read resolves its language once, as an ordinary read does (a language the site does not configure reads as the default), and refuses a selector such as `all`.

  id, the same way a list read already does. The answer is unchanged: it still holds only those fields.

- [#3434](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3434) [`1e9176c`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/1e9176c316688a192d68694ace3a03fac7223be2) Thanks [@zeshan-rx](https://github.com/zeshan-rx)! - An access rule or a field's access rule that queries the database, and whose query waits out the pool's bound for a connection (`pool.connectionTimeoutMs`), now ends the request with a new error, `RULE_COULD_NOT_RUN` (503). It names the collection or Single whose rule it is, and the field for a field's rule, and carries the same retry hint as `DATABASE_BUSY`. Before, the wait read as the rule refusing: a publish was refused as forbidden, a field was silently left out of a read or a write, a related document read as missing, and a dashboard, a widget, release readiness or the capabilities answer quietly left the entity out. On SQLite, which keeps one connection, the same answer comes when a rule's own work queues behind a held transaction past `pool.connectionTimeoutMs`.

  Every way in answers it the same: the Direct API returns or throws it, REST answers 503 with `Retry-After` and the request id, including when the route's own gate asked the rule, and `findByID` with `disableErrors` throws it rather than answering `null`. A dashboard widget's slot that meets it carries `code: "RULE_COULD_NOT_RUN"` with the subject, since a streamed batch has already answered. A collection create (single, in a caller's transaction, or batched), a field group's instances, and in production a Single's update are refused with the not-registered answer (`ENTITY_NOT_MIGRATED`, 409, naming `nextly migrate` and a restart) and write no row. In development a Single is still recovered on a read or a write, as a second dev worker needs. The CLI commands that take the schema lock (`migrate:resolve`, `migrate:baseline`, `migrate:down`, `upgrade`, plugin install and uninstall) keep working on a database whose lock row is not yet seeded.

  **Compatibility:** an adapter used without a table registry (no `setTableResolver`) now refuses transaction inserts, as it already refused transaction updates, deletes, selects and upserts — inserts were the one write that still went through, so this makes them consistent rather than adding a new refusal.   reaches every block of that type. The edit is stored as a look in the site's
  class library, marked `isDefault`, and laid over the block's base styles
  property by property, so every default value the site didn't change is kept. A
  look, a shared style and the block's own values still win over it, and under

  seeds them in the code tier, so a site stores one only once it changes it.
  `blockLooks()` still gives only the looks a block can wear. An own look is
  never written as a class, so no block can wear it or refer to it. A variation
  that is its block's own look and also states styles is no longer read as a
  look.

  already receive. A route that states classes of its own keeps them, with the
  site's own looks carried in. `overlaidStyles()`, the layering the editor uses

  name. Own looks are read under an allowance of their own, so seeding

  whatever its variation is named.

  target site's own looks. The item draws with them instead.

  before.

- [#3694](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3694) [`dddc6fd`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/dddc6fd47521e226a4b5e9d49b6c731056ae911d) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A collection entry's page stops serving once the public may no longer read the entry. While that runs, a save that would add a new copy of the component is refused, judged against what the page stores at that moment; a page that already holds a copy can still be saved, and is converted again from what was saved. A published page with unpublished changes has its draft converted and is reported, so its author can publish or discard them first. Pages whose blocks sit inside a repeater or a named group, and Layouts naming the component, are reported rather than changed. The deleting itself, and the dialog, come next.

  The rewrite is generic: other changes to every page placing a component plug in a step `(stored value, form) => unchanged | rewritten | refuse`, and share the fence, the check and the progress. It is offered as the `componentDeleteRewrite` service, @experimental.

  This adds two tables of the page builder's own (`page_builder__component_deletions` and `page_builder__component_deletion_hosts`). Run `nextly migrate` when upgrading a production site.

- [#3067](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3067) [`61036c3`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/61036c3adb95156c2c32fb0b705a7c6ac364370d) Thanks [@faisal-rx](https://github.com/faisal-rx)! - A validation refusal no longer tells its caller about a field they may not read. A publish judges every stored value, so a refusal used to name a hidden field and say what was wrong with its value: "must be at most 10" told the caller the hidden value was over 10, "is required" that it was empty, and a field's own `validate` message could carry the value itself. Each issue on a field the caller may not read, or on a row inside one, now reaches them as one issue with no path, code `UNREADABLE_FIELD` and the message "A field you can't see doesn't pass validation." The write is still refused with a 400, and issues on the fields they may read are told as before. This holds for a collection entry and a Single, for a save, a publish of one language or of every language, the Direct API and a release's readiness check, and for the fields of a field group, whether held inside the document or saved as its own instance. A caller who may not read the entry at all is told no field of it, a password is never named, and where a field `afterRead` hook could change what a read rule decides, an issue on a field with a read rule is withheld. Trusted code (`overrideAccess: true`) is told every issue, and the server log records which paths were withheld, not their messages.

- [#3486](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3486) [`0fcfeb0`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/0fcfeb0d5b0f13addc3bd2778852c2ccd99bb93f) Thanks [@faisal-rx](https://github.com/faisal-rx)! - An update that hands back its `_rev` is now judged the same way however it arrives (experimental):
  - A version a read gave while a collection's or Single's translations were not set up yet names no language. Sending it back with a save in the default language is now accepted, judged on the document's own row; before, it was refused with 400.
  - In `updateMany` and the in-transaction updates, a version from another language's read is refused with 400 before any hook runs, as a single save's is.
  - Who changed a refused document and when are now told only to a caller whom the collection's or Single's own read rule lets read it, a rule that answers a filter included. Before, any signed-in caller who could update it was told.
  - A save in a language other than the default, while translations are not set up yet, is refused with 400 before any hook runs.

The report names a document by its collection's title as the admin does, a nominated number included.

- [#3725](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3725) [`b2cb31a`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/b2cb31ae6d5d9f9aad6c24eb449de874c07bb268) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Fix two page builder address-claim failures.

  On MySQL, releasing a document's address while another save was recording a
  wait for it could deadlock, and the release failed with "An unexpected error
  occurred." A release now reads the document's claims without a lock to learn
  which address locks to take, takes them, and only then reads the claims again
  under them, so the two saves take turns instead.

  A template saved for a collection with no address now finds the entries
  holding addresses there on its own transaction, rather than through a second
  pooled connection, which on a pool of one connection waited for the connection
  the save already held and failed as "The database is busy."

A claim is taken in the same transaction as the save it belongs to, spelled one canonical way (a trailing or doubled slash, percent-encoding and Unicode forms all name one address), and held per language. A paginated list holds all of its later pages (`/news/page/2`, …) as one claim, so a page can't be published among them, and a list can't paginate over a page that's already there. A document whose address is taken can wait for it and is served there once it's released. A new API route lists the documents waiting for an address and what holds each one, naming documents the caller can't read by id only. The store isn't yet called by page saves; that follows separately.

- [#3555](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3555) [`69f8db5`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/69f8db58fd0e83dfd4b9ec52491f321ed456cb4c) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - An accordion's sections can now have a heading for a title, and the accordion has an icon of its own. - [#3215](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3215) [`c6e029d`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/c6e029d169c484e73dc772c281545cffedc3699a) Thanks [@aqib-rx](https://github.com/aqib-rx)! - An applied app migration now carries the checksum of its file's whole text, down section included: `nextly migrate`, `migrate:baseline` and `migrate:resolve --applied` all record it. When an applied file no longer matches, `nextly migrate` (and the boot migrate step) stop before changing anything, name every edited file, and exit with code 2 (`MIGRATION_TAMPERED`, as the migrations guide documents); restore the file and put the change in a new migration, or, where the edit is intended and the database already matches it, accept it with `nextly migrate:resolve --applied <file>`, which records the new checksum. `migrate:status` shows a file as "Applied (modified)" only when it differs from a recorded checksum, so a file recorded by `migrate:resolve --applied` no longer reads as modified.

  **Checksums for existing rows.** Rows recorded without a checksum (by `migrate:resolve --applied`, or by an earlier version) are taken as matching. The next run records the current file's checksum and lists those files. Edits made before the upgrade to those files are not detected. A project whose applied rows already carry a checksum (recorded by a recent `nextly migrate`) and whose applied files were edited since will see the first run of this release stop with exit code 2, naming those files; the boot migrate step logs it, keeps serving, and applies nothing until it is resolved. Restore each file, or accept the edit with `nextly migrate:resolve --applied <file>`.

- [#3255](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3255) [`6d89981`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/6d899819c3c4669753e5adc36a39e9e55dda13ea) Thanks [@faisal-rx](https://github.com/faisal-rx)! - An editor who gains a document they were kept out of now starts from the copy
  saved while they waited. When a colleague leaves the document, their claim runs
  out, or the editor takes it over, the entry editor, a Single, a custom edit view
  and the Page Builder load the latest version before the form unlocks. Until it
  arrives the form stays read-only and says it is loading. If it cannot be loaded,
  the form stays read-only, says it couldn't load the latest version, and offers
  "Try again". Before, the form unlocked over the copy read while the colleague
  held it, so the editor's next save could put that older copy back over the
  colleague's work.

  The first claim on opening a document still unlocks at once, and an editor who
  takes back a document they were displaced from keeps their unsaved changes on
  screen as before.

  Any failed read of a document already on screen, such as the read after a save,
  now keeps the editor and its unsaved changes, read-only with "Try again",
  instead of replacing it with the page's "couldn't be loaded" error. That error
  now shows only when the document never loaded.

An entry has at most one own design, held by a unique key on every dialect; it is deleted with its entry. Own designs are stored in the `templates` collection with an empty `collection`, so a collection's template is still found by its collection, and the `collection` field is no longer required by the schema (the guard requires it of a collection's template).

- [#3679](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3679) [`41d57d9`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/41d57d9391b3c9d43fce5130cb8a89883fdba462) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - An entry with its own published design is drawn on the site with that design instead of its collection's template, and takes its SEO settings from it. The content route's `templates` config takes an optional `readFor(collection, id, locale)`, which `pageBuilderContent()` now supplies: it reads the entry's own published design and the collection's published template in one query, as the public reads them. A draft own design never reaches the public page, and a provider without `readFor` keeps drawing every entry with its collection's template. An entry keeps its address while its own design is published, even when its collection's template is unpublished or deleted, and publishing or unpublishing an own design claims or gives up the entry's address in the same transaction. A Schema Builder collection whose template is deleted has no address left, so its entries are not served, own design or not. Publishing an own design, or unpublishing a template over entries with their own designs, reads those entries on the write's own transaction, a hundred to a read, and a collection that may no longer have a template (made localized, or without its `slug` field) is served nowhere, own designs or not. A plugin can list a collection's entries inside a transaction it holds: `ctx.services.collections.listEntriesInTransaction` (experimental) is `listEntries`, with the same options, access check, read hooks and answer, read on the transaction's own connection, so on a pool of one connection it answers where `listEntries` would wait for the connection the transaction holds.

  (experimental) holds the entry's row for share in the write's transaction and answers whether
  it exists, so the write either commits before a delete of the entry goes on, which then sees
  it, or waits and is told the entry is gone. It holds the entry's collection first, so a delete
  of the whole collection takes turns with the write the same way. `PENDING_CHANGE_KEY`, the
  filter key keeping entries with changes waiting to be published, is now exported
  (experimental) from `@nextlyhq/plugin-sdk`.

  The page builder uses it for an entry's own design, on every path that creates one, the
  Direct API included: a design written while its entry is deleted is refused, or deleted with
  the entry, rather than left naming an entry that is gone. Every write to a template has what
  it serves judged again in its own transaction, so a later hook cannot store a row naming both
  a collection and an entry, nor point a template or an own design at a collection other than
  the one the template guard checked. An empty value for a field naming an entry is refused (a
  form's cleared input is stored as none). A title made from an entry's title is cut to the
  length the title field counts, never splitting an emoji. Deleting a template now empties its
  link on every design copied from it, a published design's live row included, without
  publishing a draft that waits on it; deleting an own design no longer looks for copies of it.

  On MySQL a collection's named lock is now also taken under a name for the database as well
  as the collection. It is still taken under its old name too, so instances on the old and new
  releases keep taking turns during a rolling deployment; once a later release drops the old
  name, two Nextly databases on one server stop waiting on each other's collection deletes.

- [#3662](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3662) [`6ddb2f0`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/6ddb2f003b90fdd4c0401157782c789e40c5360b) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Importing a transfer file that adds a design variable its documents use is no longer refused. Since pages were stopped from adding a reference to a variable the site does not define, an import's preview judged its documents before the variables it brings were in the site style, so any file whose blocks used one of its own variables was refused as it stood. The preview now judges the file's documents as if the variables it brings were already on the site, with every style kept, so a document that also uses a variable neither the site nor the file defines is still refused in the preview rather than partway through the import.

- [#3427](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3427) [`bf1ae11`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/bf1ae119c6787c766b9645cdae1dd27dc2a27870) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - An on/off switch in the inspector is now a 24px target on its own. The shared
  switch is 18px tall, which passes only while nothing else sits close to it,
  and a block whose last setting is a switch, such as an accordion item's "Open
  by default", drew it directly above "Visible on".

- [#3419](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3419) [`bb68b31`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/bb68b31177b8f5eded9708cbdbaf3a1689df0f91) Thanks [@faisal-rx](https://github.com/faisal-rx)! - An update that carries the `_rev` it read is now judged against it (experimental). When someone else's save changed the document in between, the update is refused with `STALE_VERSION` (HTTP 409) and nothing is written. The refusal gives the document's current version. A caller who may read the document is also told who or what changed it last and when, and, where the document keeps history, the newest recorded version to compare against. An update with no `_rev` is applied as before.
  - A save of one language is judged on that language and on the shared fields. Another language's save never makes it out of date.
  - In `updateMany` and the in-transaction updates, each entry is judged on its own: an out-of-date one is reported and writes nothing, and the others are applied.
  - An update of several documents with one set of values (by ids or by query) that carries `_rev` is refused with 400.
  - A `_rev` that isn't a version a read returned, or that comes from a read of another language, is refused with 400.
  - An update of every language at once (`locale: "*"`) needs the version a read of every language returned: one that doesn't name each language is refused with 400.

  If your code reads a document once and then saves it several times with `{ ...doc }`, take `_rev` from each save's result, or the second save is refused.

  An update can now choose to overwrite. Send `_overwrite: true` with the values, beside the `_rev` you read, and the update is applied whatever the document's current version, on REST, the Direct API and the plugin service alike, single updates, batches and bulk updates by ids or by query included. It needs no permission beyond the update itself, and `_overwrite` is never stored. Any value other than `true` or `false` is refused as a validation error.

  Every overwrite is recorded in the document's history, whether or not it keeps versions. When the version sent was out of date, the history names whose changes it replaced ("Overwrote changes by Ben"); with no version, or the current one, it says only that the save was an overwrite. A save whose overwrite cannot be recorded is not kept. `_overwrite` is experimental.

- [#3693](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3693) [`d94a171`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/d94a171a6c7ae5c89970a769301fe2b3a7326ca2) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Page builder: a template row can no longer commit linked (`forkedFrom`) to a template deleted while it was written. Every write that sets or changes the link holds that template's row on its own transaction and is refused once the template is gone, whichever path wrote it, so the Direct API is covered as well as giving an entry its own design. Deleting a collection also removes its entries' own designs before its template, so those designs are no longer updated, with their hooks, history and events, just before they are deleted; a copy of the template in another collection still has its link emptied.

- [#3638](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3638) [`e9650dd`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/e9650ddf6863f0daebc67557e3455ef246bf4412) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - In the page builder, an unfinished filter or visibility condition keeps what was typed when another row is changed or removed. Before, changing any row dropped every other row's unsaved edit, and a row could quietly go back to its stored value.

- [#3204](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3204) [`219e49b`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/219e49b036ce5be72782f098169b71f513691581) Thanks [@aqib-rx](https://github.com/aqib-rx)! - An app migration whose last attempt stopped or failed part-way, on MySQL or in a file marked `-- nextly:no-transaction`, now stops `nextly migrate`, the boot migrate step and `migrate:down` before they change anything, where before only `nextly migrate` stopped on it and `migrate:down` ran a stopped down section again. The refusal names the file and judges each of its statements from the database as it stands: done, not done, or unknown for a statement whose effect the schema cannot show (one that writes rows, say). Finish the file by hand or reverse what ran, then record which with `nextly migrate:resolve`. An unresolved attempt at a file the build no longer has is refused on every dialect, since the build cannot tell how it ran; `migrate:resolve --failed-cleanup` clears it once what ran is reversed. A down section that stopped or failed this way (one `migrate:down` left behind, before this release too) now also stops `nextly migrate` and the boot migrate step: if you reversed what of it ran, `migrate:resolve --failed-cleanup` now clears it and the migration stays applied; if you finished it, `migrate:resolve --rolled-back` records the rollback.

  **Upgrading.** After upgrading, a site whose migration history holds an old failed attempt at a migration file the project no longer has stops applying migrations. The site keeps serving: its startup log says `Boot migrations failed: …` and names the file with an unresolved attempt, and `nextly migrate` exits with a failure that names it too. A failed migration record from before this release can also stop it for a file the project still has, when that file has changed since the attempt (or the record holds no checksum matching it). To go on, run `nextly migrate:resolve --failed-cleanup <file>` for each file the message lists, or `nextly migrate:resolve --applied <file>` if that migration fully ran. `--failed-cleanup` needs no file and changes no schema.

While the switch is on, the canvas reads its lists as a visitor would: published entries and public fields only, and only for a document the person editing may open. A block an entry hides is drawn as a marker in its place that says why, and the Previewing count no longer treats such blocks as unchecked. With the switch off, the canvas shows the person's own rows again, drafts included. Published pages are unchanged: a block an entry hides is still left out. `PageRenderer` takes an experimental `itemHiddenAs` for an editor to draw in that block's place.

- [#3744](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3744) [`fb591ad`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/fb591ad52210aa34887f764b0d6295ca5d8e1aea) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - With Apply conditions on, a list inside a placed component now gets the "Showing what visitors see" tag like any other list, a list beneath a conditioned block of the component included, and a date condition on the entries of a list a Layout region draws is judged in the site's time zone. A list whose read the page's allowance refused says it shows none of the entries.
