- [#3807](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3807) [`233c6f8`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/233c6f871c3c0af967cb2f29e6c965748a8027b3) Thanks [@zeshan-rx](https://github.com/zeshan-rx)! - A reviewer can no longer approve a change hidden from them in the language they are approving: a translated part's changed fields are judged as a read in that language judges them, so a field rule that answers by language (`read: ({ locale }) => ...`) refuses the approval where a read in that language would withhold the field, and the people suggested to approve instead are judged the same way.

- [#3756](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3756) [`bbfca44`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/bbfca445ca7c1e869abf41bf9df13c164dfe93c8) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - On the dashboard, a card's saved height is now the most it is drawn at, and a row of cards is as tall as the tallest of the cards that share it needs. Needs your attention and Upcoming releases holding fewer items than their rows hold are drawn at the height their items take, so one item no longer sits above rows of empty room; the two cards side by side keep one height, with their bottoms aligned, at the taller of their contents. Every other card is drawn at its saved size as before, and holds its row at that height, and no card moves to another place. In customise mode every card is drawn at its saved size, so it can still be resized.

- [#2781](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/2781) [`eb0bace`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/eb0bacec2d601b99a590e8a2b197a950aaae06c5) Thanks [@muzzamil-rx](https://github.com/muzzamil-rx)! - A password-reset, email-verification or invite link, an API key, and a refresh session store their expiry as the whole second the issuer computed. A column that keeps whole seconds — MySQL's `DATETIME` — rounds milliseconds rather than cutting them, which stored such an expiry up to half a second after the instant the code computed, and the checks comparing that stored value with a millisecond clock accepted a password-reset token briefly past its end. An expiry can now end up to a second earlier than its lifetime nominally runs, which is the safe direction.

- [#3717](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3717) [`f25576d`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/f25576d0723ebeaa39078a924fa8c4c1ad8db718) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The inspector binds and unbinds a prop: a bind button beside each bindable field opens a picker of the fields that fit it, grouped by source, with each field's value as the author reads it and words for one visitors can't read or a draft holds; a bound prop shows a chip naming its field and source, its fallback, and a menu to change the field or unbind it, keeping what visitors saw.

- [#3698](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3698) [`7b8750b`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/7b8750b6c3a2c15477a540d098ca7db6025af22b) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A block's prop can be bound to a field, and unbound, through the page actions API: `bind-prop` and `unbind-prop` on `POST /pages/actions`, each with a dry run, judged as an editor save is. An unbind keeps what a visitor sees now, read on the server from the published page with the public's access: never a pending draft's value, nor a field visitors can't read, for which the fallback or the prop's own value is kept instead. A template's and a list item's value is kept once the entry or item is named, and a value can be given. - [#3321](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3321) [`0f79732`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/0f797326d74fd7664650e5831d136931ead5e867) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Stored bindings now fill their props on published pages. Before blocks render,
  one pass checks each binding and fills its prop from the entry the page shows,
  the list item a collection loop is drawing, a Single or the public site
  settings, following one to-one relation at most. An empty value shows the
  binding's fallback, or the prop's own value when there is none. The routes read
  the entry, each Single and the site settings a page binds, and the related entry
  a path follows, through the public reader, and check each binding against the
  field shapes the public may see.

  Bindings are read with a visitor's access. `createBlocksPage` and
  `createPublicBlocksPage` read the entry again through the route's public reader
  for the fields the page binds, at one claim on the page's query budget, rather
  than using the row the route resolved: a public route reads that row with
  trusted access, and a draft preview reads the draft. So a field the public may
  not read shows the fallback, and a preview shows the published values.

  Dates, numbers and currency amounts format in the page's language. A date picked
  as a day keeps its day in every time zone, a month shows its month and year, and
  a time of day shows only its time; a date-time is shown in the route's new
  `timeZone` option, else the site's time zone, else UTC. Every block receives the new `bound` render
  argument (`@experimental`), which carries a bound date's machine-readable value,
  and the core heading, text, quote and button blocks wrap a bound date in
  `<time datetime>`.

  A binding stored before these checks existed may break them. None fails the
  page: a binding to a prop the block does not have fills nothing, a format this
  release does not apply (`relativeTime`, `list`) shows the value as it is when it
  fits, and any other broken binding shows its fallback, or the prop's own value
  when the fallback is not valid. Each is reported through `PageRenderer`'s new
  `onBindingIssues`, and the routes log one warning per report.

  Compatibility: a page that stored bindings through the API showed each bound
  prop's own value until now, and now shows the bound value. Pages without
  bindings render exactly as before. `PageRenderer` takes the new `bindings` and
  `onBindingIssues` props; `PageContext` gains `itemSource`; `DocumentReadStages`
  gains the `bound`, `boundValues` and `bindingIssues` stages, and
  `prepareDocumentAsDrawn` returns the bound stage. The validator accepts an
  optional `bindingSchema` that checks each binding's path, field and format, and
  its issue codes gain the binding codes; `ISSUE_CODES` is now typed as a record
  of `IssueCode` to `string`, so a caller that read a description's literal type
  reads `string`. `@nextlyhq/blocks-engine` exports the binding vocabulary
  (`BindingValueKind`, `FIELD_TYPE_BINDING_KIND`, `BINDABLE_KINDS`,
  `STORAGE_PRIMITIVE_AS_FIELD_TYPE`, `BindingEndpoint`, `bindingKindOf`,
  `canBindFieldToProp`), `@experimental`. `BlocksPublicReader` gains an optional
  `findSingle`. A route prepares each document once per render and hands that to
  the renderer. Existing callers that pass none of these see no change.

- [#3669](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3669) [`da6ed74`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/da6ed74310734e1c7453da2206ce81af2d1caa24) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The Page Builder shows the bindings that no longer fit their fields where authors look: a "Bindings to fix" page under Page Builder, a line on the dashboard's Needs your attention card (and a card to add), and a notice in the editor's top bar that lists the open page's broken bindings and selects each one's block.

- [#3623](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3623) [`bbbba9f`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/bbbba9f44a9626bcd192a7ab840956fa38698ca6) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The Design panel's Block looks group now tells apart two block types' own looks that share an id when searching: each is found by its own name and the values it sets, so a search for one no longer lists the other or hides both.

  A block type's own look is now held from editing whenever any other look or shared style in the site's library carries its id, not only another type's own look, since a write by id would reach both. The editing bar says why.

  A worn look's row now counts the open page's blocks wearing it, unsaved ones included, beside the documents the site has counted, as a shared style's row does.

- [#3485](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3485) [`528fb0a`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/528fb0ae95ba226e1f025d2c7d1c00b4f30e05ff) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Blocks can declare looks: named variants such as a button's Secondary, Outline
  and Text, an image's Rounded and Circle, and a section's Hero. A look is a
  `variations` entry with `styles`, and the site receives it as a shared style
  bound to that block type, supplied by code and editable by the site. Looks are
  written before every other shared style, so a shared style and the block's own
  values still win over them. The core blocks ship these looks, built from the
  site's tokens. The Add panel lists each block once, and looks stay out of the
  shared styles list and picker until their tiles arrive in the inspector.

A resolved node names it for each exposed prop, so a host typing a resolved page can name it without depending on the engine directly.

- [#3277](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3277) [`6982e03`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/6982e03cbe78694113c9085f474c8275c22cfaa5) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - `@nextlyhq/blocks-react` now re-exports `ExposedPropertyType`, `ResolveComponentOptions` and `WorkAllowance` from the engine, which types it already exports refer to, so a host can name them without depending on the engine directly.

- [#3373](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3373) [`76b2a7b`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/76b2a7be870ca883081f00b106fa03b976cd6dae) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Blocks now carry no outer margin; the space between blocks comes from the block holding them. A heading, paragraph, list, figure, quote, rule and code block have no margin above or below (an `h2` drew 42px above and 14px below), and a figure has none at its sides, so a captioned image sits as flush as one without a caption. Section, Box, Card, Column, an accordion item and a collection loop put a gap above every block after the first, which becomes `gap` when the container is set to flex or grid. Rich text spaces its own paragraphs inside the block. Section is padded above, below and at the sides, Card is padded, and Button padding is 12 × 20. Every value is a site variable (`space.stack`, `space.section-y`, `space.gutter`, `space.columns`, `space.card`, `space.paragraph`, `button.padding-y`, `button.padding-x`), most growing with the screen, and spacing set on a block always wins over them (in flex or grid a block's own margin adds to the container's gap). A `childGap` must be a length both a margin and a gap take, so a negative one is refused at registration. The canvas labels a container's gap "Gap · from Section". Block definitions take a new optional `childGap`.

  **Visual change.** Existing pages move: headings lose their space above and below, paragraphs lose the space below them and gain the container's gap above, Divider and Quote lose their space above and below, Sections gain 48–80px of padding above and below and 16–32px at the sides, Cards gain 16–24px of padding, Columns and Gallery gaps grow from 16px to 16–32px, and Buttons grow. Stored page stylesheets are recompiled on their next render rather than served with the old spacing; a render under a host-fetch policy judges their URLs by that policy as it does, and one that names a policy without its predicate withholds them. To keep a block's old look, set its spacing explicitly in Style → Spacing (or change the variables under Design → Variables).

- [#3727](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3727) [`cda526e`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/cda526e0231a413cdadf4b2379efb5152c951dc0) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The blog template credits each post to a public author profile. A new `authors` collection holds the profile a reader sees: a name, a slug for `/authors/<slug>`, a bio and an avatar from the media library. Posts gain a `byline` relationship to it, while `author` stays the account that owns the post, so who may edit a post is unchanged. A new post is credited to its writer's profile when it has none, and a byline an editor chose is never replaced. Only a caller who may publish posts chooses a byline, as for `author`, and an account has one profile at most. A profile's account is read only by a caller who may change profiles, and deleting a profile clears the byline of its posts. A post written inside a transaction its caller holds is credited once that transaction commits. A blog made with the visual approach registers the hooks that fill a new post's owner and byline through a plugin of the template's own, since its Posts can hold no function. The demo seed creates one profile per seeded user, with its avatar uploaded to the media library (a file name or an absolute address, which it fetches), and credits each post to it; running it again credits a post an earlier run left uncredited, and uploads an avatar only for a profile without one.

  The post, author, category and tag pages read the author from the byline, so the post page's author link and biography now show; before, it read the owning account, which carries neither, and linked to `/authors/undefined`. The post page still draws the author's initial in place of the avatar, because a post read does not yet load the avatar of its byline. Existing scaffolded sites are untouched: the template is copied into a site when it is created, so this reaches new sites only.

  The table of contents block's links are underlined, with hover and keyboard focus states, so they read as links on any site.

The blog template's migrations now create those three tables outright, and writing them needs no consent.

  A blog scaffolded with `--approach code-first` type-checks again once `nextly generate:types` has run: `bylineFromCreator` and the seed's Single writer no longer pass a plain `string` where the generated collection or Single slug union is expected. A site that renames the collections keeps naming them by slug, as before.

  A visual blog's build now installs the plugin it registers from its own source (`nextly plugins install --all`). A production boot refuses any enabled plugin that nothing has installed, and `create-nextly-app` only installed plugins from `@nextlyhq/plugin-*` packages, so `next build` stopped on `/_not-found`.

- [#3761](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3761) [`cc6549d`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/cc6549d9783f98809df5af4e43e9f1ee596fe887) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - In the page builder, choosing Currency as a bound value's format keeps its Code field open for a code to be typed, an unfinished condition or filter row keeps its draft when another row is written or removed, and the switch for applying conditions is offered when the only condition sits on a component placed inside another placed component.

- [#3368](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3368) [`fc0c116`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/fc0c11664925306e61445ce52691903aebdbb2ae) Thanks [@aqib-rx](https://github.com/aqib-rx)! - Every Schema Builder save now holds the schema lock, and while a migration holds it the save is refused at once with nothing changed, telling the editor a migration is running and to save again once it ends. That covers collection create, update, delete and confirmed apply, a Single's confirmed apply, user-field create, update and delete, and the published collection, Single and user-field schema routes. Before, these saves could run beside `nextly migrate`, `db:sync` or a field-group migration. A save in production takes the lock wherever its table exists and never creates that table, so a database role without DDL rights keeps saving as before; a development save may create it.

- [#3282](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3282) [`58dbe40`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/58dbe4031729853abeea2f71556ba4e69ecb1123) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - On a page with an Embed block, the Page Builder's canvas follows the device
  and zoom controls again when the app runs in development. React's
  development build describes a component's changed props by walking into
  them, and the window the canvas handed to its blocks led that walk to the
  embed's frame, which the browser does not let the admin read. The resulting

Nothing changes for authors yet; this prepares the canvas to move into a frame.

- [#3747](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3747) [`aadfae2`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/aadfae2a751972df49fc4841a982bc43a77641b8) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The canvas's preview tags (the variant previewed and the Light or Dark preview) stay at the top of the canvas while a long page scrolls under them, instead of leaving with the page's top. `CanvasFrame` gains an experimental `pinned` slot for chrome held at the frame's viewport.

- [#3699](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3699) [`1714d78`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/1714d78fb436c9c953eed2f130c6ac030f5e311b) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A binding to the site settings is now checked at save: the four settings a page is handed (`applicationName`, `siteUrl`, `logoUrl`, `timezone`) are one table in `@nextlyhq/blocks-engine`, read by the renderer, the save and the "Bindings to fix" report, so a binding to any other setting is refused, and one saved before is kept and listed.

- [#3212](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3212) [`0ec6311`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/0ec63112154d54879d806d698297d3334c1ddb7f) Thanks [@aqib-rx](https://github.com/aqib-rx)! - The checks in front of the version, preview, content-event and release routes now answer `ENTITY_NOT_MIGRATED` (409) when the database lacks an entity's table or a declared field's column. Before, they answered a 500. Those checks are reading a Single's document id, judging whether a document may be read or updated, the release readiness reads, and the legacy batch writes. A table name holding a space, a dot or a dash is also now recognised whole in the database's error.

  **Compatibility:** a legacy batch write (`createMany`, `updateMany`, `createEntries`, `updateEntries`, `deleteEntries` and their transaction versions) now stops at the first item the database is not migrated for (for the batch's own collection), whatever `stopOnError` says. A batch that runs its own transaction rolls it back whole and reports that answer on every item; a transaction version throws that answer, and the caller's transaction decides what it keeps. Before, whether its other items were saved depended on the database and on which columns each item's write named. Each item in a batch's `errors` also now carries the error `code` of its own failure. A transaction version with `stopOnError` now throws that item's own error (such as 409 or 404) instead of a generic 500.

- [#3286](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3286) [`11604e6`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/11604e62e6fca49efdbf9cf798c494097954c1c9) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Choose a page's Layout in the editor. One **Layout** picker, at the top of the editor's Settings and on the page's Page Builder card, offers the site default (named), each Layout (unpublished ones marked) and "No header or footer", and the line under it says which Layout is in effect and why. The page's two stored values are now set only through that picker, so the form no longer shows them as separate fields.

  The editor draws the Layout's header and footer around the page, locked, as visitors get them. A click on a region shows where it comes from, with "Edit Layout ↗" opening the Layout in a new tab for authors who may edit it, and Layers lists the regions as locked rows. Publishing a page that names an unpublished Layout now tells you the site default shows until that Layout is published.

- [#3207](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3207) [`a0e3103`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/a0e3103b8d77d13fd198107b3f9b88c88ac17dc1) Thanks [@aqib-rx](https://github.com/aqib-rx)! - `nextly --version`, `nextly --help`, a command's `--help` and a mistyped
  command now answer in a fraction of a second instead of several. Each command
  is declared without loading what it does, and its work is loaded only when it
  runs. They also read nothing from the project: neither `nextly.config.ts` nor
  `.env`, so they answer the same in any folder, even one whose configuration
  does not parse.

  `.env` is now read just before a command's work starts rather than when the
  CLI starts. The colour choice of the CLI's own output is made at start, so a
  `NO_COLOR` or `FORCE_COLOR` set only in `.env` no longer changes it; set it in
  the shell instead.

- [#3369](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3369) [`cc98f18`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/cc98f18d926dc3b9b33957fbe7ea7a1e138d553d) Thanks [@aqib-rx](https://github.com/aqib-rx)! - The CLI's flags now mean one thing on every command, every command's help ends
  with its exit codes, and no command waits for an answer it cannot get.

  Compatibility, for scripts and CI:
  - A deletion declined at the prompt now exits 1 on `migrate:fresh`,
    `migrate:down` and `prune` (it exited 0). A `prune` that cannot be asked (no
    terminal, `CI` set, or `--non-interactive`) and has no consent now exits 1 as
    well; `migrate:fresh` and `migrate:down` already exited 1 there. Give
    `--accept-data-loss` (or `NEXTLY_ACCEPT_DATA_LOSS`) to let it run.
  - `--yes` never consents to deleting data. `migrate:fresh --yes` is refused and
    names `--accept-data-loss`.
  - `webhooks:prune` and `permissions:cleanup` now take `--accept-data-loss`.
    In this release a run that cannot be asked still deletes and prints a
    notice; from the next release it needs `--accept-data-loss` (or
    `NEXTLY_ACCEPT_DATA_LOSS`). With a terminal they ask. `i18n:restore --purge`
    takes the consent too.
  - `nextly db:sync --remove-orphaned` now lists the orphaned tables, registry
    entries and permissions it would delete and takes the data-loss consent
    first: at a terminal it asks, and a no exits 1 with nothing deleted; where
    nobody can be asked it still deletes in this release and prints that the next
    release needs `--accept-data-loss`.
  - `nextly migrate:create` with nothing to do exits 0 (it exited 2).
  - `nextly generate:types --check` exits 2 when the component map is out of step
    and 1 when it could not check (the two were the other way round).
  - A failed `nextly add` exits 1 and names the package manager's own code.
  - Retired spellings, honoured for one release with a notice: `migrate:fresh
-f/--force` and `prune --force` (use `--accept-data-loss`), and
    `generate:widget --force` (use `--overwrite`). `db:sync -f/--force`, which
    never did anything, is refused.

  New:
  - A global `--non-interactive`: never prompt; a command that needs an answer
    stops before changing anything and names the flag that gives it. Prompts are
    also skipped whenever stdin or stdout is not a terminal, or `CI` is set.
    `migrate:create`'s own `--non-interactive` is now this one.
  - `db:sync --yes` answers `--promote` / `--demote`'s confirmation. Without a
    terminal, `init` (without `--yes`), `db:sync --promote/--demote` (without
    `--yes`) and `upgrade --reconcile-core` stop with an error of their own
    instead of waiting.
  - A misspelt flag or command is refused with the nearest one suggested, on
    every command, `media` and `permissions:cleanup` included.
  - Ctrl+C at a prompt of a `nextly` command ends the run with exit 130; it is
    no longer taken as a no. Inside `next dev`, Ctrl+C at a schema prompt still
    cancels only that change and the server keeps running.

- [#3594](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3594) [`b709913`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/b7099131c2cfc6df8d3b8ac53534944ac992c83b) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The page builder gains collection templates: a `templates` collection of builder documents of kind `template`, each naming the collection whose entries it draws in a unique `collection` field. A collection has one template whatever its state, so a second is refused when it is created, naming the first, and the database refuses one that gets past that check, on every dialect. A template's collection is fixed while that collection exists, and may be pointed at another once its own is renamed or deleted. `POST /templates/actions` and the composition service's `templateAction` create a template (`create-template`) and publish one (`publish-template`), each with a dry run that answers refusals, asking the caller's rights first. The schemas are published as `templateActionSchema` from `@nextlyhq/builder/ops`. The collection is built by the schema pipeline from its fields, with no migration file, and stays out of the admin's navigation until its screens ship. Templates are not served yet: nothing renders an entry with one in this release.

- [#3494](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3494) [`cfa94e4`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/cfa94e497c3c003ab63cbfb33f9ebcaba3490177) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A Columns row has a layout in its Style tab: tiles for Auto, 50 / 50, 33 / 67, 67 / 33, 25 / 75, 3 equal and 4 equal, written as its columns at the edited device, adding or removing empty columns to match; where it stacks (Tablet, Mobile or Never); and whether it stacks reversed. Each choice writes the row only, as one undo step.

- [#3656](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3656) [`4745a55`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/4745a551932d4e408ae280d076242b7e2b644c48) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A component delete's check now asks each write it will make with the body that write sends (the converted blocks, and the status where the write names one), so a field rule reading `data` answers the check as it answers the write; `mayWriteEntry` takes that body as an optional `data`. A component store without the Draft/Published lifecycle no longer treats a change to its own `status` field as an unpublish.

- [#3609](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3609) [`d8a418b`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/d8a418b715b9e4154911dcca5446eab764aeb07a) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The Page Builder can delete a component that pages use, turning every copy into plain blocks first. `POST /components/:id/delete` (with `dryRun` for the plan) and `GET` for progress run the delete as the person who started it, one bounded step per request: a check before anything changes (a Layout using it, a copy that cannot be converted, or a document they may not change stops it with nothing changed), the conversion, then the delete. Before each step it asks core's new `mayDeleteEntry` (in `@nextlyhq/plugin-sdk`, experimental) whether the person may delete that component: the delete's own gate, a rule over the row included, with no hook run and nothing written. A save already in flight is judged again inside its own transaction, and a deleted component leaves a lasting record that refuses any save still holding it, so no save leaves a copy of it. A component's own delete now goes only through this action, and unpublishing a component that documents use is refused, naming them; when the usage index names none, every document is read to confirm it.

- [#3497](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3497) [`cc9c510`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/cc9c510dc03e1367eade187bd4ba5eeadd658205) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Publishing a component that removes an exposed field now counts again: when
  more documents place the component than the removal dialog said, the editor
  asks again with the new count before anything goes live. While the removal is
  held for its publish, a write that newly sets one of the removed fields on a
  placement of the component is refused, saying the field is being removed, so
  the count the designer confirms is the one that loses a value.

- [#3308](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3308) [`57934c2`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/57934c24a63f5a6cc85150122e19d47724a38734) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A block a component locks in Layers is held in the editor on every page that places it: the field that drives it is read-only in the placement's panel with "Set by the component <name>. Change it where the component is edited.", double-clicking its text on the canvas says the same instead of opening it, and an edit that would change it is refused before it is applied, judged as the save judges it. A field a `contentOnly` area holds says that area's reason the same way. A component's variant that sets a value on a block the component locks is refused when the component is saved, naming the block and the variant. Moving another block across a locked one is now allowed by the save as it is by the editor: a reorder is read as the fewest blocks moved that explain it, so the locked block counts as moved only when moving it is the shorter explanation, and the editor refuses a group of moves the save would read that way. In `@nextlyhq/blocks-engine`, `componentLayersLocks`, `placedLockChanges`, `placementsAsComponentsHoldThem` and `variantLockChanges` are new exports; in `@nextlyhq/builder`, `LockedRelation` gains `"component"` (a consumer switching over it adds a case, worded with `lockRefusalWording`), `useEditorState` takes an optional `componentName`, and `lockViewOf` is exported from `@nextlyhq/builder/shell`.

- [#3279](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3279) [`be53f2a`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/be53f2aaf97b451ee2840865c8b2e214a68327f3) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A component's variants can now be defined, renamed and deleted in the component's own view, and a placement picks one in its inspector. A variant's id is its stored key, so a rename keeps every placement on it, and a new variant gets an opaque key that is never reused. Variant names are unique per component, ignoring case and spaces: a save that creates a clash is refused, while a clash already stored is only warned about. A page write that newly sets a variant the component does not define is refused. Deleting a variant shows how many placements use it, and those placements show the component's defaults while keeping their own values; the inspector says "Variant removed, showing defaults" with Clear. A variant that presets nothing is marked "(no changes)".

- [#3365](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3365) [`1993a3f`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/1993a3f6ff19324a8eae96c9382c17f97cda3c6f) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The component view and the "Turn into component" dialog now speak plainly. The icon beside a property is named "Let each page change <property>", and its tooltip says in one line what turning it on does; every sentence in these surfaces says "page" where it said "placement", and none says "expose".

- [#3328](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3328) [`91cdb31`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/91cdb3164534edbbfa6ce29448f73c4dde33044e) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The Page Builder's rail has a Components panel: search the site's components,
  place one by click, keyboard or drag where the Add panel would, and open it
  alone with Edit. Components in the Add panel can now be dragged too.

- [#3387](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3387) [`22a4cf3`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/22a4cf345bc9f8d7ab994d060eb1f32e67f5a781) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The Components panel works out which components have nothing to place from
  the list it has already built, instead of reading every definition twice.

- [#3455](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3455) [`3d541bb`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/3d541bb08b5c4d6612b4d3f2515016ac52a23dff) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Everything an editor does to compose a page can now be done through the API,
  with a dry run first.

  `POST /pages/actions` inserts a pattern, places a component (with a variant and
  values), changes a placement's values or variant, and chooses a page's Layout.
  `POST /components/:id/definition` exposes, renames, retargets and removes a
  component's fields and adds, renames and deletes its variants and their values,
  held to the same rules as the component's own view. `save-as-pattern` takes
  `dryRun` too.

  A dry run makes the write as the caller and rolls it back, so it answers what
  the site would refuse. Every answer carries a `fingerprint`; sent back as
  `expect`, an apply refuses with 409 when the item changed since. Each answer
  says who it ran as, a person or an API key. These routes are experimental.

- [#3492](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3492) [`9da66af`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/9da66afeeb7da8a8e3f682b69761deac36f807bf) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - An API client or an agent can now find every id the composition actions take,
  and reach the actions from server code without an HTTP round trip.

  `GET /manifest` on the page builder lists the patterns, the components with
  their exposed fields, slots and variants (by id and name), and the Layouts with
  their regions and which is the site default, each read as the caller, with the
  actions and the JSON Schema of their requests. `compositionManifestSchema`
  validates it. The same manifest and the page and definition actions are a
  service, `composition`, that another plugin's route calls with its own
  request's context, with every check the routes make.

  `@nextlyhq/builder/ops` now publishes the actions' schemas
  (`pageActionSchema`, `definitionActionSchema`, and their JSON Schema forms),
  `planDefinitionAction`, and the editor's planners. The routes parse with those
  schemas, so a client validating against them is refused for what the route
  refuses. `@nextlyhq/builder` now depends on `zod`, used only by that subpath.

  A component kept in a collection of the site's own, named by
  `componentReadiness`, can now be edited through `POST /components/:id/definition`;
  it was refused before.

- [#3617](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3617) [`b4636f8`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/b4636f8fe90cc1f527fc2240b516c20f712c4697) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Two page builder saves made at once can no longer each pass against the composition graph as it stood before the other. Every write that changes a blocks value is judged again inside its own transaction, after it is stored, while it holds a lock on the graph: no component loop, the composed nesting and depth of the document, and for a component the documents placing it. A second writer waits at the lock until the first commits, and is then judged against what the first stored; a write refused there is rolled back whole. Writes to collections without a blocks field, and writes leaving their blocks unchanged, never wait on it. The lock is a row of the plugin's own options table, locked by the write on PostgreSQL and MySQL; SQLite already runs one writer at a time.

  A write made inside a transaction its caller opened at a snapshot isolation (MySQL's default) that started before another write held the lock is refused as a conflict, to be saved again, rather than judged against a graph it cannot see.

  Plugins: an in-transaction handler is now handed `readStored(fieldType, target)`, the stored read a field type's validator has, on the write's transaction and scoped to field types the plugin contributes, and `fieldPaths(fieldType)`, the written document's fields of that type (`@experimental`). A collection write that runs in-transaction handlers, and a batch of creates, now read committed on MySQL as they already did on PostgreSQL, so a handler that waits on a row lock reads what committed before it took it.

- [#3649](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3649) [`f5fb5bd`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/f5fb5bd67b819d0ffd62b4cff5bc38b87081ee9a) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The page builder canvas judges a placed component's own conditioned blocks as it judges the page's, so one the page can't check is badged red. Two conditioned blocks in one component get a badge each, and a badge stays clear of the block toolbar and on screen at either edge. Only the components a page places are prepared for the canvas, and conditions stored as an empty value can be removed from the inspector.

- [#3703](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3703) [`d1d6f15`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/d1d6f15b9d0a27f8ea80962715e9764d76040b0f) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A page holding a block with visibility conditions gets a strip above the canvas with an **Apply conditions** switch. Turned on, the canvas shows the page as a visitor reads it, from its published values and the fields visitors may read, read by a new route that answers nothing else.

- [#3692](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3692) [`791e6ac`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/791e6accfb123899ce7b9afacc66445654d01ed0) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A template's Previewing strip offers an **Apply conditions** switch while the template holds a block with visibility conditions. Turned on, the canvas shows the page as a visitor reading the previewed entry would get it: a block they would see is badged "Shown for this post", and one they wouldn't is drawn as one line naming it and why. A component or a Layout holding a conditioned block shows the switch turned off, with the reason.

- [#3525](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3525) [`ae6f2bf`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/ae6f2bfceaeba916ced1e02dd6c6e21679d293fe) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - On SQLite, `contains` and the search box now ignore case for letters outside ASCII, as on PostgreSQL and MySQL, so searching "CRÈME" finds "crème brûlée".

  In the media library, permission, role and user searches, a typed `%` or `_` is now matched literally rather than as a wildcard.

  A SQLite adapter of your own must now register the case fold on each connection with `registerSqliteFoldCase` from `@nextlyhq/adapter-drizzle/text-match`; the official SQLite adapter does this for you.

- [#3671](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3671) [`219384f`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/219384f09dbdeb1a5acb6d46da44e6501641e2e3) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The content route draws a link to a page or an entry only where a visitor may read the target, so a published entry kept from the public by its collection's read access no longer has its address published in a link. Pre-rendering lists the entries' addresses alone beside the pages the pages route lists, so a site with many pages still pre-renders its entries within `staticParamsLimit`. A published template pointed at another collection, after its own was renamed or deleted, now serves the new collection's entries in the same save.

- [#3787](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3787) [`44b83c6`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/44b83c6b538a104ae83912720151ab11e603306a) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - The collections, relationship and field-group services type-check again, so the core package builds. Three changes that merged together had each left a type error, and fixing them changes no behaviour.

- [#3517](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3517) [`627d428`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/627d42807aaa4b3ce9e5ebb38d14e1dbae19f5b4) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Core's own writes now rely on the transaction scope the adapters share, on every dialect.
  - A version-number race on a versioned collection or Single is retried inside the adapter's transaction rather than around it, still up to three attempts. A lost attempt's after-commit effects are dropped with it and its after-rollback effects never run. When the write runs inside a transaction someone else opened, the conflict reaches that outermost transaction instead of being retried by the inner call alone. When every attempt loses, the caller still gets a 409.
  - A migration refuses to run inside an open transaction on every dialect, before any of its work runs. On MySQL its DDL would otherwise commit the enclosing transaction implicitly.
  - Creating a user inside a plugin's `ctx.db.transaction` no longer fails with a 500 on PostgreSQL and MySQL: the new account is read back inside its own transaction, which has joined the plugin's and not yet committed.
  - Creating a user with roles, assigning a role and removing one inside a transaction someone else opened (a plugin's `ctx.db.transaction`) now flush the user's cached access once that transaction commits, not before. A permission check made while it was still open could otherwise keep the user's old access until another change to roles retired it.

- [#3450](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3450) [`95548ed`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/95548ed3d513e8ce44984bb7766e23e008093590) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The Shared styles tab offers Count now beside its note that some pages have not been counted yet: it runs the usage count for up to ten seconds and reads the counts again, for authors who may change Design, so the counts settle on a site with no scheduler for its background jobs. A plugin can run one of its own sweeps this way through `ctx.services.jobs.runSweepNow(slug)` (experimental).

- [#3770](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3770) [`5a47e82`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/5a47e82c696f13c7fb8857e71c43fe019d749872) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - The admin's notification count and the initials in the Team activity card now meet WCAG AA contrast in light and dark.

- [#3472](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3472) [`d0eb95a`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/d0eb95ae614b5f7ccd324a0f34e0a85de4357ea5) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Text decoration's icons show the line just chosen while a shared style's write is on its way; its style popover's controls are held with a section held while it is open; and its CSS row writes a value as typed. Opacity says its unit only while it holds a number.

- [#3641](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3641) [`0bc7f5d`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/0bc7f5d5a91c3e9e7702f7fa412e092941749192) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Delete component has its dialog in the admin. The component store's own Delete, in the document's menu, is now "Delete component…", and so is each row's action on the store's list. The dialog lists the documents that use the component, offers to turn each copy into plain blocks and then delete it, and shows the delete's progress until it finishes. It also says what stops a delete: a Layout that uses the component, a document it can't change, a delete someone else is running, or missing permission. It follows the configured component store, the plugin's own collection or a host's. A collection can now set `admin.disableDelete` to hide the admin's own Delete for its entries on list rows, in the selection bar and in the editor, where a plugin may replace that Delete with an action of its own. Removing a shared style now says that a class written by hand, outside the editor, isn't counted.

- [#3355](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3355) [`db2703b`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/db2703bb37071e2908354ae3de0ca83f53672f00) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The Pages panel's "Delete page" confirmation uses the admin's destructive button colours, so its label reads clearly against the red.

- [#3376](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3376) [`fa5ca4e`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/fa5ca4eeff920f3581ded6e111d85a92a784c51b) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The page builder's Design panel now takes a type size's line height without a unit, such as 1.2, starts a new type size at 1.25, says in words why a line height it refuses is refused, and writes the site style once the author pauses or closes a variable's editor, as one undo step, instead of once per field; what is still waiting is written when the page is saved or hidden, sent so it outlives the page.

- [#3357](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3357) [`fc8b6f0`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/fc8b6f08c11e81fb9918f6395f4e1205eee72939) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The page builder's Design panel has a Shared styles tab: find a shared style by name, property or value, show only the used, unused or locked ones, see how many blocks and pages use it and where, rename it (its class name follows the name), lock or unlock it if your role may, and remove the ones nothing uses after seeing them listed. While some pages are still being counted, numbers read "at least" and nothing can be removed. `@nextlyhq/builder/shell` replaces the experimental `ClassManagerPanel` with `SharedStylesPanel`.

- [#3646](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3646) [`cdbfd5a`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/cdbfd5ad3c72199697f79647d49c0cebb66fc97b) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Two authors editing the site's design at once no longer lose each other's changes. The editor's site style read now answers the document's version, and each save of the variables, shared styles or fonts sends it, merged onto the newest stored copy: entries are matched by their identity and merged field by field, so a token, style or font added or changed by someone else is kept beside the author's own change, and a lock that landed meanwhile still holds. When another save lands first, the editor reads again, merges again and saves, up to three times in all. Where both changed the same value, a save keeps the author's value and an undo or redo keeps the other person's; the save answers which entries those were. The Variables studio no longer drops a token added elsewhere while it was open, and every studio shows what was stored after a merged save. A server that gives no version is written to as before.

  The editor now says when a Design save met someone else's change to the same entry. The Variables panel shows a status line beside its error line, naming the variables ("Sam changed Primary while you were editing. Your value was kept. Undo puts theirs back."), with a Reload button that reads the variables again and drops the panel's own copy; it clears on the next edit. Shared style and font saves show the same words in a warning toast with a Reload action, and an undo or redo that met a newer change says that part could not be undone or redone. The person is named only when exactly one save came between, otherwise "Someone". A save refused after every try says the site's design kept changing, so it was not saved. A save merged cleanly shows nothing. Warning toasts across the admin now draw their text from the theme, so it reads at 4.5:1 on its surface in the light scheme (it read at about 3:1).

- [#3636](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3636) [`a3f9418`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/a3f9418a39cfc41c907710dac4647827f680df36) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The page builder's Design routes no longer refuse an author because another save of the site style landed while they ran. Locking or removing a shared style, removing a variable and adding a font each write with the version they read; when another save landed in between, the route now reads again, checks again on what is stored and makes only its own change there, up to three times in all, so both changes are kept. A removal is still refused when the newer copy makes it unsafe, such as a style locked or a shared style now using the variable, and a font face another add stored meanwhile is not stored twice, its extra files deleted. After three refusals the route answers the stale-version conflict as before. Putting back variables a page started using retries only on that conflict. Added fonts go into one "Fonts" media folder even when several server processes add fonts at once: the folder is claimed in the page builder's own options table, a process that loses the claim deletes the empty folder it made, and a claimed folder that was deleted is made again. No migration is needed.

- [#3483](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3483) [`be722df`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/be722df50843441f3690f0e49556789e945c91da) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The Detach from component dialog says "Checking what it draws…" while it checks, in the words the rest of the dialog uses, rather than the engine's word "placement".

- [#3296](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3296) [`19dfd44`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/19dfd44514127dd9a7ea5b007810d7e72293a40e) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Page Builder: detach a placement, duplicate its component, and update a pattern from a selection, from the editor.
  - **Detach from component**, in the block toolbar's More menu, the right-click menu, the block card's menu and the command palette, replaces a placement with the plain blocks it draws, as one undoable step. The blocks look exactly as they did: the placement's own values, its variant and the content in its slots are kept, and a component placed inside it stays a placement. The form says first when the component has unpublished changes.
  - **Duplicate component** copies the placement's component under a new name, published, and points that one placement at the copy, keeping its values. Other placements keep the original. Where the copy came from is recorded in the plugin's own bookkeeping.
  - **Update a pattern** replaces a pattern's content with the selection, published. Pages that inserted it earlier keep their copies.
  - New plugin routes (`@experimental`): `POST /components/detach`, `POST /components/:id/duplicate` and `POST /patterns/:id/from-selection`. Each takes `dryRun`, runs as the caller and reports who ran it, by user or API key. Detach and duplicate take a placement in a page the caller holds (`library`) or in a stored page (`stored`), where a duplicate's create and the page's update run in one transaction.

  **Compatibility (`@nextlyhq/builder`):** `ToolbarActionId` gains `"detach-component"`, `"duplicate-component"` and `"update-pattern"`. `toolbarActions` emits `duplicate-component` (and `detach-component` when the offer carries `definitions`, `update-pattern` when it carries `mayUpdatePattern`) for a host that passes a component offer. Code keeping an exhaustive `Record<ToolbarActionId, …>` or `switch` adds the three entries; a dispatcher that does not know an id should ignore it, as `blockActionRunners` runs a verb only when the host supplies it.

  - Detaching a shared style whose look depends on a screen width and a
    container width together is refused, with the reason in the menu, rather

- [#3489](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3489) [`a797482`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/a79748201af6030138a5b475609de31dcab28c96) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The Direct API now honours `showHiddenFields: false` on `find`, `findByID`, `findSingle` and the `users` reads: it leaves `admin.hidden` fields out, and refuses a filter or a sort on one, and a `count`, `group` or `timeseries` naming one, after the caller passes the read gate.   list item under More. Text case is None, Uppercase, Lowercase and
  Capitalize as icons. A font size's menu offers the site's type scale above

- [#3596](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3596) [`d84fab9`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/d84fab9ce6db74c88831793367138f1df6ce36fa) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A builder document can state its own title, description and social image in `settings.seo`. A text value is a list of literal text and bindings, joined in order: an entry's title, then the site's name. The image is one binding, to a media field or a URL field. The page's binding pass fills each binding with the same checks, format and fallback a text prop's binding gets, so a collection template gives each entry's page its own metadata. A stated value wins over what the blocks offer, in `metadata`'s `derived` argument. The validator refuses a malformed value, a list item as a source, more than 32 segments and literal text over 1,000 characters (`invalid-seo`). `resolveDocumentSeo` is exported from `@nextlyhq/blocks-engine`.

- [#3433](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3433) [`eacbb38`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/eacbb385ddc06c99ae25229cb8dcb05e10107220) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Change a number field in the Style panel by dragging its label.
  - Drag a number field's label left or right to change its value. Shift moves it in
    steps of ten and Alt in tenths. The field shows the value as it changes, and
    letting go writes it once, so one Undo takes back the whole drag. Escape during
    a drag puts the value back.

- [#3265](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3265) [`107e27b`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/107e27b45b1a0cb18a8062bf34be02c943e44a49) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Page builder: drag a row in Layers to move its block, and drag it to the right to put it inside the block above. A closed block opens when you rest on it, and the list scrolls near its edges. A drop the placement rule or a locked area refuses shows a red line with the reason, and the block stays where it was. The block menu gains Move in and Move out, so every move also works from the keyboard or the menu. Layers rows indent 20px a level, the same distance a drag moves to nest, and a selected row is shaded so it stands apart from a hovered one.

- [#3541](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3541) [`a2a5505`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/a2a55055c0c101c59b5884e52b6264ae6ff32b4e) Thanks [@aqib-rx](https://github.com/aqib-rx)! - `--dry-run` on `upgrade`, `plugins install`, `plugins uninstall` and
  `media reindex-usage`: show what would change, change nothing. Each opens the
  database read-only, takes no lock, asks no confirmation or data-loss consent,
  and exits 0, naming the real run's refusal where it would refuse. `db:sync` is
  now the only command that writes by default without `--dry-run`.
  - `upgrade --dry-run` counts each step's pending work, all counts taken before
    any step runs, and names a refusal such as a backup nobody can confirm.
  - `upgrade --reconcile-core --dry-run` names each statement the reconcile's
    push would run, and each table or column drop it leaves in place.
  - `plugins install --dry-run` names each pending module with what it deletes,
    the owner rows set back to active and the record made; with `--all`, a
    plugin is planned as if the installs before it had run.
  - `plugins uninstall --dry-run` names each module's DOWN, what it drops (none
    with `--keep-data`) and the records made.
  - `media reindex-usage --dry-run` names the usage record it would replace and
    the collections, Singles and email templates it would read, without booting
    the app.
  - Plugin hooks (`onInstall`, `onUninstall`) are not run by a dry run, which
    says so.

  `upgrade --reconcile-core` now asks to confirm only the destructive changes it
  will make. A core reconcile never drops one of Nextly's own tables or columns,
  so such a drop is reported as left in place instead of asked about, and with
  nothing else destructive to make it asks nothing, even without a terminal.

- [#3515](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3515) [`067ba55`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/067ba555243e6acbbd0c7e06b09d0e6fd4dfdf63) Thanks [@aqib-rx](https://github.com/aqib-rx)! - More commands that write the database take `--dry-run`: show what would
  change, change nothing. Each opens the database read-only, asks no
  confirmation or data-loss consent, and exits 0, naming the real run's refusal
  where it would refuse.
  - `prune --dry-run` lists every table it would drop, in the words the consent
    uses, and still reports a collection something depends on.
  - `permissions:cleanup --dry-run` names each permission it would delete with
    its grants.
  - `migrate:fresh --dry-run` names every table it would drop and each migration
    it would run again (and the seeders with `--seed`).
  - `migrate:resolve --dry-run` runs the same checks and names the ledger rows it
    would record.
  - `i18n:restore --dry-run` counts the translation rows it would write, the
    archived values it would claim and, with `--purge`, those it would delete.
  - `users:create-admin --dry-run` runs the checks without taking the setup
    claim and names the account it would create.
  - `setup-token --dry-run` names the replacement and prints no token.

- [#3438](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3438) [`6901487`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/69014872cf148c9d747c8584160b38fb64ae7ba7) Thanks [@aqib-rx](https://github.com/aqib-rx)! - Every command that writes the project folder now offers `--dry-run`, with one
  meaning everywhere: show what would change, change nothing.
  - `init`, `add`, `build`, `generate:types`, `generate:manifest`,
    `migrate:create` and `migrate:baseline` take `--dry-run`, and so do
    `telemetry enable`, `telemetry disable` and `telemetry reset`.
  - A dry run prints one "Would …" line per file it would write or remove, per
    command it would run (`add` prints the install command and installs
    nothing; `--skip-install` keeps its meaning) and per setting it would change,
    then "Dry run: nothing was changed."
  - Where the real run would refuse, the dry run says "A real run would refuse:
    …" and still exits 0. It takes no lock and asks no confirmation or consent;
    it still asks questions that decide what would be written, such as `init`'s
    answers and `migrate:create`'s renames.
  - `migrate:baseline --dry-run` writes nothing to the database: it names the
    migration file, its snapshot and the ledger row a real run would record.
  - `generate:types` and `generate:manifest` keep `--check`, which exits non-zero
    when the files are out of date; `--dry-run` lists the files and exits 0.
  - `migrate`, `migrate:down`, `webhooks:prune` and `generate:widget` keep their
    `--dry-run`; its help line now reads the same on every command.

- [#3338](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3338) [`3f32eeb`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/3f32eeba007ffbc15a2b95b38dcd1cb8f37b6b4a) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Duplicating an entry now copies a draft the caller may read. Before, a duplicate made through the REST route or with `overrideAccess: false` read only published rows, so a never-published draft answered 404 even for its author. The source is still read as the caller: a draft their read rule excludes answers 404, as a missing id does, and the copy is still checked as a create. A published entry's pending changes are not copied; its live content is.

- [#3750](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3750) [`fbb3028`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/fbb30286972489047c285235823b396ff69f71ae) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A change to what a role grants now expires the cached content pages until the expiry lands,
  rather than trying twice and logging an error. The expiry is queued as a job before it is tried
  and withdrawn once it lands, so if the process stops first, the next jobs run (`/api/jobs/run`)
  expires the pages. A process still running tries again, waiting longer each time, up to a
  minute between tries.

- [#3579](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3579) [`abfdfb2`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/abfdfb21fea98dd9de527c2a835694c4e5691d5d) Thanks [@faisal-rx](https://github.com/faisal-rx)! - Each person can store their own interface language, the language they want the admin in, through their own profile: `PATCH /admin/api/me` or `updateMe` take `interfaceLanguage` (a language tag such as `fr` or `pt-BR`, or `null` to follow the browser), and `GET /admin/api/me` returns it. It is kept in a new nullable `interface_language` column on `users`, which `nextly migrate` adds to an existing install without rewriting a row. An administrator's `PATCH /admin/api/users/:id` or `users.update` naming it is refused, naming the field.

  **Compatibility:** `interfaceLanguage` is now a reserved user field name. An app that defines a custom user field with exactly that name is refused at startup and must rename it.

- [#3545](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3545) [`ad21c2f`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/ad21c2f119303f62387c07c85af23c452051d271) Thanks [@faisal-rx](https://github.com/faisal-rx)! - A plugin schedule in the earlier `{ name, schedule, handler }` shape now runs, with a deprecation warning at start-up: `name` is the slug, `schedule` the cron, or an interval in milliseconds of whole minutes dividing an hour or whole hours dividing a day, and `handler` runs as a job of its own, given the plugin's context. One that cannot be mapped, such as a 7-minute interval, a cron that doesn't parse, or one with no handler, is not run, and the warning says why. Neither stops start-up. Declare `{ slug, cron, job }` instead.

- [#3578](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3578) [`f4d5a25`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/f4d5a25b31b0f00be103cbe779e30f8469dd5213) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The Design panel's Shared styles tab lists the site's block looks, grouped by
  block type above the shared styles. Each type's own look comes first, such as
  a button's Primary, with a Default chip that says what it covers. The looks its

  change, and the blocks the edit reaches are marked on the canvas. Selecting a

  The look tiles in the Style tab now draw on the type's base with the site's
  edits to its own look laid over, as the canvas does.

- [#3271](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3271) [`ead2dc1`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/ead2dc1aaa83c0d2bb6c7e93c2c978188518ae31) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - "Edit component" opens a placed component alone, in its own Page Builder view.

  palette and the context menu, to an author who may update components. It loads
  the component's view with a checked way back to the page, at the placement,
  and asks first about unsaved changes. A banner over the component's view names

  `ToolbarActionId` (exported by `@nextlyhq/builder`) gains `"edit-component"`.
  A `Record<ToolbarActionId, …>` or an exhaustive switch over it needs an entry
  for it; `blockActionRunners` already has one, and the new verb is optional on
  `CommandVerbs` and `BlockActions`, so a host that builds those keeps compiling.

- [#3249](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3249) [`0d8be01`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/0d8be01749ef1af708989101a1cd29db46bb2133) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A placed component's exposed fields can be edited on the page and in the panel. Double-click a component's exposed text on the canvas to type into it: the edit is stored on that placement only. Text the component does not expose selects the placement and says which component (and variant) it belongs to. In the panel, each field shows whether it is inherited, set here, from a variant or cleared, with a distinct icon for each; emptying a field clears it, and "Reset" returns it to the inherited value. A placement locked in Layers shows its fields read-only, and inside a `contentOnly` area the fields that are not content are read-only with the reason. A link the page could not draw is refused in the field with a message naming it.

  Saving a page, Single, component or pattern now refuses a placement value that does not fit its field ("Headline needs text") and an id the component does not expose, when the write sets it; a value the stored document already held is kept. The engine adds `placementValueIssues`, `exposedValueFits` and `neededFor`, and `resolveComponentInstances` takes `exposures: true` to record, for an editor, which exposure feeds each prop of a composed node (`exposedProps`); a render never carries it.

- [#3363](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3363) [`1a5d80b`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/1a5d80bd580ac09757b29bcbed75bddd46b551b4) Thanks [@faisal-rx](https://github.com/faisal-rx)! - Every collection entry and every Single now has a version. Every save changes it and no read does, and every read and write returns it as `_rev` (experimental). It is an opaque string. Two saves within the same second still differ. Each translation keeps its own counter, so saving one language does not change the version a reader of another language holds. A client that sends `_rev` back with a save has it ignored; before, such a save failed.

  Existing sites get the new columns from `nextly migrate`, on its usual run and on the boots that run it: a version counter and the last changer's ids, on every content and translation table. Existing documents start at version 1 with no recorded changer. No content and no `updated_at` is rewritten, and running it again changes nothing. A development boot of a project without a migrations directory adds them too. These columns never appear in a migration file, `migrate:check` or a drift report.

- [#2885](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/2885) [`5c354d6`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/5c354d6fbd0739a5eb0025324bca85b923be6afd) Thanks [@muzzamil-rx](https://github.com/muzzamil-rx)! - Every pooled MySQL connection now pins its session time zone to UTC (`SET SESSION time_zone = '+00:00'`) the moment it connects, so writes, timeseries windows and session-zone comparisons answer the same instants whatever zone the server itself runs in — and a replaced connection is pinned again by the same listener. mysql2's driver-level `timezone` is kept in agreement with the pin: a caller-configured zone that is not UTC is aligned to UTC (with a warning) rather than refused, so a driver parsing in one zone beside a session computing in another can no longer shift values a round-trip fails to cancel. Installations already on UTC servers notice nothing.

- [#3415](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3415) [`e4663d1`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/e4663d183e08d0b1b60411afde31c90840bff9b0) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Existing sites keep their spacing. A site's spacing is now a choice, **Space between blocks** under **Design → Variables**: **From each block's margins (classic)**, the spacing every page had before blocks took their spacing from their container, or **From the container's gap**. A site that already has block content (a page, a component, a Layout, or a document of any collection or Single holding a blocks field, in any of its languages; the seeded default Layout does not count, while a default Layout an earlier version set, which no seed record names, does) is put on Classic once, when it first starts on this version, so its pages render exactly as before: headings keep their 1.5em above and 0.5em below, paragraphs their 1em below, Divider and Quote their 1.5em, Sections and Cards stay unpadded, Columns, Gallery and Accordion keep the `space.4` gap, Buttons keep 0.5rem × 1rem, and no container writes a gap. A new site starts on the container's gap. A page rendered while that first decision is still running waits for it, so it is never drawn with container gaps first. A model stated in the host's configuration (`pageBuilder({ siteStyle: { spacingMode } })`) is the site's choice, and the step records nothing. The step runs once and never overrides a choice made under Design → Variables; to move an existing site to container gaps, choose **From the container's gap** there. Under Classic the spacing variables `space.stack`, `space.section-y`, `space.gutter`, `space.columns`, `space.card`, `space.paragraph`, `button.padding-y` and `button.padding-x` are not used.

  The choice is kept in a new table of the plugin's own, `page_builder__site_options`, which the plugin's migration creates: run `npx nextly migrate`. `loadSiteStyle` reads it through the plugin's service, from the reader it is handed or, when that reader is a wrapper of `find` and `findSingle` as the docs' route builds, from the instance the process booted, so a published route needs no change. Recording the model, at that first start or by a choice under Design → Variables, expires the cached pages tagged with the Site Style single, so the next render is drawn under it; a page stylesheet stored under the other model is recompiled. The instance `getNextly()` returns now carries `plugins`, the plugin services the `Nextly` class already offered. `SiteSheetInput` and the style compile context take an optional `spacingMode` (`"classic" | "gaps"`), the engine exports `SpacingMode`, `SPACING_MODES`, `DEFAULT_SPACING_MODE`, `isSpacingMode` and `spacingModeOf`, and a block's render arguments carry `spacingMode`.

- [#3484](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3484) [`6999793`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/6999793bf535822c8286bd73e015ff8a0324bbfd) Thanks [@faisal-rx](https://github.com/faisal-rx)! - The Page Builder, the Form Builder, the blog template's seed and the API Playground now say, with every update they make, which version of the document they change, or that they set it whatever is stored.   - **Page Builder:** component actions, the default Layout's settings, Layout removal and its repair, renaming from the Pages panel, shared styles, site fonts, the transfer import and the host rewrite send the version of the read they acted on. Putting back a stored copy, publishing what a page needs, making a Layout the default, and the Settings screen's breakpoints choose `_overwrite` (the breakpoints will send their version in a later change).
  - **Form Builder:** marking a submission read chooses `_overwrite`, and still only touches a submission that is new.
  - **Blog template seed:** patching a post's categories and tags sends the post's version; the Singles' demo copy chooses `_overwrite`, and a Single the seed cannot write now fails the seed with its reason instead of being skipped.
  - **API Playground:** the generated SDK code reads the document first and sends its version with the update; a bulk body with `revs` becomes one update per id, each with its own version.

  - **Draft warning under row rules:** it warns of draft changes on a Layout, or a region's component, whenever the author may see that row's working draft, which is the case when they may update or publish it, including under a row-filtered rule. An author who may do neither is still told nothing.

A new site's own default Layout is now called "Site layout" (address `site-layout`); a site set up earlier keeps "Default (site)", since stored titles are never renamed.

  Admin: the entries list no longer picks a field the form hides (`admin.hidden`) as one of its automatic columns, so the Pages list loses its "No header or footer" column. The field is still offered in the column picker, and a collection's own `admin.defaultColumns` may still name it.

- [#3386](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3386) [`0dba9bb`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/0dba9bbac9a834e94267fcae23c0c4caca191ac0) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Page Builder: Remove Layout reads past a page deleted while it runs. A page deleted after a removal listed it no longer stops the removal's scan of the pages using the Layout, or the clearing of the other pages left on it afterwards; a page is read past only once a second check confirms it is gone. A page that is still there but can't be read refuses the removal with "Not every page could be checked", and any other failure still stops it.

  The default Layout repair, at startup and in its background job, now finishes a restore of a deleted default that stopped after creating the restored Layout, pointing the default at it, before it would fall back to the seed Layout. The restored Layout is no longer left behind unused. If that Layout was deleted or unpublished in the meantime, up to the moment the default is written, the repair falls back to the seed as before.

  The check Remove Layout makes after its write, which clears pages a save in flight left on the Layout, is now tried again by the background job when a page it reached could not be read, keeping the removal open until then. A check that reaches its 2,000-page limit still finishes, with a warning in the log; a page past the limit still left on the Layout uses the site's default Layout.

  The lock's messages always name whoever holds the document: a person by their name, else their email; an API key as one ("Ana's API key", or "An API key" when its maker has no name); otherwise "Someone". They never read "null". When a person opens a document they are editing in another tab, the first tab says so and offers "Continue editing here", with its unsaved changes kept, instead of saying they took it over.

  While a document is held elsewhere, the reason shown beside its disabled actions reads "This document is being edited elsewhere", which is true whoever holds it, the same person in another tab included.

The companion `EXISTS` bound the operand raw, so on SQLite an integer epoch column compared with a text parameter and type ordering answered instead of time — a "later than" filter matched entries it should not, and a bulk update or bulk delete by that filter acted on the wrong documents, while PostgreSQL and MySQL each read the same operand alone. The localized builder now resolves the companion column and reads date operands through the same strict reader the main where builder uses; an operand no date can read is refused with the answer the main filter gives, where before each dialect decided by itself.

- [#3197](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3197) [`a81db00`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/a81db005338161d6545330337fc2476dfe9ec23c) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Media fixes for libraries upgraded from before image sizes were removed, and the bulk dialogs.
  - A folder deleted with its contents removes the size files of every item it deletes, an item moved
    into the folder as the delete began included.
  - Deleting an item removes a size recorded by its URL alone where the media storage configured now
    serves it there, and names any other in the log by its URL, rather than leaving it unnamed. Such a
    size stays while another item still names it.
  - `nextly media remove-sizes`, the check `nextly media orphans` makes before each batch, and a
    delete's check for files another item uses compare stored keys exactly on S3 and UploadThing,
    which keep them as written, so a file whose key differs from another's only in spelling
    (`media//x.webp`) is removed rather than kept with nothing naming it. Every other storage, a
    custom adapter included, still reads both spellings as one file.
  - A bulk delete or move dialog closes when the library's folder, view, search or type changes,
    rather than staying open over the cleared selection.

- [#3847](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3847) [`fc14b0e`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/fc14b0e5989b16adba90cbae3b8b7426ba0dc078) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - Paging through the media library lists each file once, even when files share an upload time or a size. Before, such files could show on two pages while another showed on none, so a transfer import could miss an identical image already in the library and add a second copy, most often on MySQL.

- [#3305](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3305) [`f31acfe`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/f31acfea62730865a5ec7f85cfc9511b7669c8bf) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Accessibility: a page builder block's context menu, toolbar menu and card menu no longer
  hide the rest of the editor from assistive technology while open. The shared tabs draw
  the open tab's label in the text colour and keep the brand colour as its underline, so a
  mid-tone brand colour no longer fails contrast on any admin screen's tabs. A page builder
