- [#3384](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3384) [`69c9d5c`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/69c9d5c8c0bf761332feaa2030bd68f2e3741095) Thanks [@aqib-rx](https://github.com/aqib-rx)! - `nextly migrate` no longer applies a migration file that deletes data without consent. Before it changes anything, it reads each pending file statement by statement and names what it would delete: a dropped table or column, rows a `DELETE`, `TRUNCATE` or MySQL `REPLACE INTO` removes, the tables an `ON DELETE CASCADE` reaches from the live foreign keys, a SQLite table rebuild that leaves a column or rows behind, and a column type change. On a terminal it lists every file with what it deletes and asks once; elsewhere it refuses, naming the consent that covers it: `--accept-data-loss` (every deletion) or `--accept-data-loss=posts,pages.summary` (only those), or `NEXTLY_ACCEPT_DATA_LOSS` with the same values. A statement it cannot read, or a cascade whose foreign keys it cannot read, needs the consent without targets.

  `migrate:down` names each deletion its down sections make in the same way, so a consent naming tables now covers them. `migrate:check` reports such a file as `DESTRUCTIVE`, naming what its UP or DOWN deletes, and still passes. `nextly migrate --dry-run` and `migrate:down --dry-run` list each deletion and the consent a real run needs.

  **Compatibility:** a pending file that deletes data, already committed in a project, now stops `nextly migrate` until consent is given. The boot migrate step reads only `NEXTLY_ACCEPT_DATA_LOSS`; without it the step logs the file and the consent it needs, applies nothing, and the site keeps serving. `NEXTLY_ALLOW_CORE_DESTRUCTIVE` still covers only Nextly's own tables, never an app file's deletion. A column type change is refused until the consent names the column.

  **Upgrading:** before deploying, run `nextly migrate:check` or `nextly migrate --dry-run` to see which pending files delete data, and set `NEXTLY_ACCEPT_DATA_LOSS` (or pass `--accept-data-loss`) naming what each may delete.

- [#3426](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3426) [`95d1507`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/95d1507cbe963126b0712d4cc3facca42bdb12ac) Thanks [@zeshan-rx](https://github.com/zeshan-rx)! - `nextly migrate` checks a field that stops being translated with Required or Unique before the move runs. When an entry has no default-language value, or two entries would share one, it refuses with the field and how many entries are in the way, and changes nothing. Before, the move stopped part-way, after its first two files had run. Migration files written this way need this version of Nextly or a newer one.

- [#3364](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3364) [`0764b63`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/0764b6345445a430d12fa9121a9d5778d9717120) Thanks [@aqib-rx](https://github.com/aqib-rx)! - No behaviour change: the migration statement readers share one cursor over the splitter's tokenizer, so every reader of a statement's shape reads it the same way.

- [#3478](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3478) [`9ae7218`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/9ae7218a2b68ee6fe529a03645ce668b94c056d8) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Remove Layout can move the pages that use a Layout to the site default, then
  delete or unpublish it. Until now a Layout any page used could not be removed

- [`b93944d`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/b93944d61ad68fd7a43abfa2d305d0250040773d) Thanks [@nextly-agent[bot]](https://github.com/nextly-agent%5Bbot%5D)! - Move a pattern, a component or a Layout between sites as one file. Each row of
  the Components, Patterns and Layouts lists offers "Export", and "Import from
  file" above each list brings a file in after a preview. API clients use
  `POST /transfer/<components|patterns|layouts>/:id/export` and
  `POST /transfer/import` (with `dryRun: true` for the preview).

  The file holds the item and everything it depends on: the components it places
  (and the ones those place), the shared styles and variables its styles use, the
  breakpoints its styles and per-device hide settings name, and the images it
  shows, with their bytes. It lists the block types it uses but never carries a
  block's code, and it never carries the site's default Layout mark.

  An import shows what it adds, what is already here and reused (an identical
  image, shared style or variable), and what clashes by name. Each clash is added
  under a new name by default, or can use the existing item instead; nothing on
  the site is ever overwritten. A breakpoint maps only to one of exactly the same
  width; one with no match is added (by someone who may manage site settings) or
  has its styles dropped. A file using a block the site lacks, making a component
  loop or breaking a lock is refused before anything is written, and an import
  whose site changed since its preview asks for a new one.

- [#3297](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3297) [`de14285`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/de142852930bd636e01863199838dbe0f2650b87) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - On MySQL, a batch update now judges each entry it publishes on the components and many-to-many relationships stored once it locks that entry, as on PostgreSQL and SQLite. The batch ran at MySQL's default REPEATABLE READ, so an entry later in the batch was read as it stood at the batch's first read: a change another writer committed in between was missed, and the batch could publish a document whose required relationship had been removed. The batch's transaction now reads committed data on every dialect. `updateEntriesInTransaction` runs in the caller's transaction: on MySQL, open it with `{ isolationLevel: "read committed" }` for the same behaviour.

- [#3213](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3213) [`689fd82`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/689fd82e0fb7aeb8c831a850239f129684465abf) Thanks [@aqib-rx](https://github.com/aqib-rx)! - On MySQL, a text, textarea or rich-text field with `index: true` and no `maxLength` is indexed by its first 191 characters on every road. A component (field group), a custom user field, a migration file that adds the index, and the development push adding an indexed field to an existing table each wrote a whole-column index on the TEXT column, which MySQL refuses ("BLOB/TEXT column used in key specification without a key length"), so the save or migration failed. Collections and new tables already used the prefix; every road now writes it from the same rule, which also covers the other TEXT and BLOB sizes. PostgreSQL and SQLite still index the whole value, and a unique index is unchanged.

- [#3314](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3314) [`5865504`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/5865504d81c58daa55d9e4647f01631edec07bb6) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A placed component is named by what the author placed. In the page builder's Layers panel, its bottom bar, its search and a page's list of sections on the entry screen, a placement read "Component instance", the engine's name for its node type. It now reads as the name the author gave the placement, else the component's title, else "Component". In Layers the placement's row also carries the component mark in the component colour and the word "component" after a title, so a title is not mistaken for a block's own name. The editor's other messages that name a block, such as a toolbar action's lock reason, now say "Component" for a placement too.

  `@nextlyhq/builder` adds `componentTitles(components)`, which builds a title lookup from a component library's rows, and the `ComponentTitleOf` type. `layerLabel`, `layersOf` and `pathTo` take that lookup as an optional last argument, and `LayersPanel`, `SelectionBreadcrumb` and `EditorCommandPalette` take it as `componentTitle`. Without it a placement reads "Component". `LayerNode` gains `component`, true for a placement.

- [#3625](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3625) [`2eb3a26`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/2eb3a26026444921a20646e94d59ae8b457bd426) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - The page builder's editor offers a Collection list's custom sources: the site's named queries are listed above its collections in the Source menu, each with its description and a Needs input tag, and choosing one draws an Inputs group with a control per input. A source whose input needs a value is written only once it can run, while the canvas tags the list with what it still shows. The canvas runs the query on the server with the editing person's own access, drafts included, as the canvas's other lists read; a failed run's note offers its log reference to copy.

- [#3607](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3607) [`0474f6c`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/0474f6c0c88904211c688e879d2cb9d829a216ea) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - A Collection list can take a named query as its source: a query a developer declares in code with `defineNamedQuery` (experimental), with typed inputs authors set on the list. It reads only what it declares, as an anonymous visitor, and the Direct API refuses every other read made while it runs. `set-list-query` takes `namedQuery`, and the composition manifest lists the site's queries.

- [#3759](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3759) [`ea2146c`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/ea2146cc3af02239db1e41e6506a192f3cd5a5c8) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - A component nested in another now expands on published pages when both carry visibility conditions, and a social image bound to a URL field reads its fallback as the address it is.

- [#3456](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3456) [`561d443`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/561d44310140deb791c7da8fd7d6d591061272b1) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - On PostgreSQL and MySQL, a transaction opened inside another transaction's work now joins it, as it already did on SQLite, instead of taking a second connection. Before, such a nested transaction could not see the outer one's uncommitted writes, committed on its own, and could wait forever on a row the outer had locked. This covers the adapter's `transaction()`, the Drizzle handle's `transaction`, and Drizzle's own `tx.transaction`. On PostgreSQL a joined call runs as a savepoint, so its failure undoes only its own part. On MySQL a joined call shares the outer's statements, so its failure fails the whole transaction, even when the outer catches it.

  What this changes for code that nests transactions on PostgreSQL and MySQL:
  - `afterCommit` now holds an effect until the outermost transaction commits, on every dialect, and drops it when that transaction rolls back.
  - `inTransaction()` can now answer true.

  New, and experimental:
  - `afterRollback(effect)` runs an effect once the outermost transaction has rolled back for good. A retried attempt's effects are dropped with it.
  - `TransactionOptions.retryWhen` lets a caller retry an outermost transaction for an error of its own choosing, application errors included.
  - SQLite now honours `retryCount` when `retryWhen` accepts the error.

- [#3464](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3464) [`75600fb`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/75600fbed6b85c4dc5d9fe996d59e79ac781eb4d) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The index-name check run before a collection's schema is applied now has one element type, so `nextly` type-checks again. No behaviour changes.

- [#3585](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3585) [`fdc120b`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/fdc120bea2453ff749e332440f44cdc1513acddb) Thanks [@aqib-rx](https://github.com/aqib-rx)! - An older build stops instead of calling the database up to date, and every command that changes migration history checks it first.

  **Compatibility: older builds stop, from this version on.** A build whose migrations folder lacks an app migration the database records applied now stops with exit code 3 (`MIGRATION_MISSING`), naming each missing migration, before it changes anything, core tables included. Before, it printed "Nothing to migrate. Database is up to date." Stop every build released before this check, preview deployments that share production's database included, before the first `nextly migrate` of this version. A migration the folder lacks that a newer build tried and did not finish stops the run the same way.

  **Compatibility: history is checked by every command that changes it.** `nextly migrate` and the boot migrate step, `migrate:down`, `migrate:baseline` and `nextly upgrade --reconcile-core` each check, before their first write, for an applied migration the folder lacks (exit 3), an unresolved attempt, and an applied file edited since it ran (exit 2). `migrate:resolve` and `migrate:fresh` are exempt. A plugin's modules are never counted as app migrations. `nextly upgrade --reconcile-core` now loads the config, as `nextly migrate` does, to find the migrations folder.

  `nextly migrate:resolve --removed <file>` records an applied migration's file removed on purpose: the migration stays applied, later runs go on, and if the file returns it is never run again and is checked against its recorded checksum. `migrate:down` refuses to roll it back while its file is absent, and `nextly migrate:status` lists it with a new status, `applied (file removed)` (in `--json` too), as information rather than the `applied (file missing)` problem. `nextly migrate:resolve --rolled-back <file> --file-missing` records a migration rolled back whose file is gone, an attempt a newer build left unfinished included; without the flag, `--rolled-back` still needs the file.

- [#3203](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3203) [`5b3efda`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/5b3efdae8b4fb9cda4acba5f233ea257e1d3c240) Thanks [@aqib-rx](https://github.com/aqib-rx)! - The Schema Builder's field picker is now one shared picker. It opens on its search box and shows a short "Most used" group, then the categories. Search matches a type's name, description, category and the words people use for it, so "relationship" finds Link to entries, "repeater" finds Repeating rows and "image" finds Image or file. It works by keyboard alone: arrows move, Enter picks, Escape closes. Picking a type asks only for a label, shows the name it derives, adds the field where the picker was opened (the end of the list, or inside the group or repeater it was opened from) and opens it for editing. "Add and add another" returns to the search for the next one. Picking Field group lists the existing field groups by name and address.

  `@nextlyhq/plugin-sdk/admin` adds `FieldPicker` with its `FieldPickerConfig`, `FieldPickerChoice`, `FieldGroupOption` and `FieldPickerProps` types, plus `describeFieldTypes` and `FieldTypeDescription`. All are `@experimental`. `nextly/field-catalog` adds `describeFieldTypes`, `FieldTypeDescription`, `MOST_USED_FIELD_TYPES` and `FIELD_TYPE_CATEGORY_ORDER`. The existing field-UI exports, `FieldTypePicker` among them, are unchanged.

- [#3224](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3224) [`b63dfe5`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/b63dfe53823b15beb4ae6de615c1219bff3576e9) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Page builder: one rule now decides where a block may go, in the editor and on every save. It adds the HTML content model to the existing `parent` and slot `allow` checks: nothing clickable inside a link or a button, no header or footer inside another, and a `main` only inside plain boxes. It also refuses a block in a slot its container does not declare, which the container would never draw. Box and Card gain a `link` that makes the whole block a link. Blocks can declare what they are as HTML through an optional, experimental `contentModel(props)`; a block that declares nothing keeps working as before. A page saved before the rule keeps its existing breaks as warnings and still saves other changes; a write that adds a break is refused, worded the same way in the editor and from the server.

- [#3304](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3304) [`01762de`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/01762de32ffffd848922c11cd2b4211afcc10efa) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The page builder's search finds more than commands. Press Ctrl+K (⌘K on a Mac), or the new search button in the top bar, to find blocks to add, which say where each will go and add it there; the page's blocks, which it selects and scrolls into view; the site's other pages, which it opens in the editor; and the commands. Results stay grouped by kind as you type, and the line at the bottom names what Enter does. `EditorCommandPalette` and `CommandPalette` take the new options for this (`insert`, `revealBlock`, `results`, `groups`, `onSearchChange`), and a command can carry an `icon`, a `detail` and a `verb`; all are additive and @experimental.

- [#3670](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3670) [`fe5844f`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/fe5844f695078f23b877dcf68e6b0db2c4c08f80) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The admin shows an entry's own design where an author meets it: a Design section first in every entry's side panel, and above the form on a phone (which design the entry is shown with, giving it its own design, editing or removing it, and the template to open or create where its collection has no published one), a Design column right after Status (or after the entry's name, where the list has no Status) on the entry list of a collection with a template or own designs (taken back from an open list once a later read finds neither), and, on a template, the entries with their own design in its side panel and a count in the builder's top bar. - [#3768](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3768) [`eb01975`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/eb0197561141efa9e1b3e70251f2cb72ff51ecea) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - A page action's dry run now reports a binding to a field that does not exist, and the action itself is refused with the same message, instead of the dry run passing and the save failing. Plugin authors can also declare the `disclosure` block support.

- [#3739](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3739) [`a88d43e`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/a88d43e89458a7874ef472d04a2d7d02301c5038) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Keep the page builder's checks after every write from waiting on a second
  database connection while the write holds one.

  On a pool of one connection, the usual serverless setting, a save inside a
  transaction waited five seconds for each extra connection it asked for, and
  other requests waited behind it. The breakpoint-removal and bindings-report
  checks that follow every write now run once the write's transaction has
  committed, as they were meant to, rather than inside it. A rolled-back write
  no longer runs them at all.

No behaviour changes.

- [#3663](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3663) [`8cf5167`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/8cf5167e8ca390db14280a7e8df967556a18ddc2) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The page builder's address claims read on the saving transaction's own connection instead of a second pooled one, so publishing a page no longer stalls on a database pool of one connection, the usual serverless setting, and a refusal names the page in the way from the same connection. A page's lock rows are read for update, so two saves contending for one address take turns.

- [#3696](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3696) [`1018fca`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/1018fcad1bfa247bb64cbbad6456ee1df275ac89) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - `nextly.media.findByIDs({ ids })` reads several media files in one query, judged exactly as `findByID` judges one (@experimental). A list's reads ahead are scheduled in page order, and the read-limit warning counts each cache scope apart. - [#3704](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3704) [`30a604c`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/30a604c237fe7fb09e3fc97814f07ef70ba1d8b8) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A list's reads ahead read no media for an image drawn from an address (a bound URL field, or an address fallback), stop after a link batch the route could not use, and let two lists drawing one image share the one batch read for it.

- [#3273](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3273) [`c924ccf`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/c924ccf2f063802b0ef94310c14fec8ebbfce83c) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A page route can now draw each page inside its Layout (experimental: the option may change before it is marked stable). Pass `layouts: pageBuilderLayouts()` (from `@nextlyhq/plugin-page-builder`) to `createBlocksPage` or `createPublicBlocksPage`, and every page is served as its Layout's header, the page, then its footer. A page gets the Layout it names while that is published, otherwise the site's default Layout, and no header or footer when "No header or footer" is on. The header and footer are drawn on the server and add no JavaScript, and a page's title and description still come from the page alone.

  Publishing a Layout, or a component a Layout uses, refreshes only the pages drawn inside it, and changing the default Layout refreshes only the pages that use the default. A site with no usable default serves its pages without a header or footer and logs a warning; those pages pick up the repaired default within a minute.

  The option is off unless you pass it, so existing routes serve exactly what they did before.

- [#3393](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3393) [`e57f61b`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/e57f61b1d9d0ab6197d94c58189a126656f53345) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The Page Builder's Pages panel lists each collection's pages together, its own Pages first and the others by name, and says over another collection that it uses the Page Builder. The pages search takes `order=collection` for this; a search by title is unchanged. Help inside the editor lists only the editor's own shortcuts: the admin's site navigation keys are left out, fitting the page is listed under Shift+1 alone, and the document's save reads Save. Each editor's panel keys register in a layer of their own, so Help lists the right ones with two editors on a page.

- [#3320](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3320) [`2dedc02`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/2dedc02089c8fe15dfea0b52f2c5a86676e9d6ea) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - `nextly plugins install` now records the columns, indexes, foreign keys and checks a plugin's

  used to record only the plugin's own tables, so until the next `nextly migrate` nothing said whose
  those elements were, and an install run again after one that stopped between a migration's record
  and its ownership left them unrecorded as well. The install now records them on every run, the

  the key's owner, as a REST write by the same key is. When a route writes through
  `ctx.services.collections` as the request's own user (`{ as: "user", user: ctx.user }`),
  the entry's content events, its history, the webhook outbox and the activity log name
  the API key itself. A session's write still names the person. A write a route makes
  as the system, or as another user, is recorded as before. A plugin still cannot name
  whom a write is attributed to, and how a key's write is judged is unchanged.

A schedule's first job is for the first window after it is first seen, and missed windows are not run later. A schedule that cannot run stops start-up, naming the plugin. - [#3251](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3251) [`665583e`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/665583e908febef9fb2bf8f72abfab408fe78d39) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - `nextly plugins uninstall` now refuses a full uninstall while another owner has built on
  the plugin's schema, instead of dropping it after consent. That covers a column, index,
  foreign key or check the app or another plugin added to the plugin's tables, a key or a
  relationship field pointing into them, and an index or key using or referencing a column
  the plugin added to someone else's table. Dropping these would delete data that belongs to someone else.
  Each is judged by the definition the database holds, so one whose declaration changed in code
  but was never migrated still counts while the database's definition uses the plugin's schema.
  The refusal names each one and its owner. Remove them in their owner's code and migrate,
  or uninstall with `--keep-data`, which drops nothing.

  A full uninstall now also deletes the plugin's settings (secrets included), its owner
  records and its migration history, so a later install applies every module again. It does
  so only once its DOWNs have removed everything it added to other owners' tables; if one is
  left, it keeps them and refuses, and the uninstall can be run again once it is dropped. The
  record that it was uninstalled stays, and the boot still refuses the plugin until it is
  removed from the config or installed again.

Each is checked when the app starts (its place, whether the place takes its kind, its fields, its namespace, and its order beside the others there) and sent only to a signed-in admin, already in order, leaving out for each reader what needs a permission they lack or names a field they may not read. A plugin may now declare an event `durable: true` in `contributes.events`; startup refuses a `durable` flag that is not `true` or `false`. - [#3559](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3559) [`d3bc66d`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/d3bc66d4c4cdd08e355ba4f9169928231976e11b) Thanks [@faisal-rx](https://github.com/faisal-rx)! - Plugins can add filters to the entry list's toolbar (experimental).
  - A plugin declares them in `contributes.admin.filters`. Each filter has options, and each option has a value, a label and a `where`.
  - Choosing an option adds its `where` to the list's request, which the server answers with the reader's access, so a filter only narrows the list. The choice is kept in the page's URL (`?pf=<filter>:<value>`), and one naming an undeclared filter or option is ignored.

- [#3611](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3611) [`9459451`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/9459451585761eb76dec1325b0dd7a2d1accc1e5) Thanks [@faisal-rx](https://github.com/faisal-rx)! - A plugin's declared row and bulk actions now run (experimental). A plugin route an action runs is reachable only as that action: before its handler runs, every request to it is refused unless it names the action and its rows, the caller holds the action's own permission, and the action's rule holds on every row as the caller reads it, so a bulk request with any row failing is refused whole. A row the caller may not read answers as a missing one. The entry list shows a collection's declared row actions in each row's menu, on the rows their rule holds for; one runs the plugin's route with the admin's CSRF token, or opens the plugin's component with the row. An action's `run` must now name a route that answers a write (`POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` or `DELETE`), whose path takes no parameters, and that is neither public nor a route for a plugin's own kind of signed-in person: a declaration naming any other refuses to start, and `run.method` no longer accepts `GET`. To keep such an action, declare a non-public write route at a literal path for it, and read the rows from the request body. Adds the `ACTION_NOT_AVAILABLE` (403) error code.

- [#3558](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3558) [`0b8c367`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/0b8c367e1f0345c80e4d2b55b3bd1dde29eb169f) Thanks [@faisal-rx](https://github.com/faisal-rx)! - A plugin can verify the webhooks it receives with `ctx.security.webhooks.verify(request, { scheme, secrets })`: in Standard Webhooks (`standardWebhooks`, the scheme Nextly signs its own webhooks with) or in a provider's own scheme the plugin describes. Core refuses a delivery signed more than 5 minutes away from now (`toleranceSeconds` changes it, finite only), compares every signature with every secret in constant time so a rotation verifies with both secrets, and refuses a body over 1 MiB (`maxBytes`). A scheme with no timestamp must say `timestamp: "none"`, and its verified result says `freshness: "unchecked"`. The answer is `{ verified: true, body, … }` or `{ verified: false, reason }`; nothing is verified by default. Experimental.

Options neither side can carry, such as a preview link or hooks, are named in a note instead of being dropped silently.

- [#3697](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3697) [`6c1f028`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/6c1f028d947e5ba3bcc6809845dcdd5fe5cdd6f7) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - `nextly db:sync --promote` prints every collection-level option a Schema Builder collection stores that changes how it behaves, not only its slug and fields. A collection with Draft/Published is printed with `status: true` (and `versions: false` where it keeps no history, since in code `status: true` alone turns history on), so once promoted its drafts stay unpublished and off its public pages. Its drafts and history settings, translations, `timestamps: false`, cache and webhook opt-outs, indexes, and a table name code would derive differently (`dbName`) are printed too, each spelled so that the code-first sync stores it back as the value the collection had.

- [#2560](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/2560) [`718a900`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/718a90027f23a14c93ebf174f63fd41f764589e4) Thanks [@faisal-rx](https://github.com/faisal-rx)! - Adding an email provider in the admin is now three steps: choose its type, connect it with only that type's settings, and send a real test. Where a provider can be asked without sending (an SMTP sign-in, a Resend key), its settings are checked before they are saved. A new provider is saved off and is never the default until its test is accepted or someone turns it on, and only a provider that is on can be made the default (an existing default is left as it is). A failed check or test is explained by what to check: the sign-in, the sender or its domain, the recipient, a rate limit, the connection, or something else. An accepted test is reported as accepted, not delivered, and a test through the Log provider as logged. **Send a test** works from every provider's row and page, and replaces the old disabled Test Connection button. The Sending tab shows the default sender, a provider set in code, and a warning when the Log provider is the default outside development; a provider's page shows its sending domain's status where the provider reports one (Resend does). A provider whose type is off can now be tested. A provider test email now goes to your own address: the address in the request is ignored, and an API key, which has no address of its own, is refused. New routes: `POST /api/email-providers/check` and `GET /api/email-providers/settings`; `GET /api/email-providers/[id]` adds `domainStatus`. The routes you mount yourself answer the same way: `nextly/api/email-providers-test` sends only to the signed-in person's own address (a body `email` it used to accept is ignored, and an API key is refused), and `nextly/api/email-providers-detail` returns `domainStatus` too. Provider definitions may declare `domainStatus`, and a `testConnection` result may carry `setup`; the `detail` a probe returns is now logged with the provider's declared credentials redacted, as a thrown failure already was. A test's result now names the address it went to, so the panel's outcome follows the server's own resolution rather than a cached profile. The catch-all create route validates its body as the mounted one does, so a boolean that is not one is refused instead of stored.

- [#3477](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3477) [`a6d6c40`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/a6d6c4096db826bde09edfcc5da8a4e8f75d6004) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A public blocks page can now be prerendered under Cache Components. Each public read a page makes (a list, an entry by id, a Single, and the field shapes its bindings are checked against) is cached whole, so the judgement of which fields the public may see runs inside the cached read. A public route also caches its `siteStyles` provider's read, tagged with the Singles the provider names and named by the route and the provider, so two routes' providers never share an entry; an access-enforced route still reads it per request. Under Cache Components a prerender refuses a read outside the cache that takes the current time, and that judgement does when it checks the access rules are current.

- [#3294](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3294) [`0b1bc3c`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/0b1bc3cc64c6ed367c8110c2646f68d3e05769dc) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The public reader (`createPublicReader`, `toPublicFind`, `@experimental`) refuses a sort key that is only a sign, such as `"-"`,
  and refuses `true` or `false` for `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte` and `contains`, before it builds a read; core refused
  both later, or dropped the sign-only key silently.

- [#3315](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3315) [`33b9a71`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/33b9a7198fe7f443dc98e920f1375b2e1be1af79) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The public reader (`createPublicReader`, `@experimental`) reads one Single as an anonymous visitor would:
  `findSingle({ slug, select?, locale? })` answers the published document with the fields the public may read, or `null`
  when there is nothing a visitor may see, and never creates the document. It takes the list read's fixed options and
  refuses anything else by name; `toPublicFindSingle` is the read it becomes. Beside it in `nextly/runtime`:

- [#3466](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3466) [`26403e4`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/26403e471ebf5046dbe7ad350158dbab45e19ad8) Thanks [@zeshan-rx](https://github.com/zeshan-rx)! - The admin's "Publish all" confirmation now lists every configured language with what publishing does to it, read from the server's preview: its pending changes go live, it stays as published, it goes live for the first time, or it goes live with no content of its own and shows another language. A language behind the published shared values, or a change the server would refuse, is named and the publish is not offered until it is resolved. The result message then reports each language's outcome. The document rail's "Publish all languages" button confirms through the same dialog instead of publishing at once.

- [#3431](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3431) [`b8e0e8b`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/b8e0e8b121ada1d7b4124568a576347bba406cd3) Thanks [@zeshan-rx](https://github.com/zeshan-rx)! - A publish of every language now runs the update hooks for an unlocalized collection's pending change it puts live: the registered and stored `afterUpdate` hooks and the fields' `afterChange` get the promoted document, as a publish of that change alone gives them. And previewing a Single's publish of every language names an invalid pending change's fields only to a caller who may read the Single, as the publish's own refusal does.

- [#3035](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3035) [`a4d5aec`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/a4d5aec25a30db373755e10e5b335f80c23e4b51) Thanks [@zeshan-rx](https://github.com/zeshan-rx)! - Publishing every language of a localized Single now records, for each language, the events a publish of that one language records. A language that was already live and whose pending change goes live gets a `single.updated` event tagged with its locale; before, it got none. A language going live for the first time gets a tagged `single.updated` as well as its tagged `single.published`; before, it got only `single.published`. For the default language, the untagged `single.updated` and the tagged one both describe the write.

  Each event's `previous` now holds the content readers saw before the publish. Before, it was built from translated values read after the pending changes were promoted, so it already held the new text.

  When a pending change edited a field every language shares, the version a publish of every language records, and each event's current state, now hold the shared value it put live. Before, both kept the value from before the publish.

  You can now ask what publishing every language of a Single would do before doing it: `GET /api/singles/{slug}/publish-all`, or `previewPublishAllLocales(slug)` on the Single service. It lists every configured language with its outcome: `goes-live-with-pending-change`, `stays-published`, `goes-live`, `shows-fallback` (naming the language it falls back to), or `out-of-date` (naming the shared fields you may read and counting the others). It also lists what would refuse the publish as a whole: edits two languages made that can't be combined or ordered, and a pending change the publish's own checks refuse, because it edits a field you may not write or would leave the document invalid. It's asked as the publish is: a caller who may not publish is refused. Publishing every language now returns the same `languages` list with its result.

  Publishing every language of a collection entry now puts each language's pending change live, as publishing every language of a Single already did. Before, it moved every language's status and left the pending changes pending. It judges the changes as a Single's publish of every language does: a change behind newer shared values is refused naming the fields, as are shared edits that can't be combined or ordered, and each change must pass its validation and the caller's field write rules. If any change is refused, nothing goes live. Each language's webhook subscribers get the events a publish of that language alone sends (a tagged `entry.updated`, plus the status events where it goes live). Its history records the move from draft, and the result lists each language's outcome. A collection publish of every language whose entry falls outside a write rule's filter is now refused with 403 before anything else is judged; before, an invalid pending change could answer 400 first.

  You can ask the same of a collection entry before publishing it: `GET /api/collections/{slug}/entries/{id}/publish-all`, or `previewPublishAllLocales({ collectionName, entryId })` on the collections handler. It answers with the same language outcomes and the same blockers as a Single's preview, judged by the same checks the publish runs, and refuses a caller who may not publish.

  Publishing every language whose translations table is missing, for a collection or a Single, is now refused with 409 and the repair to run, as a write of one language is. Before, a table dropped while the app ran answered 500, and once the app noticed, the publish put only the main row live.

- [#3508](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3508) [`5b814d5`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/5b814d5f2dd2721c43a72da13aab1f4ce67a456b) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Publishing now waits for the publish question to be about the draft being stored. An edit made while the question was being asked, such as choosing another Layout on the form, is asked about too, so a page no longer goes live with unpublished parts nobody was told about. A draft that keeps changing while it is checked is not published, and the author is asked to publish again once they've finished editing.

  A before-action handler can now give the store a check to make immediately before it writes, after every other handler and tracked write (`store.checkBeforeWrite`, experimental). A check that finds the work changed runs every handler again, so a question answered about the work is answered about the work as stored.

- [#3346](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3346) [`cb1f776`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/cb1f77676956f334a8b5ee7210a11d418f06d196) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Publishing a page whose components or Layout aren't published now asks first, in the editor and on the entry page: publish the page only, or publish the parts too, each as you, with any you can't publish named and left as they are. Making a Layout the site default asks the same about its header and footer components. Publishing a Layout from its own page now reports an unpublished header or footer component afterwards. A document action's before-action handler can cancel the action by throwing an `AbortError`. - [#3435](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3435) [`45ebb80`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/45ebb80041e429d0e28a2717598be49767d08f58) Thanks [@faisal-rx](https://github.com/faisal-rx)! - Publishing and unpublishing every language, batch and bulk updates, restoring a version, taking the live values into a pending change, and discarding a pending change are now judged by the version their caller read, as a save is. Each is refused with `STALE_VERSION` (409) when the document changed since, and changes nothing. `_overwrite: true` applies it anyway and records the overwrite in the document's history. A request that gives no version is applied as before. Experimental.
  - **Publishing or unpublishing every language** (`POST …/entries/{id}/publish-all` and `/unpublish-all`, `POST /singles/{slug}/publish-all`, and an update with `locale: "*"`) is judged on every language. Send `_rev` and `_overwrite` in the request body. The version must be one a read of every language returned (`7.en:2,es:3`). A one-language version is refused with 400, since it can't say whether another language changed. The answer gives every language's new version.
  - **A batch that gives each document its own version** (`updateMany`) reports each out-of-date document as a conflict and applies the rest. Each conflict's error carries its current version in `data`, and, where the caller may read the document, who changed it and when.
  - **A bulk update by ids** (`POST …/entries/bulk-update`, `bulkUpdateEntries`) takes a version for each id in `revs: { "<id>": "<_rev>" }`, and judges each document on its own. A `revs` that leaves out some of the ids is refused with the new `VERSION_REQUIRED` (428). A bulk update by query can't take `revs`. A bulk update that gives neither `revs` nor `_overwrite: true` is still applied for now.
  - **A restore** (`POST …/versions/{n}/restore`, for an entry or a Single) takes `_rev` and `_overwrite` in its body, and answers with the document's new `_rev`.
  - **Taking the live values** (`POST …/versions/working-draft/take-live`) takes `_rev` and `_overwrite` in its body.
  - **Discarding a pending change** (`DELETE …/versions/working-draft`) takes them in the query string (`?locale=es&_rev=7.es:3&_overwrite=true`). For plugins, `ctx.services.versions.deleteWorkingDraft(ref, locale, opts, version)` takes a new optional fourth argument, `{ _rev, _overwrite }`.
  - **A body that is not an object** sent to publish-all, unpublish-all, restore or take-live, which those routes used to ignore, is now refused with 400: it can't say which version the request was made from.
  - **A release's run** and **autosave** are never judged. A release moves each document as it stands when it runs. A recovery point changes no version.

Where the new type cannot keep one of them (for example a PostgreSQL view that reads the column, a MySQL index on a column becoming JSON, a default the new type cannot hold), the column is reported as blocked, naming what is in the way and what to change. A collation or character set a JSON column has no place for is named as not carried. The report also says what the conversion costs while it runs. The command still changes nothing.

- [#3664](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3664) [`3de18da`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/3de18daec5a404e941409c730bd7b14e5e2e8f64) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Every repeater row now has a saved `id`. Rows get one when they are written, at every nesting level. Ids you send are kept, and a repeated id is given a fresh one. A row sent without an id keeps its stored id only when it is unchanged at the same position; otherwise it gets a new one. The admin gives a row an id when you add it, and restoring a version keeps repeater row ids.

  API answers now include `id` on repeater rows after a save. Existing rows get their ids on the next save that sends their repeater; an update that leaves the repeater out doesn't touch it, and there is no backfill. That first save shows those rows as changed in version history and in webhook `changedFields`.

  Password fields inside repeater rows: when a write leaves a row's password out, the stored one is kept. Rows are matched by the ids the writer sends, and a writer that sends no ids is matched by position, as before. Matching no longer counts the ids rows now carry in storage. So a writer that never sends ids keeps its rows' passwords, a reorder by id keeps each password on its own row, a removed row's password is dropped, and a copied row gets none.

  Compatibility: a write that sends a repeater row without its `id`, leaves that row's password out, and changes the row's other values is now refused with `ROW_ID_REQUIRED`. This applies only when the saved row has an `id` and a password. By position alone, a reorder could hand one row's password to another. Send each row's `id` from your last read, or send the password again. A repeater whose rows declare their own `id` field keeps that value as written, and its rows get no saved id. Adding such a field to a repeater that already has saved rows makes their saved row ids that field's values until changed; Nextly warns about it in development.

- [#3370](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3370) [`59e6973`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/59e6973a9adafd1301b60747d20ea46b45c3890c) Thanks [@aqib-rx](https://github.com/aqib-rx)! - Making a column required is now refused, before anything runs, when rows of its table would hold no value in it, on every road that can do it: a Schema Builder save or apply for a collection, a Single or a field group, the development push (`next dev`, `nextly db:sync`), and `nextly migrate` applying a migration file. The refusal names the collection, Single, field group or table, the field or column, and how many rows are in the way; for a field group, each collection and Single whose rows those are.
  - A save or a migration that fills those rows first is not refused: a value chosen in the Schema Builder or at the push's prompt, or (in a migration file) an earlier statement that writes to the table, after which the rows still empty are counted at the statement that makes the column required. On MySQL, a migration refused there names the statements that ran before it, and its attempt is recorded as failed, never as applied.
  - A required field added in the Schema Builder or the push with a value for the existing rows is now added, filled, then made required; before, the fill ran before the column existed and the save failed.
  - Every table is checked by `nextly migrate`, including one that is not a collection, Single or field group (a plugin's), which the refusal names by its table and column.
  - A count that fails refuses the change before anything runs, naming the table, rather than leaving it to the database.
  - The CLI ends these refusals with two new codes, `REQUIRED_COLUMN_HAS_NULLS` and `REQUIRED_COLUMN_UNCOUNTED`, each with its own docs page.

There, a text `slug` beside a column-less `slug`, or a text `title` beside a column-less `Title`, is refused like any other pair of sibling fields. - [#3467](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3467) [`56b7cd0`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/56b7cd0be32a439454c0309187297cf9d94bd888) Thanks [@zeshan-rx](https://github.com/zeshan-rx)! - Scheduling a document from its editor is one "Schedule…" dialog, on the arrow beside whatever action leads (Publish, or Save on a published document with nothing to publish), under "Publish now". It puts the document:
  - **on its own, at a time** — a release of one, named after the document's saved title, scheduled at once;
  - **with an existing release** — only an ordinary release in draft or scheduled that you may add to, shown with when it acts and how many documents it holds; single-document, stopped, published, cancelled and overdue releases are not offered;

A refusal for the document's hard problems is said in the dialog, one line per problem, and the dialog stays open. A translated document says that every language moves together, and on a collection entry, unsaved edits are noted as not included.

  "Schedule publish…" and "Add to release…" are replaced by "Schedule…".

  The banner above a scheduled document lists each release holding it on your clock (with the zone it was scheduled in), with Remove where you may change that release's documents (taking it out of its single-document release cancels that release), Change time on a single-document release you may reschedule, and, where two releases act at one moment, which one readers end up with.

- [#3780](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3780) [`8b24a23`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/8b24a23dc3b9afda25cb49a8f21d30e11bedc5a2) Thanks [@mobeenabdullah](https://github.com/mobeenabdullah)! - A development schema apply on PostgreSQL failed on a database whose owner registry
  did not exist yet, with "current transaction is aborted": the apply read the registry
  inside its own transaction, and the failed read aborted it. The apply now asks the
  catalog whether the registry is there before reading it.

  Renaming a field to a required one, on a table with rows, was refused as if the field
  were added without a default, though the rename carries every row's value. A required
  field a confirmed rename fills is now judged by the rows of the column it is renamed
  from, and refused only when some of them hold no value.

  `nextly migrate` failed with "duplicate column name" on a translated field added to a
  translated collection when its translations column was already there, as a dev push,
  the Schema Builder or a change that stopped part-way leaves it. The migration file now
  adds only a missing column, and a column already there is judged, as before, by whether
  it can hold the field.

  When two server processes added fonts to a site at once, the page builder sometimes
  stored one add's files at the media root rather than in the site's Fonts folder: the
  media library refused that add's folder because the other process had just made one.
  The add now takes that folder instead.

Plugin-migrated tables are still never dropped by a dev push.

- [#3428](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3428) [`03fa183`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/03fa1838cc11891ed1a630bc2c742ee548c2dc13) Thanks [@aqib-rx](https://github.com/aqib-rx)! - Every CLI command that changes the schema now holds the one schema lock, and the development start's schema sync waits for it. `migrate:fresh` keeps the lock tables through its drop, and a failed re-apply releases the lock before the command exits. `permissions:cleanup` reads and deletes under the lock. `prune` and `db:sync --promote`/`--demote` ask first and take the lock only for the change, reading again under it. If what you agreed to changed in between, nothing is changed and the command stops with `PLAN_CHANGED_AFTER_CONSENT` (exit 1). `migrate:status`, `migrate:check`, `migrate:create` and the field-groups preview still take no lock.

A Section's Size section offers Height: Auto or Full screen (`min-height: 100svh`). A Button's Size section offers Small, Medium and Large, which scale the button's own padding tokens and its text size, and Full width. A design token reference may carry `times`, a factor from 0.25 to 4 for a length or a number, written as `calc()` over the token under the site's prefix. A Button's label is centred in it, as a `<button>`'s is, whether it renders as a link or not, so a full-width or wider button reads the same either way.

- [#3288](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3288) [`6292e92`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/6292e9221497d512552d006a7ee2fcade4607cec) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Selecting a block in the page builder no longer changes how the page draws that block: the selection ring stays an outline, and its white halo is measured and drawn by the editor in its own layer, for every selected block and every copy a block repeats, rather than set on the block as a shadow or an anchor. The halo follows the block's rounded corners, stays above page content however high a site stacks it, and is left off a block it cannot trace (sticky or fixed, rotated, or cut off by a container), where the ring shows alone. A shadow or anchor the page gives the block survives selection. The canvas also no longer treats a translucent dark background colour as a dark page, whatever number syntax its alpha is written in.

- [#3613](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3613) [`329ee3c`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/329ee3cccb6b6fa40a94b4387005657fe05a1376) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Settings can now undo the newest breakpoint removal. The Site tab offers it on the removal's row, saying until when it can be undone, every time Settings opens for 30 days. Undo asks first ("Put Mobile back?"), then puts the breakpoint and its styles back, following the undo to its end as a removal is followed. When it is done it says the breakpoint is back, or lists each page it could not put every value back into and why (set again after the removal, on a block deleted after it, on a page deleted after it), linking the pages that still exist. A refused undo says why in the server's words. A removal's confirmation now says it can be undone from Settings for 30 days. The Site tab's 10-second watch for another tab's removal reads the removals alone (`GET /site/breakpoints/removal`, which now answers them, and the removal that can be undone, when no run is named) instead of all of Settings. An unreadable status at the end of a removal is read again rather than calling the removal route again.

Saving a set without one checks what is stored under it; where something is, Settings shows what would go (per place, the pages named, locked blocks, drafts and anything it could not read or reach) and removes it only on Remove, saying "This can't be undone." A removal that does not finish in its save is followed until it does, a removal still going when Settings opens holds editing the breakpoints until it ends, and one that had to leave documents (a live page under a pending draft) says so. - [#3289](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3289) [`edfd879`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/edfd8798d418cb7db8a8c566dc55d792c37c04df) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The page builder's **Settings** is now a dialog with two tabs. **This page** holds the entry's own fields and a preview of how a shared link looks, built as the published page's metadata is. **Site** holds the site's breakpoints and its default Layout, and applies to the live site at once. It is offered only to a role that may manage the page builder's site settings.   The site's breakpoints now change through one route, guarded by the `manage-page-builder-site` permission, and a write to the `site-style` Single that changes them any other way is refused with a 403. This includes the REST API and the Single's own form, even for a role holding both permissions. A role with the site permission alone can change breakpoints; a role with Design's alone cannot. Writes that change only tokens, fonts or classes are unaffected.

  `@nextlyhq/plugin-sdk/admin` adds `writePluginRoute` (experimental): a one-shot write to a plugin's own route that rejects with the parsed error.

- [#3330](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3330) [`0f98adf`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/0f98adf766c02a50eaf5934ba25a83e1b5ce89f8) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The page builder can now lock a shared style: a role holding the new "Lock shared styles" permission locks and unlocks it, and while it is locked nobody can change, rename or remove it. Unused shared styles are removed through a route that refuses a style still in use, and refuses every removal while some pages are still being counted; the same routes report how widely each style is used and where. - [#3465](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3465) [`3da634c`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/3da634c3c62dc5bfcfbb633246e03d66f3dd7ab0) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Shared styles now keep what the page shows in a few cases where they drifted:

- [#3557](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3557) [`a6fb447`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/a6fb447a2741eeed528a609bf024e276ea2319be) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A Section's and a Button's shortcuts now read back the value they write over one from elsewhere: Auto shows chosen after writing `auto` over a wider Full screen, and Medium after writing the button's own padding over a wider size. A size reaching from elsewhere is matched to the button's own tokens exactly, under the site's token prefix, so a token whose name merely ends the same way no longer reads as Small or Large. The overlay is offered by the image that wins where it is edited, so an image cleared with `none` there no longer offers one. - [#3206](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3206) [`e622611`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/e622611cabe5122d9c361b4a23e3e8ecd2edb509) Thanks [@aqib-rx](https://github.com/aqib-rx)! - One rule now judges sibling fields wherever a definition is written: `nextly.config.ts` at start, on a config reload and in `nextly db:sync`, the Visual Schema Builder, the REST schema endpoints, the collection and field-group services, `nextly migrate:check` and `nextly migrate:create`. Two fields directly inside one container (the top level, one group, one repeater, or a field group's own top level) may not have the same name, names that differ only in letter case, or names that become one column (`fooBar` and `foo_bar`, `Title` and `title`). Before, the Builder compared only top-level names spelled alike, configuration compared each level ignoring case, and neither compared columns at every level.
  - A change that would create such a pair is refused before anything is written, naming the entity, the container and both fields. Fields of one name in different containers are accepted.
  - An entity that already holds such a pair keeps being served, saved and migrated as it is, and `nextly migrate:check` warns once for each pair, naming the column or key the two share and saying to rename one.

- [#3654](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3654) [`17fb332`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/17fb332584b189a8f81d0a9bad58e49f9f019faa) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Site code can now be edited in the page builder's Settings, under Site → Code (experimental). The section says what each place holds in plain words and who changed it last. Saving checks the code first: what can't be stored is named under its place and nothing is saved; what the site's Content Security Policy would block is listed with what to add to the policy, ready to copy, and is saved only once you confirm; with no policy known, the section says so before saving.

  The site code read now also answers `described`, `changedAt` and `changedBy`, and each policy check answers `additions`, from the new `siteCodePolicyAdditions`. Under `'strict-dynamic'`, scripts the loader builds are trusted once the loader is allowed. The head's code finishes loading before the end of the body's starts.

- [#3624](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3624) [`2a55975`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/2a55975917c886c180275f2c99c5a1a6c36f73b7) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The page builder can now judge site code before it is stored: `sanitiseSiteCode` turns pasted HTML into entries a published page can carry in its head or at the end of its body (scripts, styles, meta tags, links and a no-script pixel), refusing with a reason anything that hides code in markup, loads from anywhere but `https:` or the site itself, or would break out of its place. `checkSiteCodeAgainstCsp` says which entries the site's Content Security Policy would block, and `mergeSiteCodeIntoCsp` adds what the code needs to a policy without widening anything else it allows. These are experimental until site code renders.

- [#3702](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3702) [`4fa74de`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/4fa74de085f9f3d96d091d5cbe58ff5177e5ed3a) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - `<SiteCode>` no longer fails a production build now and then under Cache Components. It read the site code through `unstable_cache` whenever the app's `"use cache"` read function was not yet registered, and on a route that imports nothing that registers it, `/_not-found` among them, that read could still be running when the prerender stopped. It now stops with an error that names the fix instead: add `src/nextly/cached-read.ts` and import it from the layout that renders `<SiteCode>` (`import "@/nextly/cached-read";`). With Cache Components off, or with a `read` of your own, nothing changes.

  New apps need nothing: the base, blank and blog templates and the plugin template's dev app now ship `src/nextly/cached-read.ts` and import it from their root layout. That one import registers the cached read, and registers how Nextly starts (`registerNextlyStart(() => getNextly({ config }))`) for a read that finds it not started, so a page only the root layout renders, such as `/_not-found` during `next build`, starts Nextly rather than failing with "getCachedNextly() called before initialization". Nothing starts eagerly, so an app page that calls `getNextly` with options of its own first still starts it with them. An app made by an earlier release that renders `<SiteCode>` under Cache Components adds both, as the [site code page](https://nextlyhq.com/docs/page-builder/site-code#with-cache-components) shows.

  `nextly` adds `registerNextlyStart(start)`, which `getCachedNextly()` runs only when nothing has started Nextly, nothing is starting it and no failed start is left to retry.

  `nextly/runtime` adds `cachedReadRegistered()`, which says whether the app has registered its `"use cache"` read function in this process.

  `getCachedNextly()` now starts Nextly again after a start that failed, with the complete options that start was given (its config and any adapter, logger, image processor or service overrides beside it), so a worker whose first start met a database that was down recovers once the database is back instead of refusing every read until it restarts.

- [#3642](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3642) [`c0b062c`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/c0b062c5fe65fd4dc5077343fbc3ef6ddcf16dab) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Site code's URL check now takes out the characters browsers ignore in a URL by code point instead of a pattern, with the same characters as before, so the page builder's site code modules lint clean. Nothing a user can see changes.

- [#3644](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3644) [`5466120`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/546612009a94cb815022b5dd6647bf468053bea6) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - Sites can now add code to every published page. People who may change the site's settings save it through the page builder's site code route, which judges it on the server and refuses API keys. The route checks the code against the site's declared Content Security Policy, and asks for an acknowledgement before saving code the policy would block. Each save writes an audit row of hashes and counts, never the code. `<SiteCode>` from `@nextlyhq/plugin-page-builder/site` renders it from the site's layout. In draft mode it renders nothing. Scripts and styles run only through a fixed loader that refuses the admin, the editor's canvas and any page the site frames, so the code never runs inside the admin even when the layout is shared with it. Experimental until site code can be edited in Settings.

- [#3752](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3752) [`dd27f80`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/dd27f804b983f8e15764e9411a985d8500f46dcd) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - On the page builder canvas, the tabs on blocks no longer cover each other. A block drawn shorter than its "Conditional", Entry content or "Visitors won't see this" tab, under another marked block, now carries its tab on its bottom edge, so each block's tab stays readable and on its own outline. A selected block's "Visitors won't see this" tab no longer sits under the block toolbar.

- [#3037](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3037) [`b4f06ab`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/b4f06abe6848285738aac360f84f67014821449f) Thanks [@muzzamil-rx](https://github.com/muzzamil-rx)! - Storage plugins no longer stop the config from loading when their credentials are absent. `vercelBlobStorage()` and `s3Storage()` validated the token, bucket and region inside the factory call, which runs while `nextly.config.ts` is evaluated — so every command refused to start without them, including `generate:types` and the other schema-only commands that never touch storage. The check now happens at the first storage operation (such as the first upload, read, delete, or `nextly media` command) and refuses with the same messages as before. A deployment missing `BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN` or S3 variables now starts cleanly, and misconfiguration surfaces at the first editor upload rather than at server boot. A site running schema-only commands can unset placeholder credentials, and a deployment with real credentials sees no change. `enabled: false` and uploadthing's warn-and-degrade behave exactly as they did.

- [#3512](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3512) [`b4fdcbc`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/b4fdcbcd13dd95d24be2307d0b1750a9a287d8a7) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A conditional write that adopts a Single another writer created during it now reads that row under its lock, so on MySQL the value its expectation is judged against is the one committed when the lock is taken, not an older snapshot. Two first conditional writes of a Single that is not stored yet now run one after the other: one lands and the other is refused with a conflict, where on MySQL one used to fail with a deadlock and on PostgreSQL both inserted a row.

- [#3395](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3395) [`e86d8ed`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/e86d8ed5efee3a6534636326652e8e5f92b41796) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - In the page builder's Style tab, font size, line height, spacing, radius, shadow and every other field that can take a site variable now offers the site's variables beside it, with a sample of each, and typing a variable's name such as "Display" picks it, so a block follows the variable when its value changes in Design.

- [#3392](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3392) [`2689ab8`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/2689ab877604a0080ea421434971c98cec6d6e3c) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - In the page builder's Style tab, a number typed and then given a unit from its menu is written once, so one Undo restores the value from before. A unit can be typed letter by letter ("2ch") without being cut while it is typed.

- [#3709](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3709) [`b0f6e90`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/b0f6e90e24c81412440593dd89a8d585f93cd9b8) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A new Table of contents block lists the headings of a passage of rich text, each linking to its heading. On a collection template, bind its Content to the same field as the article body so every entry gets its own contents.

  Every heading the Rich text block draws now carries an id made from its words (`Getting started` becomes `getting-started`, a repeat `notes-2`), so a link can reach it. - [#3676](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3676) [`3f2cd91`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/3f2cd91bd3ccf5d2868c57c00ef6eb4ce0a7256f) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - An entry's save reads its collection's template on the save's own transaction, so a save in a collection served at an address set in the admin never waits for a second connection from the database pool, and only an entry with a slug takes its collection's lock. A collection's eligibility for a template address is judged from one read of its record, and `set-template-address` no longer reports a committed change as failed when the count of waiting entries cannot be read.

- [#3658](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3658) [`b4a66bb`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/b4a66bbb8361e775697b2a6b142d8e011c1a53b6) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - A collection created at runtime, in the Schema Builder, can now be served under a template address set in the admin, with no restart: its template stores the address (a new `address` field on the page builder's templates), and its published entries are served at `<address>/<slug>` once the template is published. Setting or changing an address needs a new permission of its own, `manage-template-routing` ("Manage template routing"), apart from updating templates: the field takes the address out of a save by anyone without it, through the admin, REST or the Direct API, and the template form shows it read-only to them. A stored address is judged as a code-declared one is (its one spelling, outside the paths the runtime keeps, not `/`), and is refused, naming the other collection, when another collection is given it in code or stores it; an address declared in code wins over a stored one, and a code-declared address that another collection stores refuses to start. Changing a published template's address moves every entry: the old addresses are freed and the new ones claimed, an entry whose new address another document holds waiting until it is given up. The template actions gain `set-template-address` (experimental), with a dry run, which asks for the routing permission first and answers how many entries wait. Templates now appear in the page builder's menu, listing each template's collection and address. `nextly db:sync --promote` prints the `pageBuilder({ templates: { addresses } })` line for a promoted collection whose template stores an address.

A Posts template binding a post's body, excerpt, image or author is no longer refused.

Blocks that render asynchronously, such as images and buttons, never drew in the editor, which renders the page in the browser: React refuses an async component there. `@nextlyhq/blocks-react` now reads an async block's output with `use()`, which works on the server and in the browser alike. When the editor draws the page again for a selection or an opened panel, a block's output is reused while the block, its class and its stored props are unchanged, so images and buttons no longer blink out. An image chosen from the media library now resolves on the canvas too, through the admin's own read of a media item, cached by id. `@nextlyhq/admin` adds `useMediaResolver`, built on the same query as `useMediaItem`, and `@nextlyhq/plugin-sdk/admin` exports both, `@experimental`.

- [#3336](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3336) [`154dd04`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/154dd0450da51aeed43790dbb47bf76fdcfa5c78) Thanks [@nextly-agent](https://github.com/apps/nextly-agent)! - The page builder's canvas can draw the page inside your site's own layout, so your app's global stylesheet, fonts, header and footer are around it, as they are around the published page.

  Add a route, inside the layouts your pages are published in, whose page is the new `PageBuilderCanvas` from `@nextlyhq/plugin-page-builder/canvas`, and name its path as the new `canvasPath` option, for example `pageBuilder({ canvasPath: "/page-builder-canvas" })`. The editor loads that page into the canvas and draws the page being edited in it. Your layout stays visible around the page, faded and inert, so its links and forms do nothing in the editor; pointing at it shows that it is part of your site's layout.

  `canvasPath` must be a path on the admin's own site; a full or protocol-relative URL is refused when the plugin is configured. A site whose pages sit under their language writes `{locale}` where the code goes, for example `"/{locale}/page-builder-canvas"`, and the editor loads the route for the language being edited, leaving the segment out for the default language. Without it, the canvas draws on its own blank page as before. When the route is set but not found or does not load, the canvas does the same, and a note above it says so, with a link to the docs.

  On the blank page, the canvas's stand-in base styles (no body margin, a light ground, and the site's ink and body font on the canvas) still apply. On your site's page, your own stylesheet decides them instead. The canvas also states the direction of the language being edited, as `dir` beside `lang`.

  `CanvasFrame` from `@nextlyhq/builder/shell` takes a `source` that is either the editor's blank page or a page the site serves, and reports through `onSourceFallback` when that page cannot be shown. Both are experimental. **Compatibility:** the experimental `CanvasFrameSource` type is now the union of `BlankFrameSource` (its previous shape: `srcDoc`, `ready`, `mountPoint`) and the new `SiteFrameSource` (`src`, `served`, `ready`, `mountPoint`, `watch`). Code that read `srcDoc` from a `CanvasFrameSource` narrows first with `"srcDoc" in source`, or types its value as `BlankFrameSource`.

The editor's marks on the page are clearer too: a selected block has a blue ring with a white halo that reads on light, dark and coloured sections, the drop line uses the same blue, a selected component placement is purple, and the block toolbar is a dark bar with light text in both admin themes.

Escape while typing on the canvas keeps what was typed and ends the edit; a second Escape selects the block's parent. Where the write can't be made, the text stays open with the words in it and the editor says why: the page refused it (a size cap), the block was locked while it was typed, or someone else changed the same text meanwhile, which is never written over. A second Escape over the same words lets them go; words revised since are tried again, and a held Escape key does not count as a second press. `InlineEditRefusal` gains `"no-longer-editable"`, for a value locked or no longer storable while its element is still on the page; it used to come back as `discarded`, which is now kept for an element that has left the page. A host branching on the reason should handle the new value. `useInlineText` takes an optional `onFinished`, told when a key's way out of a line was refused.

The canvas reads the media item as the person editing, under the same `read-media` check as the admin's media library. A person who may not read the library sees the binding's fallback.

An empty page shows a "Start your page" card with an Add section button, and takes a dragged block anywhere on it. A "+" in the gap between two top-level sections, shown when the pointer is near the gap or on keyboard focus, adds a section there. An empty box says "Drop a block here, or click to add one". - [#3200](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/pull/3200) [`e3df75f`](https://github.com/nextlyhq/nextly/commit/e3df75f7d76b2538f34152f43441856c360d8cf2) Thanks [@aqib-rx](https://github.com/aqib-rx)! - The CLI now reads the same environment files as the Next.js app in the folder
  it runs in, through Next.js's own loader: `.env`, `.env.local`, `.env.<mode>`
  and `.env.<mode>.local`, in Next.js's order, with a variable already set in the
  process environment winning over every file. It used to read `.env` alone.

  The mode is the new global `--mode development|production|test`, else
  `NODE_ENV` (`production` or `test`), else development, unset included. The run
  sets `NODE_ENV` to it before loading the configuration, so a configuration that
  branches on `NODE_ENV` declares the same schema under
  `nextly migrate --mode production` as `next build` evaluates. A command that
  reaches the database prints the mode and the file its `DATABASE_URL` came from
  on standard error, once (none under `--quiet`).

  A project's `build` script runs `nextly migrate` before `next build` with no
  mode, so with `NODE_ENV` unset that step runs in development mode. Add
  `--mode production` to its `nextly migrate` and `nextly plugins install` steps
  so they read the production files and evaluate the configuration as
  `next build` does. In production mode the environment check asks for
  `NEXTLY_SECRET` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`, as the app itself does at build
  time.

Nothing changes at runtime.

"Save as component" and "Convert to component" are one "Turn into component…" item, whose dialog offers to keep the original blocks and names values by the block's own property labels.

  exports the admin's `MediaPickerDialog` (experimental). A block prop may name itself

Before, the main column was added empty and the translations were left in a column nothing reads.
